desktop.bodyText: Cloud Console Hardening — wave 29: “I could not look” gets a grammar, and the merge lane stops being someone else’s host Status: SURVEYING. Strategize is closed; 16 Opus surveyors are in flight. Digest appends the survey digest and the verify plan below before any verifier runs; Decide appends the decisions and the wave plan before any builder flies; Review closes this Paper as the debrief. Epic cloud-console-hardening-epic · predecessor wave Paper cloud-console-hardening-wave-28-2026-08-03 · charter .claude/workflows/bp-cloud-console-hardening-charter.md (read from origin/main, not the primary checkout, which is 401 commits behind). The wish Seven numbered instructions. Condensed, with the load-bearing corrections preserved: Finish the discrimination. cch-w28-s2-history-unavailable-discrimination is round 2 and #9356 has landed, so it is unblocked. Teach the git legs to tell rc 1 ("not an ancestor" — an honest answer about the PRODUCT) from rc 128 / missing object / shallow ("I could not look" — an honest answer about the ENVIRONMENT). Its hard constraint is already armed as a tripwire by s1: HISTORY-UNAVAILABLE must surface as a verdict-token LETTER at exit 1, never a process-level exit-2 INFRA-FAULT. The merge lane changed and every earlier brief is stale on this point. Live protection enforces FOUR contexts as of today. Console gate and Cloud gate are BLOCKING, not advisory. Required-check spec drift is GREEN on main for the first time this session. A required gate a third-party host can red is the same defect class as a guard no job runs. Wave 28 s3 documented that the now-REQUIRED Console gate depends on guerrilla.barkpark.cloud being reachable, and nobody fixed it. Tolerable while advisory; an outage on someone else’s host is now a repo-wide merge freeze. The D307 guard’s promotion. The guard is armed at the birth seat (#9405, a723ec0dd); the surface ENUM and the BACKFILL of open rows are what turn the WARN tier hard. The contested scoping criterion was re-measured by the lead: deleting only the scoping leg gives 46 tests / 1 failure, not the 23 the criterion predicted — so the scoping is a DESIGN BOUNDARY, not a load-bearing guard. Do not restate it as load-bearing. The s7 residue, person-facing. A re-check affordance for a TERMINAL unknown domain rail (the poll stops with no way back short of a navigation), plus domainRungChip’s missing unknown arm (task-1daff7bc1bf46ceb). cch-w22-s7’s remainder — finished or closed against origin/main’s bytes rather than rebuilt. .preview-url IS NOT A SLICE and the wish was wrong about it. Wave 28’s smoke killed it; that row reads DONE 10/10. Do not rebuild it. Ratio floor: at least four slices where a PERSON is misinformed or cannot reach a control. The standing test, now six clauses. A fix whose only guard is a sentence is not fixed; a guard no job runs is a sentence with a shebang; a guard that cannot lose is a sentence with an exit code; a guard whose FIXTURE cannot produce the defect is green by construction; a guard whose SELECTOR cannot reach the defect is green by construction even with a cruel fixture; and an instrument POINTED AT THE WRONG ROOT — or reading an object its clone does not have — reports defect-shaped prose for a condition that is only "I could not look". REGISTER NOTHING. Do not touch .github/required-checks.json — it now MATCHES live protection, and any edit re-opens a drift that is finally closed. Ground truth re-derived at Strategize Everything the lead handed down was treated as L6 and re-derived. Four measurements, each with its own command, all taken from a detached worktree at origin/main a723ec0dd — never from the primary checkout, which reads ## main...origin/main [ahead 48, behind 401]. CLAIM COMMAND RESULT Four contexts BLOCK merges gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches/main/protection CONFIRMED — Elixir gate, PR references an active task, Cloud gate, Console gate; enforce_admins: true; identical to the committed spec on context AND app_id (15368). The required Console gate depends on a foreign host BP_SERVER=http://127.0.0.1:1 node --test cloud/priv/static/__preview__/seal-predicate.test.mjs CONFIRMED, and located to one line. 65 tests / 64 pass / not ok 56 — wave 11: --ladder-only reaches the ladder the live refusals never can, failing at seal-predicate.test.mjs:1090 with 2 !== 1: the control demands NO_SEAL(1) and a dead server yields INFRA(2). The reaching line is :1089 — run(['--repo', REPO, '--successor', 'TERMINAL']), a LIVE run whose roster fetch precedes the TERMINAL refusal. That roster read is anonymous curl -G .../v1/data/query/production/task -H "Authorization: Bearer undefined" 200 in 340ms. CI has no BP_TEST-scoped secret and does not need one — the gate is green today purely because guerrilla is up and the roster is world-readable. An ACL change reds it as surely as an outage. The unknown domain rung lies to a screen reader cloud/priv/static/app.js:9598 domainRungChip vs :9500 domainStageRows CONFIRMED, and it is the epic’s exact disease. The pure fold computes an honest unknown role and its 60-line header explains at length why an unmeasured rung must never fall into the waiting bucket. The RENDER has no unknown arm: it falls through to · and state = "waiting", so the aria-label says "waiting" for a check nobody made. The model knows; the screen lies. Premise smoke. Every charter D-number this direction cites was git show-n from origin/main and read for coverage, not existence: D307 (Law 0’s filing half), D325 (the cch-w22-s7 split), D331 (the D307 seat moves to writer.ex, the presence requirement stays unarmed), D334 (Law 0 re-derived; .preview-url cleared 20/20 by measurement; D325’s kill of C9 REFUTED on both its stated reasons). All four exist and all four authorise what they are cited for. Two code sites confirmed present on origin/main: seal-predicate.mjs verifyCommit (the catch that collapses rc 1 and rc 128 into one sentence) and app.js:9598 domainRungChip. Roster at Strategize: 310 children — {done 201, open 73, cancelled 35, considering 1}. The seal predicate’s own denominator (published-only) will read lower; wave 28 quoted roster 307 at 52a80c7be. Both integers get re-derived at Decide. Direction "I could not look" gets a grammar — and the merge lane stops being someone else’s host. Wave 27 found the sentence at the ROOT. Wave 28 found it at the OBJECT and shipped it to two audiences — the instrument and the person. Wave 29’s claim is that the sentence now has three audiences, and that the third one arrived today, uninvited, when branch protection went hard: AUDIENCE THE SENTENCE, POINTED AT IT WHAT IT COSTS TODAY The predicate rc 1 is an honest answer about the PRODUCT; rc 128 / missing object / shallow / no origin/main ref is an honest answer about the ENVIRONMENT. HISTORY-UNAVAILABLE surfaces as a verdict-token LETTER at exit 1. Six verbatim false "not an ancestor" sentences at b=FAIL in any depth-1 clone. Two waves quoted output of that shape as this epic’s primary finding. The merge lane A context that BLOCKS a merge must be a function of the DIFF. It may red for this repo’s bytes and for nothing else — not for a host we do not own, not for history the clone was never given. One line under a REQUIRED gate reaches guerrilla.barkpark.cloud. When that host blinks, every PR in the repo stops merging — not just this epic’s. The person A screen may say "we could not check" or it may say what it measured. It may never spend the product’s vocabulary for a deliberate non-measurement on a measurement that crashed. A crashed usage meter reads unmetered — the same word the flow meters use for "we deliberately do not measure this". An unmeasurable domain rung tells a screen reader "waiting". A resolver blip leaves the rail TERMINAL with no way back short of a navigation. This is not three themes stapled together. It is one sentence that generates all three, which is the shape wave 28 already proved works — "one disease, two audiences", now three. The ratio floor is not a tax on this direction; four of the strongest person rows on the board ARE instances of it. What the finished wave looks like The seal predicate can be run anywhere and never invents a finding. In a full clone it says b=PASS with a byte-identical token. In a pristine git clone --depth 1, a grafted depth-1, and a simulated actions/checkout@v4 PR shape it says HISTORY-UNAVAILABLE with ZERO "is not an ancestor" sentences — at exit 1, as a letter, never as an exit-2 INFRA-FAULT that would red s1’s merged control. And on a full clone with a register entry retargeted to a present-but-genuinely-not-an-ancestor sha it still prints exactly ONE honest product sentence at b=FAIL. The discrimination is proved by clones, not by stubs. No merge-blocking job can reach a host this repo does not own, and something reds if one regains the ability. The predicate’s exit-2 on an unreachable server is CORRECT and stays exactly as it is — the wave does not green a red. What moves is the QUESTION: the live-network assertion leaves the required path for somewhere it can be honestly red without freezing the repo, and a hermetic control just as cruel keeps proving the contrast that test exists to prove. Backed by a ratchet in the console-path-escape-check.sh --selftest family that can lose. Four screens stop reporting a failed measurement as a fact about the product. A meter that crashed says so. An unmeasurable rung says so, in its aria-label as well as its glyph, and offers a re-check instead of a dead end. Copy stops naming a provider it never asked. A publish that silently refused to deploy leaves an event a person can find. The board is shorter and honest about it. cch-w22-s7’s remainder is rebuilt against origin/main’s bytes — including the C9 leg D334 resurrected, whose substantive defect (collecting ws and te but not overflow) has its own model arm 400 lines below it in the same file. What this wave deliberately does not take .preview-url — D334 measured it 20/20 clean from a clean detached worktree, rc 0, worst urlLost −6.44px inside the clipper. The row reads DONE 10/10. Named here so no surveyor re-opens it. Any edit to .github/required-checks.json. REGISTER NOTHING. The spec matches live protection on context and app_id today; Required-check spec drift is green on main for the first time. An edit re-opens a drift that took eleven waves to close. Arming the D307 ABSENT tier. D331 measured the backfill: a description classifier scores 47%, a structured classifier 40%, and a one-line constant return "instruments" scores 73% — both classifiers below the majority baseline, on a three-day-old convention absent from 91% of the live population. A refusal cannot be armed over rows nobody can classify. At most a narrow ENUM question; the survey decides whether even that is a slice. And the scoping leg is a design boundary, not a load-bearing guard — 46 tests / 1 failure, not 23. Direction debate Two rivals were developed far enough to be shippable, then argued against each other. Neither was a straw man; both are what a reasonable strategist would do with this wish. Rival A — SCREENS ONLY Spend the whole wave on person rows. Take s2 because it is mandated and nothing else instrumental. The argument is strong: the epic’s vision sentence is the console stops lying, the ratio floor exists because instrument work keeps crowding out screens, and the board carries at least a dozen live person rows. The finished wave would be six screens a person can actually reach, which is the most legible good this epic produces. Why it loses: it was true yesterday and stopped being true today. The day four contexts started blocking, a host nobody in this repo controls acquired the power to freeze every merge in the repository — and I measured the coupling live rather than inferring it (not ok 56). Rival A spends the wave on this epic’s screens while every OTHER concurrent wave pays the outage. And it misreads the vision: a gate that reds for the wrong reason is the same lie, pointed at the fleet instead of at a customer. Rival B — THE LANE, END TO END An instrument wave. Harden all four required contexts, finish s2, promote D307, run the live half of required-checks.test.sh at four contexts for the first time, adjudicate Security gate’s registrability now that it is green. The argument: the merge lane is the single highest-leverage surface in the repo and it has never been exercised in its current shape. Why it loses: it violates two of this epic’s own laws at once. The ratio floor demands four person bodies. And Standing Law 0 sends every gate, generator, harness and required-checks row to the SUCCESSOR epic cch-instruments-epic — so an all-instrument wave filed under this parent would breach the filing law that wave 28 just armed a door guard for. Rival B is a real wave; it is the successor’s wave, not this one’s. Why the winner won The winner is not a split of A and B. It is the observation that the SAME sentence generates both halves, so the wave does not have to choose. "I could not look" ≠ "the thing is broken" is what s2 teaches a predicate, what the lane slice teaches a required context, and what four screens on the board are already failing at. A wave with one sentence is a wave whose Decide phase can adjudicate slices against a criterion instead of a wishlist — and it satisfies the ratio floor with rows chosen on merit rather than on quota. The sharpest attack on the winner, and how the wave absorbs it THE GATE SLICE MAY BE A NON-DEFECT, AND THE "FIX" MAY BE A WEAKENING. On a dead server the predicate correctly emitted an INFRA FAULT and the test correctly redded. That is an HONEST red. A wave that makes it green has softened a guard and called it hardening — the exact failure this epic exists to catch, committed by the wave that cites the standing test. Absorbed, not hedged. The wave does not green the red. The predicate’s exit-2 on an unreachable server is correct behaviour and is not touched. The defect is narrower and different: a context that BLOCKS a merge is asking a question whose answer lives on a host outside this repository. The remedy is relocation — the live assertion moves somewhere it can be honestly red without freezing the lane — plus a hermetic control that is just as cruel and still proves the contrast the test exists to prove (a live refusal never reaches the ladder; --ladder-only does). Three wrong fixes are banned by name in the slice brief, because each is green by construction under standing clause 4: try/catch around the spawn — the control passes on a dead server AND on a broken predicate. assert(status === NO_SEAL || status === INFRA) — a disjunction that admits the failure it was written to detect. Deleting the control — the contrast at :1089 IS the slice that shipped in wave 11; removing it retires a real proof to buy a green. Three further assumptions that could kill the direction, each now a survey question rather than a hedge: (i) Cloud gate may carry its own foreign coupling I have not measured — survey 1; (ii) the fix may require a .github/workflows/** edit that collides with the concurrent PDS wave — survey 12; (iii) the four person rows I named may be outranked on merit by rows I did not (phone overflow, PAT-survives-demotion, the credential Back button) — survey 7 ranks all 73 open rows without deference to this direction. Survey plan Sixteen broad assignments, one Opus surveyor each at medium effort. Width now buys precision at Verify. Every load-bearing assumption in the direction above appears below as something a surveyor can refute. # KEY QUESTION WHY IT CHANGES THE PLAN 1 gate-foreign-host Walk the needs graph of all four required contexts and enumerate every command that can reach a host this repo does not control. I measured exactly one under Console gate. Is that the only one? Decides whether the lane slice is one line or a family — and whether Cloud gate needs its own slice. 2 gate-history-coupling The five ladderOnlyRun sites read REAL git history through --repo REPO. Do they survive a real git clone --depth 1 --no-local? Row cch-w28-followup-seal-suite-depth1-coupling (0/2) asks exactly this. The second half of the lane slice. s1 proved 65/65 in a depth-1 clone — so either the coupling is benign or s1’s clone differed from CI’s. 3 s2-criteria-to-bytes Map s2’s nine criteria to the exact bytes they change in seal-predicate.mjs. Confirm the port source scripts/pds-record-parity.sh:261 walk_truncation() exists on origin/main and does what the criterion claims. s2 is mandated and its port citation is a premise nobody has smoked. That file is PDS-owned. 4 s2-exit-contract Trace how Infra propagates to the exit code, and find where a HISTORY-UNAVAILABLE LETTER can be emitted at exit 1 without touching the exit-2 path. Run s1’s clause-(a) assertions against a candidate shape. Getting this wrong reds a control that is already merged. The tripwire is armed on purpose. 5 person-unmetered Find the SERVER producer of usage meters and the client render. Prove or refute: a meter whose measurement CRASHED reaches a person as unmetered — the product’s own word for a deliberate non-measurement. Name the non-admin route. The purest person-facing instance of the wave’s sentence. If it refutes, the ratio needs another body. 6 person-domain-rung Confirm the aria-label an unknown rung produces, whether .dom-rung--unknown CSS exists at all, and map the TERMINAL half: where terminal stops the 4s poll and what mount could host a re-check control. Wish item 5, two halves in one slice. The builder named this risk himself; it cost three lines. Budgets PASS. One cross-slice landmine defused. render_test.exs quoted "Hetzner ran out of server capacity for this size." while the capacity-arm slice retires that literal IN THE SAME WAVE — green apart, RED TOGETHER. The leg now pins the class by derivation and asserts what it actually owes. Proved by an actual merge of both -r branches: 158/0. The three app.js slices were merged the same way: 814/0, smoke 102, cssom-parity PARITY PASS at 1289, __css_check 0 errors. What stalled, and what nobody proved Nothing stalled. All eight round-1 slices are green; there were no deferred rounds this wave, so there is no sequenced-rounds dispatch to chase. The seal predicate's NO-MERGE-BASE corroborator rests on ONE measured corroboration. A register entry on a genuinely disjoint history would degrade to HISTORY-UNAVAILABLE rather than the honest 'not an ancestor'. Fail-closed — it can never become a false PASS — but it is a behavioural claim, and it is this wave's flip-risk row. The byte-identity test skips itself on a checkout with unreadable history, so in a depth-1 CI clone it contributes nothing. The alternative pinned CI to a shape it does not have, which is what redded the roster control. No browser was driven anywhere. The domain re-check's guard reads source order, not behaviour; the refusal panel's ~230-character sentence has never been seen wrapping in a .deploy-row; the usage strip's new glyph was rendered only through the preview smoke. The overflow guard's new term has no COMMITTED fixture that exercises it, because its fail-before requires shipping the defect in CSS. It is protected in CI only in the negative sense — inherent to the leg, not a deferred task. Ledger audit All eight slice tasks: published, claimed, criteria stamped AS THE BUILDERS WORKED (evidence carries run output, not assertions), lifecycle honest, and only the merge-gated criterion open on each — 12/13, 6/7, 9/10, 7/8, 7/8, 7/8, 6/7, 6/7. Several criteria carry the builder's own limitation written INTO the evidence rather than hidden: the seal predicate's full-clone byte-identity substitution, the usage raise not being driven through the gatherer, the domain re-check's source-order guard. That is the behaviour the epic wants. Reviewer ledger fixes: every now-line named the PRE-REVIEW branch (and one said 'not pushed'), so all eight were re-pulsed with the final -r branch, its PR number and the reviewer's fix. One new backlog row filed — cch-w29-bl-safe-url-resolver-seam-unguarded — for the production affordance the new :resolver seam opens. The four rows builders filed were verified published under the epic. No task outside this wave was touched. Grade — A Earned, not given. What is genuinely strong: the discrimination slice is the best instrument work this epic has produced — five probes, a fifth leg nobody asked for that turns out to be the false PASS hiding behind the false FAIL, an exit contract honoured rather than re-litigated, and four REAL clones instead of stubs. The overflow slice's four-part probe is a model of refusing a comfortable non-mutation. Every builder report named its own weakest claim before anyone asked, and two of them argued with their brief and said so. The wish's ratio was not just met but exceeded — five person-facing rows, including two of the epic's purest examples. What falls short: three of the eight shipped a defect of exactly the class the epic exists to close, and a reviewer had to catch them — a cue predicate that could not reach a defect one CSS axis over, a refusal predicate that would have re-cast a progress line as an explained decision, and a recovery control that ate itself on failure. A cross-slice literal collision made two slices green apart and red together, which no builder could see and the wave's own file-fence discipline did not prevent. And nothing in this wave was seen by a human eye in a browser: five person-facing rows shipped on source-order guards and static renders. That is the gap between A and A+. What the next wave should take The D307 guard's promotion. The surface ENUM and the BACKFILL of open rows are what turn the WARN tier hard. The scoping leg is a DESIGN BOUNDARY (46 tests / 1 failure on deletion, not the 23 the criterion predicted) — do not restate it as load-bearing. cch-w22-s7's remainder, still adjudicated against origin/main's bytes rather than rebuilt. D325 stamped the five criteria the tree had already settled. A BROWSER PASS over what this wave shipped. Click the domain re-check; look at the refusal panel's 230-character sentence in a .deploy-row at 320px; look at the amber '?' in the fleet strip. Three of the five person rows have never been seen by an eye. The instrument rows this wave opened: cch-w29-bl-safe-url-resolver-seam-unguarded (a seam nothing stops production from using), the refused-auto-deploy event dispatcher (the toggle must not land ahead of it), the Go CLI usage twin, and task-79aa75e4be7a0067's two remaining stale capacity quotes in router.ex and a Go test comment. Dispatch order: merge round 1 in any order — the eight -r branches are file-disjoint except for app.js (three slices, disjoint regions, merged and proven together at 814/0) and the notifications pair (proven together at 158/0). If anything else adds a CSS rule head before #9460 lands, RE-MEASURE the cssom baseline by running cssom-parity.mjs on the merge; never add up two deltas. An independent second reviewer is owed on #9455 before merge. This workflow spawns exactly one reviewer, so the dispatch is a manual lead step. The judgment to re-derive independently is the NO-MERGE-BASE corroborator: whether 'merge-base found no common ancestor' is genuinely inseparable from 'this store cannot place the commit'. It was measured once, and it decides whether an honest product FAIL can be silently downgraded to an environment excuse.

reflow200.bodyText: Cloud Console Hardening — wave 29: “I could not look” gets a grammar, and the merge lane stops being someone else’s host Status: SURVEYING. Strategize is closed; 16 Opus surveyors are in flight. Digest appends the survey digest and the verify plan below before any verifier runs; Decide appends the decisions and the wave plan before any builder flies; Review closes this Paper as the debrief. Epic cloud-console-hardening-epic · predecessor wave Paper cloud-console-hardening-wave-28-2026-08-03 · charter .claude/workflows/bp-cloud-console-hardening-charter.md (read from origin/main, not the primary checkout, which is 401 commits behind). The wish Seven numbered instructions. Condensed, with the load-bearing corrections preserved: Finish the discrimination. cch-w28-s2-history-unavailable-discrimination is round 2 and #9356 has landed, so it is unblocked. Teach the git legs to tell rc 1 ("not an ancestor" — an honest answer about the PRODUCT) from rc 128 / missing object / shallow ("I could not look" — an honest answer about the ENVIRONMENT). Its hard constraint is already armed as a tripwire by s1: HISTORY-UNAVAILABLE must surface as a verdict-token LETTER at exit 1, never a process-level exit-2 INFRA-FAULT. The merge lane changed and every earlier brief is stale on this point. Live protection enforces FOUR contexts as of today. Console gate and Cloud gate are BLOCKING, not advisory. Required-check spec drift is GREEN on main for the first time this session. A required gate a third-party host can red is the same defect class as a guard no job runs. Wave 28 s3 documented that the now-REQUIRED Console gate depends on guerrilla.barkpark.cloud being reachable, and nobody fixed it. Tolerable while advisory; an outage on someone else’s host is now a repo-wide merge freeze. The D307 guard’s promotion. The guard is armed at the birth seat (#9405, a723ec0dd); the surface ENUM and the BACKFILL of open rows are what turn the WARN tier hard. The contested scoping criterion was re-measured by the lead: deleting only the scoping leg gives 46 tests / 1 failure, not the 23 the criterion predicted — so the scoping is a DESIGN BOUNDARY, not a load-bearing guard. Do not restate it as load-bearing. The s7 residue, person-facing. A re-check affordance for a TERMINAL unknown domain rail (the poll stops with no way back short of a navigation), plus domainRungChip’s missing unknown arm (task-1daff7bc1bf46ceb). cch-w22-s7’s remainder — finished or closed against origin/main’s bytes rather than rebuilt. .preview-url IS NOT A SLICE and the wish was wrong about it. Wave 28’s smoke killed it; that row reads DONE 10/10. Do not rebuild it. Ratio floor: at least four slices where a PERSON is misinformed or cannot reach a control. The standing test, now six clauses. A fix whose only guard is a sentence is not fixed; a guard no job runs is a sentence with a shebang; a guard that cannot lose is a sentence with an exit code; a guard whose FIXTURE cannot produce the defect is green by construction; a guard whose SELECTOR cannot reach the defect is green by construction even with a cruel fixture; and an instrument POINTED AT THE WRONG ROOT — or reading an object its clone does not have — reports defect-shaped prose for a condition that is only "I could not look". REGISTER NOTHING. Do not touch .github/required-checks.json — it now MATCHES live protection, and any edit re-opens a drift that is finally closed. Ground truth re-derived at Strategize Everything the lead handed down was treated as L6 and re-derived. Four measurements, each with its own command, all taken from a detached worktree at origin/main a723ec0dd — never from the primary checkout, which reads ## main...origin/main [ahead 48, behind 401]. CLAIM COMMAND RESULT Four contexts BLOCK merges gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches/main/protection CONFIRMED — Elixir gate, PR references an active task, Cloud gate, Console gate; enforce_admins: true; identical to the committed spec on context AND app_id (15368). The required Console gate depends on a foreign host BP_SERVER=http://127.0.0.1:1 node --test cloud/priv/static/__preview__/seal-predicate.test.mjs CONFIRMED, and located to one line. 65 tests / 64 pass / not ok 56 — wave 11: --ladder-only reaches the ladder the live refusals never can, failing at seal-predicate.test.mjs:1090 with 2 !== 1: the control demands NO_SEAL(1) and a dead server yields INFRA(2). The reaching line is :1089 — run(['--repo', REPO, '--successor', 'TERMINAL']), a LIVE run whose roster fetch precedes the TERMINAL refusal. That roster read is anonymous curl -G .../v1/data/query/production/task -H "Authorization: Bearer undefined" 200 in 340ms. CI has no BP_TEST-scoped secret and does not need one — the gate is green today purely because guerrilla is up and the roster is world-readable. An ACL change reds it as surely as an outage. The unknown domain rung lies to a screen reader cloud/priv/static/app.js:9598 domainRungChip vs :9500 domainStageRows CONFIRMED, and it is the epic’s exact disease. The pure fold computes an honest unknown role and its 60-line header explains at length why an unmeasured rung must never fall into the waiting bucket. The RENDER has no unknown arm: it falls through to · and state = "waiting", so the aria-label says "waiting" for a check nobody made. The model knows; the screen lies. Premise smoke. Every charter D-number this direction cites was git show-n from origin/main and read for coverage, not existence: D307 (Law 0’s filing half), D325 (the cch-w22-s7 split), D331 (the D307 seat moves to writer.ex, the presence requirement stays unarmed), D334 (Law 0 re-derived; .preview-url cleared 20/20 by measurement; D325’s kill of C9 REFUTED on both its stated reasons). All four exist and all four authorise what they are cited for. Two code sites confirmed present on origin/main: seal-predicate.mjs verifyCommit (the catch that collapses rc 1 and rc 128 into one sentence) and app.js:9598 domainRungChip. Roster at Strategize: 310 children — {done 201, open 73, cancelled 35, considering 1}. The seal predicate’s own denominator (published-only) will read lower; wave 28 quoted roster 307 at 52a80c7be. Both integers get re-derived at Decide. Direction "I could not look" gets a grammar — and the merge lane stops being someone else’s host. Wave 27 found the sentence at the ROOT. Wave 28 found it at the OBJECT and shipped it to two audiences — the instrument and the person. Wave 29’s claim is that the sentence now has three audiences, and that the third one arrived today, uninvited, when branch protection went hard: AUDIENCE THE SENTENCE, POINTED AT IT WHAT IT COSTS TODAY The predicate rc 1 is an honest answer about the PRODUCT; rc 128 / missing object / shallow / no origin/main ref is an honest answer about the ENVIRONMENT. HISTORY-UNAVAILABLE surfaces as a verdict-token LETTER at exit 1. Six verbatim false "not an ancestor" sentences at b=FAIL in any depth-1 clone. Two waves quoted output of that shape as this epic’s primary finding. The merge lane A context that BLOCKS a merge must be a function of the DIFF. It may red for this repo’s bytes and for nothing else — not for a host we do not own, not for history the clone was never given. One line under a REQUIRED gate reaches guerrilla.barkpark.cloud. When that host blinks, every PR in the repo stops merging — not just this epic’s. The person A screen may say "we could not check" or it may say what it measured. It may never spend the product’s vocabulary for a deliberate non-measurement on a measurement that crashed. A crashed usage meter reads unmetered — the same word the flow meters use for "we deliberately do not measure this". An unmeasurable domain rung tells a screen reader "waiting". A resolver blip leaves the rail TERMINAL with no way back short of a navigation. This is not three themes stapled together. It is one sentence that generates all three, which is the shape wave 28 already proved works — "one disease, two audiences", now three. The ratio floor is not a tax on this direction; four of the strongest person rows on the board ARE instances of it. What the finished wave looks like The seal predicate can be run anywhere and never invents a finding. In a full clone it says b=PASS with a byte-identical token. In a pristine git clone --depth 1, a grafted depth-1, and a simulated actions/checkout@v4 PR shape it says HISTORY-UNAVAILABLE with ZERO "is not an ancestor" sentences — at exit 1, as a letter, never as an exit-2 INFRA-FAULT that would red s1’s merged control. And on a full clone with a register entry retargeted to a present-but-genuinely-not-an-ancestor sha it still prints exactly ONE honest product sentence at b=FAIL. The discrimination is proved by clones, not by stubs. No merge-blocking job can reach a host this repo does not own, and something reds if one regains the ability. The predicate’s exit-2 on an unreachable server is CORRECT and stays exactly as it is — the wave does not green a red. What moves is the QUESTION: the live-network assertion leaves the required path for somewhere it can be honestly red without freezing the repo, and a hermetic control just as cruel keeps proving the contrast that test exists to prove. Backed by a ratchet in the console-path-escape-check.sh --selftest family that can lose. Four screens stop reporting a failed measurement as a fact about the product. A meter that crashed says so. An unmeasurable rung says so, in its aria-label as well as its glyph, and offers a re-check instead of a dead end. Copy stops naming a provider it never asked. A publish that silently refused to deploy leaves an event a person can find. The board is shorter and honest about it. cch-w22-s7’s remainder is rebuilt against origin/main’s bytes — including the C9 leg D334 resurrected, whose substantive defect (collecting ws and te but not overflow) has its own model arm 400 lines below it in the same file. What this wave deliberately does not take .preview-url — D334 measured it 20/20 clean from a clean detached worktree, rc 0, worst urlLost −6.44px inside the clipper. The row reads DONE 10/10. Named here so no surveyor re-opens it. Any edit to .github/required-checks.json. REGISTER NOTHING. The spec matches live protection on context and app_id today; Required-check spec drift is green on main for the first time. An edit re-opens a drift that took eleven waves to close. Arming the D307 ABSENT tier. D331 measured the backfill: a description classifier scores 47%, a structured classifier 40%, and a one-line constant return "instruments" scores 73% — both classifiers below the majority baseline, on a three-day-old convention absent from 91% of the live population. A refusal cannot be armed over rows nobody can classify. At most a narrow ENUM question; the survey decides whether even that is a slice. And the scoping leg is a design boundary, not a load-bearing guard — 46 tests / 1 failure, not 23. Direction debate Two rivals were developed far enough to be shippable, then argued against each other. Neither was a straw man; both are what a reasonable strategist would do with this wish. Rival A — SCREENS ONLY Spend the whole wave on person rows. Take s2 because it is mandated and nothing else instrumental. A fix whose only guard is a sentence is not fixed; a guard no job runs is a sentence with a shebang; a guard that cannot lose is a sentence with an exit code; a guard whose FIXTURE cannot produce the defect is green by construction; a guard whose SELECTOR cannot reach the defect is green by construction even with a cruel fixture; and an instrument POINTED AT THE WRONG ROOT — or reading an object its clone does not have — reports defect-shaped prose for a condition that is only "I could not look". REGISTER NOTHING. Do not touch .github/required-checks.json — it now MATCHES live protection, and any edit re-opens a drift that is finally closed. The instrument rows this wave opened: cch-w29-bl-safe-url-resolver-seam-unguarded (a seam nothing stops production from using), the refused-auto-deploy event dispatcher (the toggle must not land ahead of it), the Go CLI usage twin, and task-79aa75e4be7a0067's two remaining stale capacity quotes in router.ex and a Go test comment. Dispatch order: merge round 1 in any order — the eight -r branches are file-disjoint except for app.js (three slices, disjoint regions, merged and proven together at 814/0) and the notifications pair (proven together at 158/0). If anything else adds a CSS rule head before #9460 lands, RE-MEASURE the cssom baseline by running cssom-parity.mjs on the merge; never add up two deltas. An independent second reviewer is owed on #9455 before merge. This workflow spawns exactly one reviewer, so the dispatch is a manual lead step. The judgment to re-derive independently is the NO-MERGE-BASE corroborator: whether 'merge-base found no common ancestor' is genuinely inseparable from 'this store cannot place the commit'. 320.title: Cloud Console Hardening — wave 29: “I could not look” gets a grammar, and the merge lane stops being someone else’s host · Barkpark

390.bodyText: Cloud Console Hardening — wave 29: “I could not look” gets a grammar, and the merge lane stops being someone else’s host Status: SURVEYING. Strategize is closed; 16 Opus surveyors are in flight. Digest appends the survey digest and the verify plan below before any verifier runs; Decide appends the decisions and the wave plan before any builder flies; Review closes this Paper as the debrief. Epic cloud-console-hardening-epic · predecessor wave Paper cloud-console-hardening-wave-28-2026-08-03 · charter .claude/workflows/bp-cloud-console-hardening-charter.md (read from origin/main, not the primary checkout, which is 401 commits behind). The wish Seven numbered instructions. Condensed, with the load-bearing corrections preserved: Finish the discrimination. cch-w28-s2-history-unavailable-discrimination is round 2 and #9356 has landed, so it is unblocked. Teach the git legs to tell rc 1 ("not an ancestor" — an honest answer about the PRODUCT) from rc 128 / missing object / shallow ("I could not look" — an honest answer about the ENVIRONMENT). Its hard constraint is already armed as a tripwire by s1: HISTORY-UNAVAILABLE must surface as a verdict-token LETTER at exit 1, never a process-level exit-2 INFRA-FAULT. The merge lane changed and every earlier brief is stale on this point. Live protection enforces FOUR contexts as of today. Console gate and Cloud gate are BLOCKING, not advisory. Required-check spec drift is GREEN on main for the first time this session. A required gate a third-party host can red is the same defect class as a guard no job runs. Wave 28 s3 documented that the now-REQUIRED Console gate depends on guerrilla.barkpark.cloud being reachable, and nobody fixed it. Tolerable while advisory; an outage on someone else’s host is now a repo-wide merge freeze. The D307 guard’s promotion. The guard is armed at the birth seat (#9405, a723ec0dd); the surface ENUM and the BACKFILL of open rows are what turn the WARN tier hard. The contested scoping criterion was re-measured by the lead: deleting only the scoping leg gives 46 tests / 1 failure, not the 23 the criterion predicted — so the scoping is a DESIGN BOUNDARY, not a load-bearing guard. Do not restate it as load-bearing. The s7 residue, person-facing. A re-check affordance for a TERMINAL unknown domain rail (the poll stops with no way back short of a navigation), plus domainRungChip’s missing unknown arm (task-1daff7bc1bf46ceb). cch-w22-s7’s remainder — finished or closed against origin/main’s bytes rather than rebuilt. .preview-url IS NOT A SLICE and the wish was wrong about it. Wave 28’s smoke killed it; that row reads DONE 10/10. Do not rebuild it. Ratio floor: at least four slices where a PERSON is misinformed or cannot reach a control. The standing test, now six clauses. A fix whose only guard is a sentence is not fixed; a guard no job runs is a sentence with a shebang; a guard that cannot lose is a sentence with an exit code; a guard whose FIXTURE cannot produce the defect is green by construction; a guard whose SELECTOR cannot reach the defect is green by construction even with a cruel fixture; and an instrument POINTED AT THE WRONG ROOT — or reading an object its clone does not have — reports defect-shaped prose for a condition that is only "I could not look". REGISTER NOTHING. Do not touch .github/required-checks.json — it now MATCHES live protection, and any edit re-opens a drift that is finally closed. Ground truth re-derived at Strategize Everything the lead handed down was treated as L6 and re-derived. Four measurements, each with its own command, all taken from a detached worktree at origin/main a723ec0dd — never from the primary checkout, which reads ## main...origin/main [ahead 48, behind 401]. CLAIM COMMAND RESULT Four contexts BLOCK merges gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches/main/protection CONFIRMED — Elixir gate, PR references an active task, Cloud gate, Console gate; enforce_admins: true; identical to the committed spec on context AND app_id (15368). The required Console gate depends on a foreign host BP_SERVER=http://127.0.0.1:1 node --test cloud/priv/static/__preview__/seal-predicate.test.mjs CONFIRMED, and located to one line. 65 tests / 64 pass / not ok 56 — wave 11: --ladder-only reaches the ladder the live refusals never can, failing at seal-predicate.test.mjs:1090 with 2 !== 1: the control demands NO_SEAL(1) and a dead server yields INFRA(2). The reaching line is :1089 — run(['--repo', REPO, '--successor', 'TERMINAL']), a LIVE run whose roster fetch precedes the TERMINAL refusal. That roster read is anonymous curl -G .../v1/data/query/production/task -H "Authorization: Bearer undefined" 200 in 340ms. CI has no BP_TEST-scoped secret and does not need one — the gate is green today purely because guerrilla is up and the roster is world-readable. An ACL change reds it as surely as an outage. The unknown domain rung lies to a screen reader cloud/priv/static/app.js:9598 domainRungChip vs :9500 domainStageRows CONFIRMED, and it is the epic’s exact disease. The pure fold computes an honest unknown role and its 60-line header explains at length why an unmeasured rung must never fall into the waiting bucket. The RENDER has no unknown arm: it falls through to · and state = "waiting", so the aria-label says "waiting" for a check nobody made. The model knows; the screen lies. Premise smoke. Every charter D-number this direction cites was git show-n from origin/main and read for coverage, not existence: D307 (Law 0’s filing half), D325 (the cch-w22-s7 split), D331 (the D307 seat moves to writer.ex, the presence requirement stays unarmed), D334 (Law 0 re-derived; .preview-url cleared 20/20 by measurement; D325’s kill of C9 REFUTED on both its stated reasons). All four exist and all four authorise what they are cited for. Two code sites confirmed present on origin/main: seal-predicate.mjs verifyCommit (the catch that collapses rc 1 and rc 128 into one sentence) and app.js:9598 domainRungChip. Roster at Strategize: 310 children — {done 201, open 73, cancelled 35, considering 1}. The seal predicate’s own denominator (published-only) will read lower; wave 28 quoted roster 307 at 52a80c7be. Both integers get re-derived at Decide. Direction "I could not look" gets a grammar — and the merge lane stops being someone else’s host. Wave 27 found the sentence at the ROOT. Wave 28 found it at the OBJECT and shipped it to two audiences — the instrument and the person. Wave 29’s claim is that the sentence now has three audiences, and that the third one arrived today, uninvited, when branch protection went hard: AUDIENCE THE SENTENCE, POINTED AT IT WHAT IT COSTS TODAY The predicate rc 1 is an honest answer about the PRODUCT; rc 128 / missing object / shallow / no origin/main ref is an honest answer about the ENVIRONMENT. HISTORY-UNAVAILABLE surfaces as a verdict-token LETTER at exit 1. Six verbatim false "not an ancestor" sentences at b=FAIL in any depth-1 clone. Two waves quoted output of that shape as this epic’s primary finding. The merge lane A context that BLOCKS a merge must be a function of the DIFF. It may red for this repo’s bytes and for nothing else — not for a host we do not own, not for history the clone was never given. One line under a REQUIRED gate reaches guerrilla.barkpark.cloud. When that host blinks, every PR in the repo stops merging — not just this epic’s. The person A screen may say "we could not check" or it may say what it measured. It may never spend the product’s vocabulary for a deliberate non-measurement on a measurement that crashed. A crashed usage meter reads unmetered — the same word the flow meters use for "we deliberately do not measure this". An unmeasurable domain rung tells a screen reader "waiting". A resolver blip leaves the rail TERMINAL with no way back short of a navigation. This is not three themes stapled together. It is one sentence that generates all three, which is the shape wave 28 already proved works — "one disease, two audiences", now three. The ratio floor is not a tax on this direction; four of the strongest person rows on the board ARE instances of it. What the finished wave looks like The seal predicate can be run anywhere and never invents a finding. In a full clone it says b=PASS with a byte-identical token. In a pristine git clone --depth 1, a grafted depth-1, and a simulated actions/checkout@v4 PR shape it says HISTORY-UNAVAILABLE with ZERO "is not an ancestor" sentences — at exit 1, as a letter, never as an exit-2 INFRA-FAULT that would red s1’s merged control. And on a full clone with a register entry retargeted to a present-but-genuinely-not-an-ancestor sha it still prints exactly ONE honest product sentence at b=FAIL. The discrimination is proved by clones, not by stubs. No merge-blocking job can reach a host this repo does not own, and something reds if one regains the ability. The predicate’s exit-2 on an unreachable server is CORRECT and stays exactly as it is — the wave does not green a red. What moves is the QUESTION: the live-network assertion leaves the required path for somewhere it can be honestly red without freezing the repo, and a hermetic control just as cruel keeps proving the contrast that test exists to prove. Backed by a ratchet in the console-path-escape-check.sh --selftest family that can lose. Four screens stop reporting a failed measurement as a fact about the product. A meter that crashed says so. An unmeasurable rung says so, in its aria-label as well as its glyph, and offers a re-check instead of a dead end. Copy stops naming a provider it never asked. A publish that silently refused to deploy leaves an event a person can find. The board is shorter and honest about it. cch-w22-s7’s remainder is rebuilt against origin/main’s bytes — including the C9 leg D334 resurrected, whose substantive defect (collecting ws and te but not overflow) has its own model arm 400 lines below it in the same file. What this wave deliberately does not take .preview-url — D334 measured it 20/20 clean from a clean detached worktree, rc 0, worst urlLost −6.44px inside the clipper. The row reads DONE 10/10. Named here so no surveyor re-opens it. Any edit to .github/required-checks.json. REGISTER NOTHING. The spec matches live protection on context and app_id today; Required-check spec drift is green on main for the first time. An edit re-opens a drift that took eleven waves to close. Arming the D307 ABSENT tier. D331 measured the backfill: a description classifier scores 47%, a structured classifier 40%, and a one-line constant return "instruments" scores 73% — both classifiers below the majority baseline, on a three-day-old convention absent from 91% of the live population. A refusal cannot be armed over rows nobody can classify. At most a narrow ENUM question; the survey decides whether even that is a slice. And the scoping leg is a design boundary, not a load-bearing guard — 46 tests / 1 failure, not 23. Direction debate Two rivals were developed far enough to be shippable, then argued against each other. Neither was a straw man; both are what a reasonable strategist would do with this wish. Rival A — SCREENS ONLY Spend the whole wave on person rows. Take s2 because it is mandated and nothing else instrumental. The argument is strong: the epic’s vision sentence is the console stops lying, the ratio floor exists because instrument work keeps crowding out screens, and the board carries at least a dozen live person rows. The finished wave would be six screens a person can actually reach, which is the most legible good this epic produces. Why it loses: it was true yesterday and stopped being true today. The day four contexts started blocking, a host nobody in this repo controls acquired the power to freeze every merge in the repository — and I measured the coupling live rather than inferring it (not ok 56). Rival A spends the wave on this epic’s screens while every OTHER concurrent wave pays the outage. And it misreads the vision: a gate that reds for the wrong reason is the same lie, pointed at the fleet instead of at a customer. Rival B — THE LANE, END TO END An instrument wave. Harden all four required contexts, finish s2, promote D307, run the live half of required-checks.test.sh at four contexts for the first time, adjudicate Security gate’s registrability now that it is green. The argument: the merge lane is the single highest-leverage surface in the repo and it has never been exercised in its current shape. Why it loses: it violates two of this epic’s own laws at once. The ratio floor demands four person bodies. And Standing Law 0 sends every gate, generator, harness and required-checks row to the SUCCESSOR epic cch-instruments-epic — so an all-instrument wave filed under this parent would breach the filing law that wave 28 just armed a door guard for. Rival B is a real wave; it is the successor’s wave, not this one’s. Why the winner won The winner is not a split of A and B. It is the observation that the SAME sentence generates both halves, so the wave does not have to choose. "I could not look" ≠ "the thing is broken" is what s2 teaches a predicate, what the lane slice teaches a required context, and what four screens on the board are already failing at. A wave with one sentence is a wave whose Decide phase can adjudicate slices against a criterion instead of a wishlist — and it satisfies the ratio floor with rows chosen on merit rather than on quota. The sharpest attack on the winner, and how the wave absorbs it THE GATE SLICE MAY BE A NON-DEFECT, AND THE "FIX" MAY BE A WEAKENING. On a dead server the predicate correctly emitted an INFRA FAULT and the test correctly redded. That is an HONEST red. A wave that makes it green has softened a guard and called it hardening — the exact failure this epic exists to catch, committed by the wave that cites the standing test. Absorbed, not hedged. The wave does not green the red. The predicate’s exit-2 on an unreachable server is correct behaviour and is not touched. The defect is narrower and different: a context that BLOCKS a merge is asking a question whose answer lives on a host outside this repository. The remedy is relocation — the live assertion moves somewhere it can be honestly red without freezing the lane — plus a hermetic control that is just as cruel and still proves the contrast the test exists to prove (a live refusal never reaches the ladder; --ladder-only does). Three wrong fixes are banned by name in the slice brief, because each is green by construction under standing clause 4: try/catch around the spawn — the control passes on a dead server AND on a broken predicate. assert(status === NO_SEAL || status === INFRA) — a disjunction that admits the failure it was written to detect. Deleting the control — the contrast at :1089 IS the slice that shipped in wave 11; removing it retires a real proof to buy a green. Three further assumptions that could kill the direction, each now a survey question rather than a hedge: (i) Cloud gate may carry its own foreign coupling I have not measured — survey 1; (ii) the fix may require a .github/workflows/** edit that collides with the concurrent PDS wave — survey 12; (iii) the four person rows I named may be outranked on merit by rows I did not (phone overflow, PAT-survives-demotion, the credential Back button) — survey 7 ranks all 73 open rows without deference to this direction. Survey plan Sixteen broad assignments, one Opus surveyor each at medium effort. Width now buys precision at Verify. Every load-bearing assumption in the direction above appears below as something a surveyor can refute. # KEY QUESTION WHY IT CHANGES THE PLAN 1 gate-foreign-host Walk the needs graph of all four required contexts and enumerate every command that can reach a host this repo does not control. I measured exactly one under Console gate. Is that the only one? Decides whether the lane slice is one line or a family — and whether Cloud gate needs its own slice. 2 gate-history-coupling The five ladderOnlyRun sites read REAL git history through --repo REPO. Do they survive a real git clone --depth 1 --no-local? Row cch-w28-followup-seal-suite-depth1-coupling (0/2) asks exactly this. The second half of the lane slice. s1 proved 65/65 in a depth-1 clone — so either the coupling is benign or s1’s clone differed from CI’s. 3 s2-criteria-to-bytes Map s2’s nine criteria to the exact bytes they change in seal-predicate.mjs. Confirm the port source scripts/pds-record-parity.sh:261 walk_truncation() exists on origin/main and does what the criterion claims. s2 is mandated and its port citation is a premise nobody has smoked. That file is PDS-owned. 4 s2-exit-contract Trace how Infra propagates to the exit code, and find where a HISTORY-UNAVAILABLE LETTER can be emitted at exit 1 without touching the exit-2 path. Run s1’s clause-(a) assertions against a candidate shape. Getting this wrong reds a control that is already merged. The tripwire is armed on purpose. 5 person-unmetered Find the SERVER producer of usage meters and the client render. Prove or refute: a meter whose measurement CRASHED reaches a person as unmetered — the product’s own word for a deliberate non-measurement. Name the non-admin route. The purest person-facing instance of the wave’s sentence. If it refutes, the ratio needs another body. 6 person-domain-rung Confirm the aria-label an unknown rung produces, whether .dom-rung--unknown CSS exists at all, and map the TERMINAL half: where terminal stops the 4s poll and what mount could host a re-check control. Wish item 5, two halves in one slice. The pure fold is already honest — this is a render defect, which makes it small and provable. 7 person-row-ranking Read all 73 open children (bp task get cloud-console-hardening-epic -o json → .children, key doc_id) and rank every person-facing row by how badly a real person is misinformed, non-admin reachability, and slice size. Include rows this direction did NOT name. Ammunition against my own direction. The ratio picks must beat the alternatives on merit, not on fitting my sentence. 8 w22s7-remainder Re-derive cch-w22-s7 against origin/main: which of its 16 criteria are stampable TODAY, and is D334’s C9 re-scope a real buildable leg? The substantive defect is that overflow-guard.mjs:4083 collects ws and te but not overflow, while the model arm at :4534 collects ov: cs.overflow. Wish item 6. D325 said stamp five and kill C9; D334 refuted the kill on BOTH stated reasons. Somebody has to settle it against real bytes. 9 d307-promotion-cost What would actually turn the ABSENT tier hard? Read writer.ex:749-880 including the corrected comment at :824-834, find whether a surface ENUM exists as schema anywhere, and re-derive D331’s backfill numbers against TODAY’s roster. Decides slice vs. defer-with-a-sentence. Do not restate the scoping leg as load-bearing — the measured mutation is 46 tests / 1 failure. 10 required-checks-frozen Confirm live protection matches the committed spec on context AND app_id. Read required-checks-verify.sh, -floor.sh, -generate.sh. What could a wave do that silently re-opens the drift? REGISTER NOTHING is the standing instruction. I need to know precisely what "nothing" excludes — including whether a workflow rename counts. 11 guerrilla-as-ci-dependency How reliable is guerrilla.barkpark.cloud as a CI dependency? I measured the roster query anonymous, 200, 340ms. Search bp papers/tasks and the repo for recorded outages, 503s on cloud/** merges, rate limits, and any planned ACL change. Sizes the risk the lane slice removes. If guerrilla has never blinked, the slice is prudence; if it 503s on this repo’s own merges, it is urgent. 12 pds-collision-map The PDS wave runs concurrently on api/**, scripts/pds-*. Enumerate open PRs, live worktrees and recent commits holding anything my candidate slices touch — especially scripts/pds-record-parity.sh (s2’s port source) and scripts/elixir-path-escape-check.sh. A collision is far cheaper to route around at Decide than to merge out of at Build. 13 person-alert-email-bytes Wave 28 (#9407) wired :deployment_failed so the default-on alert can actually send. Quote the BYTES a person now receives for a deployment_failed and an agent_unreachable alert. Does FailureCopy reach the mail path at all? And what does a person NOT get told when @reap_alert_cap (25/sweep) bites? The sharpest sequencing available: wave 28 stopped the toggle lying, wave 29 stops the letter. The cap is a person-facing SUPPRESSION. 14 person-silent-deploy-refusal A content publish that silently refuses to deploy mints a cancelled row and no event exists for it anywhere. Find the refusal site, the row it mints, the event vocabulary, and what a person sees today. Confirm a non-admin publish reaches it. Same class as wave 28’s s6 — a state with no dispatch site — pointed at the deploy timeline instead of at alerts. 15 failure-copy-quota-arm Read failure_copy.ex as it stands after #9406 and #9408. Find the bare quota token’s arm and prove which provider strings can reach it — the row claims an Azure-failed person is told Hetzner ran out of servers. A small, sharp person slice adjacent to code two builders just touched, so the seam is warm. 16 hermetic-gate-precedent What in-tree precedent exists for proving a CI job hermetic? Read the path-escape ratchet family and its --selftest. Could a similar ratchet enumerate merge-blocking jobs and refuse a foreign host or a real-history read — and could it LOSE? Standing clauses 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 all apply to the lane slice at once. Without this, the lane fix is a sentence with a shebang. Tasks this Paper drives Named at Strategize as CANDIDATES, not as the wave plan. Decide files and perfects the actual slice rows and links this Paper onto each. TASK STATE ROLE IN THE DIRECTION cch-w28-s2-history-unavailable-discrimination open 0/9, unclaimed Mandated round-2 slice. Audience 1: the predicate. cch-w28-followup-seal-suite-depth1-coupling open 0/2 Audience 2, half one: the required gate’s history coupling. unfiled — the foreign-host coupling NOT FILED Audience 2, half two. Wave 28 s3 documented it; no row exists. Decide files it, and Law 0 sends it to cch-instruments-epic AT CREATE TIME. task-1daff7bc1bf46ceb open 0/3 PERSON. The unknown rung’s aria-label + the TERMINAL re-check affordance. cch-w28-bl-usage-meters-say-unmetered-when-they-could-not-measure open 0/3 PERSON. The purest instance of the wave’s sentence on a screen. cch-w26-bl-deployment-failed-email-still-unhumanized open 0/3 PERSON. Wave 28 made it send; wave 29 makes it readable. cch-w28-bl-auto-deploy-refusal-has-no-event-at-all open 0/3 PERSON. A refusal with no event anywhere. cch-w28-bl-capacity-arm-blames-hetzner-for-azure open 0/3 PERSON. Reserve body — small, sharp, warm seam. cch-w28-bl-w22s7-split-stamps-never-landed-and-c9-kill-is-refuted open 0/3 Wish item 6. Rebuilt against origin/main’s bytes, not closed against them. cch-w28-s4-followup-promote-absent-surface-to-hard open 0/3 Wish item 4. Probably a defer-with-a-sentence; survey 9 decides. Next append: DIGEST. The sixteen surveyor reports fold into a coverage-accounted digest and a verify plan, written here BEFORE any verifier flies. Nothing below the Direction heading is a decision yet — Decide is what turns a candidate into a slice. Survey digest — 16 reports, one sentence, three audiences Sixteen surveyors reported; coverage deficit none. The direction survives, but it survives CORRECTED on its most urgent half, and the survey found one hazard the direction did not anticipate that must be settled BEFORE Decide files a single row. Established, and re-derived by this phase rather than inherited FOUR required contexts, live: Elixir gate, PR references an active task, Cloud gate, Console gate — all app_id 15368, enforce_admins true. Re-derived by me and independently by three surveyors. The committed .github/required-checks.json byte-matches on context AND app_id. REGISTER NOTHING holds: no open PR touches that file. All eight wave-28 commits are ancestors of origin/main (0a1b4d2ea, dcba89411, a723ec0dd, 9b4e76d5c, 96a120b71, 156f7669d, b348779d6, 0d1936832). Verified, not inherited. Every code site the wish points a builder at still exists on origin/main: seal-predicate.mjs:489-490 (the swallowing bare catch), :1096 (the b= ternary seam), walk_truncation() at pds-record-parity.sh:261 exactly, failure_copy.ex:475-478, app.js:9598 domainRungChip, overflow-guard.mjs:4083/:4129, usage.ex:210, auto_deploy_worker.ex:176. Charter D307/D325/D328/D330/D331/D334 all present on origin/main and D334 READ FOR COVERAGE — it does authorize the C9 refutation, the cuePaints-is-alive claim, and taking .preview-url off the board on measurement (rc 0, 20/20 cells clean). The wish item 7 is correct: do not rebuild it. PREMISE SMOKE FAILURE — one phantom citation, caught before a builder chased it The charter at :536 names cssom-parity.mjs:608 as one of "two working in-tree implementations to cite" of the I-could-not-look doctrine. git show origin/main gives line 608 as a Chrome DevTools build-banner template literal. The whole 790-line file contains zero merge-base, zero shallow probe, zero git dependency — its only relevant text is the :195-200 comment REFUSING to take a git dependency. Wrong line AND "working implementation" overstates a documented refusal. The companion anchor at :538 (:189-193) is also off by ~6. s2 needs only the pds-record-parity.sh:261 citation, which is real and exact; the second citation must be struck or corrected in the slice brief, or a builder burns time on dead bytes and cites them back into the ledger. CORRECTION 1 — the lane slice’s finished state as written is unachievable, and three surveyors found it independently "No merge-blocking job reaches a host this repository does not own" cannot be built. PR references an active task reaches guerrilla.barkpark.cloud BY DESIGN and BY POLICY: pr-task-gate.yml:257 GETs the ledger, :202 POSTs a mutation with a repo secret, and the step body converts the script’s exit 2 into exit 1 under the annotation "Ledger unreachable — task backing UNVERIFIED", arguing in its own comment that "the only alternative to red is a green check that verified nothing". docs/ops/merge-gates.md:75 codifies it: ledger outage = a red that says so. So the repo has ALREADY adjudicated this wave’s question in committed bytes on a blocking gate. An unclassified reason now egresses SCRUBBED to five third-party hosts — the email's own boundary since wave 13 S2, but more bytes than yesterday. cch-w28-bl-capacity-arm-blames-hetzner-for-azure loop-epic/the-capacity-arm-names-one-provider-and--7-r #9464 Re-scoped correctly: the Azure half is NOT derivable (zero hits across source, tests and 18 fixtures), so the fix rests entirely on the resource-blindness the tree CAN produce — a verb-less zone-quota capture told it ran out of SERVER capacity. Blast radius beyond the fence handled; three co-edited test files, 123/0. Reviewer fixes — in place, gate-proven, none a redesign graftList read prose. It detected 'store is not shallow' by comparing walkTruncation().reason to a literal sentence — a control path coupled to a string anyone may reword. It reads an explicit shallowStore boolean now. The builder named this risk himself; it cost three lines. The overflow guard's cue predicate reads the X AXIS, not the shorthand. overflow-x: visible; overflow-y: clip is a legal pair the spec does not blockify, so Chrome serialises it as "visible clip". Probed both ways with a 101-char email and an ancestor clip: the shipped shorthand test printed OVERFLOW GUARD PASS with ZERO name findings over 469px of a spilled identity (rc 0); the axis test reds at 22 findings, each naming overflow-x "visible". That is clause 5 of the standing test firing inside the fix for clause 5. A domain re-check that FAILED restored nothing. Both mounts bail on 404/error WITHOUT repainting, and the click handler disables the button and relabels it 'Checking…' — so the only way back from a terminal unmeasurable rail sat permanently disabled announcing work nobody was doing. Mutation-proven 803/1 -> 804/0. A stale stage caption is not a refusal. Registry.cancel_preview/2 changes only status + console, so a superseded preview keeps whatever caption Sites.Deploy last wrote — 'Uploading bundle', or on a cancelled LIVE row 'live at https://…'. The shipped detail-keyed predicate would have painted those inside the amber FAILURE panel: a progress line re-cast as an explained decision, the slice's own defect class one row over. Keyed on failure_reason now; the detail-only test legs adjudicated, not deleted. The Overview strip's "?" carries a sentence. A bare glyph is what this epic refuses; a screen reader said 'DOCS, question mark'. The reason the Usage tab prints in full now rides along as title + aria-label. Two now-false sentences corrected at the source. event_email.ex claimed 'Render.render/2 never reads it' — false as of this very wave (closes cch-w29-bl-event-email-scrub-comment-stale); and cloud/DESIGN.md quoted the retired capacity literal as the shipped sentence. Budgets PASS. One cross-slice landmine defused. render_test.exs quoted "Hetzner ran out of server capacity for this size." while the capacity-arm slice retires that literal IN THE SAME WAVE — green apart, RED TOGETHER. The leg now pins the class by derivation and asserts what it actually owes. Proved by an actual merge of both -r branches: 158/0. The three app.js slices were merged the same way: 814/0, smoke 102, cssom-parity PARITY PASS at 1289, __css_check 0 errors. What stalled, and what nobody proved Nothing stalled. All eight round-1 slices are green; there were no deferred rounds this wave, so there is no sequenced-rounds dispatch to chase. The seal predicate's NO-MERGE-BASE corroborator rests on ONE measured corroboration. A register entry on a genuinely disjoint history would degrade to HISTORY-UNAVAILABLE rather than the honest 'not an ancestor'. Fail-closed — it can never become a false PASS — but it is a behavioural claim, and it is this wave's flip-risk row. The byte-identity test skips itself on a checkout with unreadable history, so in a depth-1 CI clone it contributes nothing. The alternative pinned CI to a shape it does not have, which is what redded the roster control. No browser was driven anywhere. The domain re-check's guard reads source order, not behaviour; the refusal panel's ~230-character sentence has never been seen wrapping in a .deploy-row; the usage strip's new glyph was rendered only through the preview smoke. The overflow guard's new term has no COMMITTED fixture that exercises it, because its fail-before requires shipping the defect in CSS. It is protected in CI only in the negative sense — inherent to the leg, not a deferred task. Ledger audit All eight slice tasks: published, claimed, criteria stamped AS THE BUILDERS WORKED (evidence carries run output, not assertions), lifecycle honest, and only the merge-gated criterion open on each — 12/13, 6/7, 9/10, 7/8, 7/8, 7/8, 6/7, 6/7. Several criteria carry the builder's own limitation written INTO the evidence rather than hidden: the seal predicate's full-clone byte-identity substitution, the usage raise not being driven through the gatherer, the domain re-check's source-order guard. That is the behaviour the epic wants. Reviewer ledger fixes: every now-line named the PRE-REVIEW branch (and one said 'not pushed'), so all eight were re-pulsed with the final -r branch, its PR number and the reviewer's fix. One new backlog row filed — cch-w29-bl-safe-url-resolver-seam-unguarded — for the production affordance the new :resolver seam opens. The four rows builders filed were verified published under the epic. No task outside this wave was touched. Grade — A Earned, not given. What is genuinely strong: the discrimination slice is the best instrument work this epic has produced — five probes, a fifth leg nobody asked for that turns out to be the false PASS hiding behind the false FAIL, an exit contract honoured rather than re-litigated, and four REAL clones instead of stubs. The overflow slice's four-part probe is a model of refusing a comfortable non-mutation. Every builder report named its own weakest claim before anyone asked, and two of them argued with their brief and said so. The wish's ratio was not just met but exceeded — five person-facing rows, including two of the epic's purest examples. What falls short: three of the eight shipped a defect of exactly the class the epic exists to close, and a reviewer had to catch them — a cue predicate that could not reach a defect one CSS axis over, a refusal predicate that would have re-cast a progress line as an explained decision, and a recovery control that ate itself on failure. A cross-slice literal collision made two slices green apart and red together, which no builder could see and the wave's own file-fence discipline did not prevent. And nothing in this wave was seen by a human eye in a browser: five person-facing rows shipped on source-order guards and static renders. That is the gap between A and A+. What the next wave should take The D307 guard's promotion. The surface ENUM and the BACKFILL of open rows are what turn the WARN tier hard. The scoping leg is a DESIGN BOUNDARY (46 tests / 1 failure on deletion, not the 23 the criterion predicted) — do not restate it as load-bearing. cch-w22-s7's remainder, still adjudicated against origin/main's bytes rather than rebuilt. D325 stamped the five criteria the tree had already settled. A BROWSER PASS over what this wave shipped. Click the domain re-check; look at the refusal panel's 230-character sentence in a .deploy-row at 320px; look at the amber '?' in the fleet strip. Three of the five person rows have never been seen by an eye. The instrument rows this wave opened: cch-w29-bl-safe-url-resolver-seam-unguarded (a seam nothing stops production from using), the refused-auto-deploy event dispatcher (the toggle must not land ahead of it), the Go CLI usage twin, and task-79aa75e4be7a0067's two remaining stale capacity quotes in router.ex and a Go test comment. Dispatch order: merge round 1 in any order — the eight -r branches are file-disjoint except for app.js (three slices, disjoint regions, merged and proven together at 814/0) and the notifications pair (proven together at 158/0). If anything else adds a CSS rule head before #9460 lands, RE-MEASURE the cssom baseline by running cssom-parity.mjs on the merge; never add up two deltas. An independent second reviewer is owed on #9455 before merge. This workflow spawns exactly one reviewer, so the dispatch is a manual lead step. The judgment to re-derive independently is the NO-MERGE-BASE corroborator: whether 'merge-base found no common ancestor' is genuinely inseparable from 'this store cannot place the commit'. It was measured once, and it decides whether an honest product FAIL can be silently downgraded to an environment excuse. TUI view Email view
