390.title: Cloud Console Hardening — wave 29: “I could not look” gets a grammar, and the merge lane stops being someone else’s host · Barkpark

desktop.bodyText: Cloud Console Hardening — wave 29: “I could not look” gets a grammar, and the merge lane stops being someone else’s host Status: SURVEYING. Strategize is closed; 16 Opus surveyors are in flight. Digest appends the survey digest and the verify plan below before any verifier runs; Decide appends the decisions and the wave plan before any builder flies; Review closes this Paper as the debrief. Epic cloud-console-hardening-epic · predecessor wave Paper cloud-console-hardening-wave-28-2026-08-03 · charter .claude/workflows/bp-cloud-console-hardening-charter.md (read from origin/main, not the primary checkout, which is 401 commits behind). The wish Seven numbered instructions. Condensed, with the load-bearing corrections preserved: Finish the discrimination. cch-w28-s2-history-unavailable-discrimination is round 2 and #9356 has landed, so it is unblocked. Teach the git legs to tell rc 1 ("not an ancestor" — an honest answer about the PRODUCT) from rc 128 / missing object / shallow ("I could not look" — an honest answer about the ENVIRONMENT). Its hard constraint is already armed as a tripwire by s1: HISTORY-UNAVAILABLE must surface as a verdict-token LETTER at exit 1, never a process-level exit-2 INFRA-FAULT. The merge lane changed and every earlier brief is stale on this point. Live protection enforces FOUR contexts as of today. Console gate and Cloud gate are BLOCKING, not advisory. Required-check spec drift is GREEN on main for the first time this session. A required gate a third-party host can red is the same defect class as a guard no job runs. Wave 28 s3 documented that the now-REQUIRED Console gate depends on guerrilla.barkpark.cloud being reachable, and nobody fixed it. Tolerable while advisory; an outage on someone else’s host is now a repo-wide merge freeze. The D307 guard’s promotion. The guard is armed at the birth seat (#9405, a723ec0dd); the surface ENUM and the BACKFILL of open rows are what turn the WARN tier hard. The contested scoping criterion was re-measured by the lead: deleting only the scoping leg gives 46 tests / 1 failure, not the 23 the criterion predicted — so the scoping is a DESIGN BOUNDARY, not a load-bearing guard. Do not restate it as load-bearing. The s7 residue, person-facing. A re-check affordance for a TERMINAL unknown domain rail (the poll stops with no way back short of a navigation), plus domainRungChip’s missing unknown arm (task-1daff7bc1bf46ceb). cch-w22-s7’s remainder — finished or closed against origin/main’s bytes rather than rebuilt. .preview-url IS NOT A SLICE and the wish was wrong about it. Wave 28’s smoke killed it; that row reads DONE 10/10. Do not rebuild it. Ratio floor: at least four slices where a PERSON is misinformed or cannot reach a control. The standing test, now six clauses. A fix whose only guard is a sentence is not fixed; a guard no job runs is a sentence with a shebang; a guard that cannot lose is a sentence with an exit code; a guard whose FIXTURE cannot produce the defect is green by construction; a guard whose SELECTOR cannot reach the defect is green by construction even with a cruel fixture; and an instrument POINTED AT THE WRONG ROOT — or reading an object its clone does not have — reports defect-shaped prose for a condition that is only "I could not look". REGISTER NOTHING. Do not touch .github/required-checks.json — it now MATCHES live protection, and any edit re-opens a drift that is finally closed. Ground truth re-derived at Strategize Everything the lead handed down was treated as L6 and re-derived. Four measurements, each with its own command, all taken from a detached worktree at origin/main a723ec0dd — never from the primary checkout, which reads ## main...origin/main [ahead 48, behind 401]. CLAIM COMMAND RESULT Four contexts BLOCK merges gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches/main/protection CONFIRMED — Elixir gate, PR references an active task, Cloud gate, Console gate; enforce_admins: true; identical to the committed spec on context AND app_id (15368). The required Console gate depends on a foreign host BP_SERVER=http://127.0.0.1:1 node --test cloud/priv/static/__preview__/seal-predicate.test.mjs CONFIRMED, and located to one line. 65 tests / 64 pass / not ok 56 — wave 11: --ladder-only reaches the ladder the live refusals never can, failing at seal-predicate.test.mjs:1090 with 2 !== 1: the control demands NO_SEAL(1) and a dead server yields INFRA(2). The reaching line is :1089 — run(['--repo', REPO, '--successor', 'TERMINAL']), a LIVE run whose roster fetch precedes the TERMINAL refusal. That roster read is anonymous curl -G .../v1/data/query/production/task -H "Authorization: Bearer undefined" 200 in 340ms. CI has no BP_TEST-scoped secret and does not need one — the gate is green today purely because guerrilla is up and the roster is world-readable. An ACL change reds it as surely as an outage. The unknown domain rung lies to a screen reader cloud/priv/static/app.js:9598 domainRungChip vs :9500 domainStageRows CONFIRMED, and it is the epic’s exact disease. The pure fold computes an honest unknown role and its 60-line header explains at length why an unmeasured rung must never fall into the waiting bucket. The RENDER has no unknown arm: it falls through to · and state = "waiting", so the aria-label says "waiting" for a check nobody made. The model knows; the screen lies. Premise smoke. Every charter D-number this direction cites was git show-n from origin/main and read for coverage, not existence: D307 (Law 0’s filing half), D325 (the cch-w22-s7 split), D331 (the D307 seat moves to writer.ex, the presence requirement stays unarmed), D334 (Law 0 re-derived; .preview-url cleared 20/20 by measurement; D325’s kill of C9 REFUTED on both its stated reasons). All four exist and all four authorise what they are cited for. Two code sites confirmed present on origin/main: seal-predicate.mjs verifyCommit (the catch that collapses rc 1 and rc 128 into one sentence) and app.js:9598 domainRungChip. Roster at Strategize: 310 children — {done 201, open 73, cancelled 35, considering 1}. The seal predicate’s own denominator (published-only) will read lower; wave 28 quoted roster 307 at 52a80c7be. Both integers get re-derived at Decide. Direction "I could not look" gets a grammar — and the merge lane stops being someone else’s host. Wave 27 found the sentence at the ROOT. Wave 28 found it at the OBJECT and shipped it to two audiences — the instrument and the person. Wave 29’s claim is that the sentence now has three audiences, and that the third one arrived today, uninvited, when branch protection went hard: AUDIENCE THE SENTENCE, POINTED AT IT WHAT IT COSTS TODAY The predicate rc 1 is an honest answer about the PRODUCT; rc 128 / missing object / shallow / no origin/main ref is an honest answer about the ENVIRONMENT. HISTORY-UNAVAILABLE surfaces as a verdict-token LETTER at exit 1. Six verbatim false "not an ancestor" sentences at b=FAIL in any depth-1 clone. Two waves quoted output of that shape as this epic’s primary finding. The merge lane A context that BLOCKS a merge must be a function of the DIFF. It may red for this repo’s bytes and for nothing else — not for a host we do not own, not for history the clone was never given. One line under a REQUIRED gate reaches guerrilla.barkpark.cloud. When that host blinks, every PR in the repo stops merging — not just this epic’s. The person A screen may say "we could not check" or it may say what it measured. It may never spend the product’s vocabulary for a deliberate non-measurement on a measurement that crashed. A crashed usage meter reads unmetered — the same word the flow meters use for "we deliberately do not measure this". An unmeasurable domain rung tells a screen reader "waiting". A resolver blip leaves the rail TERMINAL with no way back short of a navigation. This is not three themes stapled together. It is one sentence that generates all three, which is the shape wave 28 already proved works — "one disease, two audiences", now three. The ratio floor is not a tax on this direction; four of the strongest person rows on the board ARE instances of it. What the finished wave looks like The seal predicate can be run anywhere and never invents a finding. In a full clone it says b=PASS with a byte-identical token. In a pristine git clone --depth 1, a grafted depth-1, and a simulated actions/checkout@v4 PR shape it says HISTORY-UNAVAILABLE with ZERO "is not an ancestor" sentences — at exit 1, as a letter, never as an exit-2 INFRA-FAULT that would red s1’s merged control. And on a full clone with a register entry retargeted to a present-but-genuinely-not-an-ancestor sha it still prints exactly ONE honest product sentence at b=FAIL. The discrimination is proved by clones, not by stubs. No merge-blocking job can reach a host this repo does not own, and something reds if one regains the ability. The predicate’s exit-2 on an unreachable server is CORRECT and stays exactly as it is — the wave does not green a red. What moves is the QUESTION: the live-network assertion leaves the required path for somewhere it can be honestly red without freezing the repo, and a hermetic control just as cruel keeps proving the contrast that test exists to prove. Backed by a ratchet in the console-path-escape-check.sh --selftest family that can lose. Four screens stop reporting a failed measurement as a fact about the product. A meter that crashed says so. An unmeasurable rung says so, in its aria-label as well as its glyph, and offers a re-check instead of a dead end. Copy stops naming a provider it never asked. A publish that silently refused to deploy leaves an event a person can find. The board is shorter and honest about it. cch-w22-s7’s remainder is rebuilt against origin/main’s bytes — including the C9 leg D334 resurrected, whose substantive defect (collecting ws and te but not overflow) has its own model arm 400 lines below it in the same file. What this wave deliberately does not take .preview-url — D334 measured it 20/20 clean from a clean detached worktree, rc 0, worst urlLost −6.44px inside the clipper. The row reads DONE 10/10. Named here so no surveyor re-opens it. Any edit to .github/required-checks.json. REGISTER NOTHING. The spec matches live protection on context and app_id today; Required-check spec drift is green on main for the first time. An edit re-opens a drift that took eleven waves to close. Arming the D307 ABSENT tier. D331 measured the backfill: a description classifier scores 47%, a structured classifier 40%, and a one-line constant return "instruments" scores 73% — both classifiers below the majority baseline, on a three-day-old convention absent from 91% of the live population. A refusal cannot be armed over rows nobody can classify. At most a narrow ENUM question; the survey decides whether even that is a slice. And the scoping leg is a design boundary, not a load-bearing guard — 46 tests / 1 failure, not 23. Direction debate Two rivals were developed far enough to be shippable, then argued against each other. Neither was a straw man; both are what a reasonable strategist would do with this wish. Rival A — SCREENS ONLY Spend the whole wave on person rows. Take s2 because it is mandated and nothing else instrumental. The argument is strong: the epic’s vision sentence is the console stops lying, the ratio floor exists because instrument work keeps crowding out screens, and the board carries at least a dozen live person rows. The finished wave would be six screens a person can actually reach, which is the most legible good this epic produces. Why it loses: it was true yesterday and stopped being true today. The day four contexts started blocking, a host nobody in this repo controls acquired the power to freeze every merge in the repository — and I measured the coupling live rather than inferring it (not ok 56). Rival A spends the wave on this epic’s screens while every OTHER concurrent wave pays the outage. And it misreads the vision: a gate that reds for the wrong reason is the same lie, pointed at the fleet instead of at a customer. Rival B — THE LANE, END TO END An instrument wave. Harden all four required contexts, finish s2, promote D307, run the live half of required-checks.test.sh at four contexts for the first time, adjudicate Security gate’s registrability now that it is green. The argument: the merge lane is the single highest-leverage surface in the repo and it has never been exercised in its current shape. Why it loses: it violates two of this epic’s own laws at once. The ratio floor demands four person bodies. And Standing Law 0 sends every gate, generator, harness and required-checks row to the SUCCESSOR epic cch-instruments-epic — so an all-instrument wave filed under this parent would breach the filing law that wave 28 just armed a door guard for. Rival B is a real wave; it is the successor’s wave, not this one’s. Why the winner won The winner is not a split of A and B. It is the observation that the SAME sentence generates both halves, so the wave does not have to choose. "I could not look" ≠ "the thing is broken" is what s2 teaches a predicate, what the lane slice teaches a required context, and what four screens on the board are already failing at. A wave with one sentence is a wave whose Decide phase can adjudicate slices against a criterion instead of a wishlist — and it satisfies the ratio floor with rows chosen on merit rather than on quota. The sharpest attack on the winner, and how the wave absorbs it THE GATE SLICE MAY BE A NON-DEFECT, AND THE "FIX" MAY BE A WEAKENING. On a dead server the predicate correctly emitted an INFRA FAULT and the test correctly redded. That is an HONEST red. A wave that makes it green has softened a guard and called it hardening — the exact failure this epic exists to catch, committed by the wave that cites the standing test. Absorbed, not hedged. The wave does not green the red. The predicate’s exit-2 on an unreachable server is correct behaviour and is not touched. The defect is narrower and different: a context that BLOCKS a merge is asking a question whose answer lives on a host outside this repository. The remedy is relocation — the live assertion moves somewhere it can be honestly red without freezing the lane — plus a hermetic control that is just as cruel and still proves the contrast the test exists to prove (a live refusal never reaches the ladder; --ladder-only does). Three wrong fixes are banned by name in the slice brief, because each is green by construction under standing clause 4: try/catch around the spawn — the control passes on a dead server AND on a broken predicate. assert(status === NO_SEAL || status === INFRA) — a disjunction that admits the failure it was written to detect. Deleting the control — the contrast at :1089 IS the slice that shipped in wave 11; removing it retires a real proof to buy a green. Three further assumptions that could kill the direction, each now a survey question rather than a hedge: (i) Cloud gate may carry its own foreign coupling I have not measured — survey 1; (ii) the fix may require a .github/workflows/** edit that collides with the concurrent PDS wave — survey 12; (iii) the four person rows I named may be outranked on merit by rows I did not (phone overflow, PAT-survives-demotion, the credential Back button) — survey 7 ranks all 73 open rows without deference to this direction. Survey plan Sixteen broad assignments, one Opus surveyor each at medium effort. Width now buys precision at Verify. Every load-bearing assumption in the direction above appears below as something a surveyor can refute. # KEY QUESTION WHY IT CHANGES THE PLAN 1 gate-foreign-host Walk the needs graph of all four required contexts and enumerate every command that can reach a host this repo does not control. I measured exactly one under Console gate. Is that the only one? Decides whether the lane slice is one line or a family — and whether Cloud gate needs its own slice. 2 gate-history-coupling The five ladderOnlyRun sites read REAL git history through --repo REPO. Do they survive a real git clone --depth 1 --no-local? Row cch-w28-followup-seal-suite-depth1-coupling (0/2) asks exactly this. The second half of the lane slice. s1 proved 65/65 in a depth-1 clone — so either the coupling is benign or s1’s clone differed from CI’s. 3 s2-criteria-to-bytes Map s2’s nine criteria to the exact bytes they change in seal-predicate.mjs. Confirm the port source scripts/pds-record-parity.sh:261 walk_truncation() exists on origin/main and does what the criterion claims. s2 is mandated and its port citation is a premise nobody has smoked. That file is PDS-owned. 4 s2-exit-contract Trace how Infra propagates to the exit code, and find where a HISTORY-UNAVAILABLE LETTER can be emitted at exit 1 without touching the exit-2 path. Run s1’s clause-(a) assertions against a candidate shape. Getting this wrong reds a control that is already merged. The tripwire is armed on purpose. 5 person-unmetered Find the SERVER producer of usage meters and the client render. Prove or refute: a meter whose measurement CRASHED reaches a person as unmetered — the product’s own word for a deliberate non-measurement. Name the non-admin route. The purest person-facing instance of the wave’s sentence. If it refutes, the ratio needs another body. 6 person-domain-rung Confirm the aria-label an unknown rung produces, whether .dom-rung--unknown CSS exists at all, and map the TERMINAL half: where terminal stops the 4s poll and what mount could host a re-check control. Wish item 5, two halves in one slice. The pure fold is already honest — this is a render defect, which makes it small and provable. 7 person-row-ranking Read all 73 open children (bp task get cloud-console-hardening-epic -o json → .children, key doc_id) and rank every person-facing row by how badly a real person is misinformed, non-admin reachability, and slice size. Include rows this direction did NOT name. Ammunition against my own direction. The ratio picks must beat the alternatives on merit, not on fitting my sentence. 8 w22s7-remainder Re-derive cch-w22-s7 against origin/main: which of its 16 criteria are stampable TODAY, and is D334’s C9 re-scope a real buildable leg? The substantive defect is that overflow-guard.mjs:4083 collects ws and te but not overflow, while the model arm at :4534 collects ov: cs.overflow. Wish item 6. D325 said stamp five and kill C9; D334 refuted the kill on BOTH stated reasons. Somebody has to settle it against real bytes. 9 d307-promotion-cost What would actually turn the ABSENT tier hard? Read writer.ex:749-880 including the corrected comment at :824-834, find whether a surface ENUM exists as schema anywhere, and re-derive D331’s backfill numbers against TODAY’s roster. Decides slice vs. defer-with-a-sentence. Do not restate the scoping leg as load-bearing — the measured mutation is 46 tests / 1 failure. 10 required-checks-frozen Confirm live protection matches the committed spec on context AND app_id. Read required-checks-verify.sh, -floor.sh, -generate.sh. What could a wave do that silently re-opens the drift? REGISTER NOTHING is the standing instruction. I need to know precisely what "nothing" excludes — including whether a workflow rename counts. 11 guerrilla-as-ci-dependency How reliable is guerrilla.barkpark.cloud as a CI dependency? I measured the roster query anonymous, 200, 340ms. Search bp papers/tasks and the repo for recorded outages, 503s on cloud/** merges, rate limits, and any planned ACL change. Sizes the risk the lane slice removes. If guerrilla has never blinked, the slice is prudence; if it 503s on this repo’s own merges, it is urgent. 12 pds-collision-map The PDS wave runs concurrently on api/**, scripts/pds-*. Enumerate open PRs, live worktrees and recent commits holding anything my candidate slices touch — especially scripts/pds-record-parity.sh (s2’s port source) and scripts/elixir-path-escape-check.sh. A collision is far cheaper to route around at Decide than to merge out of at Build. 13 person-alert-email-bytes Wave 28 (#9407) wired :deployment_failed so the default-on alert can actually send. That is clause 5 of the standing test firing inside the fix for clause 5. A domain re-check that FAILED restored nothing. Mutation-proven 803/1 -> 804/0. A stale stage caption is not a refusal. The shipped detail-keyed predicate would have painted those inside the amber FAILURE panel: a progress line re-cast as an explained decision, the slice's own defect class one row over. Keyed on failure_reason now; the detail-only test legs adjudicated, not deleted. The Overview strip's "?" carries a sentence. A bare glyph is what this epic refuses; a screen reader said 'DOCS, question mark'. The reason the Usage tab prints in full now rides along as title + aria-label. Two now-false sentences corrected at the source. event_email.ex claimed 'Render.render/2 never reads it' — false as of this very wave (closes cch-w29-bl-event-email-scrub-comment-stale); and cloud/DESIGN.md quoted the retired capacity literal as the shipped sentence. Budgets PASS. One cross-slice landmine defused. render_test.exs quoted "Hetzner ran out of server capacity for this size." while the capacity-arm slice retires that literal IN THE SAME WAVE — green apart, RED TOGETHER. The leg now pins the class by derivation and asserts what it actually owes. Proved by an actual merge of both -r branches: 158/0. The three app.js slices were merged the same way: 814/0, smoke 102, cssom-parity PARITY PASS at 1289, __css_check 0 errors. What stalled, and what nobody proved Nothing stalled. All eight round-1 slices are green; there were no deferred rounds this wave, so there is no sequenced-rounds dispatch to chase. The seal predicate's NO-MERGE-BASE corroborator rests on ONE measured corroboration. A register entry on a genuinely disjoint history would degrade to HISTORY-UNAVAILABLE rather than the honest 'not an ancestor'. Fail-closed — it can never become a false PASS — but it is a behavioural claim, and it is this wave's flip-risk row. The byte-identity test skips itself on a checkout with unreadable history, so in a depth-1 CI clone it contributes nothing. The alternative pinned CI to a shape it does not have, which is what redded the roster control. No browser was driven anywhere. The domain re-check's guard reads source order, not behaviour; the refusal panel's ~230-character sentence has never been seen wrapping in a .deploy-row; the usage strip's new glyph was rendered only through the preview smoke. The overflow guard's new term has no COMMITTED fixture that exercises it, because its fail-before requires shipping the defect in CSS. It is protected in CI only in the negative sense — inherent to the leg, not a deferred task. Ledger audit All eight slice tasks: published, claimed, criteria stamped AS THE BUILDERS WORKED (evidence carries run output, not assertions), lifecycle honest, and only the merge-gated criterion open on each — 12/13, 6/7, 9/10, 7/8, 7/8, 7/8, 6/7, 6/7. Several criteria carry the builder's own limitation written INTO the evidence rather than hidden: the seal predicate's full-clone byte-identity substitution, the usage raise not being driven through the gatherer, the domain re-check's source-order guard. That is the behaviour the epic wants. Reviewer ledger fixes: every now-line named the PRE-REVIEW branch (and one said 'not pushed'), so all eight were re-pulsed with the final -r branch, its PR number and the reviewer's fix. One new backlog row filed — cch-w29-bl-safe-url-resolver-seam-unguarded — for the production affordance the new :resolver seam opens. The four rows builders filed were verified published under the epic. No task outside this wave was touched. Grade — A Earned, not given. What is genuinely strong: the discrimination slice is the best instrument work this epic has produced — five probes, a fifth leg nobody asked for that turns out to be the false PASS hiding behind the false FAIL, an exit contract honoured rather than re-litigated, and four REAL clones instead of stubs. The overflow slice's four-part probe is a model of refusing a comfortable non-mutation. Every builder report named its own weakest claim before anyone asked, and two of them argued with their brief and said so. The wish's ratio was not just met but exceeded — five person-facing rows, including two of the epic's purest examples. What falls short: three of the eight shipped a defect of exactly the class the epic exists to close, and a reviewer had to catch them — a cue predicate that could not reach a defect one CSS axis over, a refusal predicate that would have re-cast a progress line as an explained decision, and a recovery control that ate itself on failure. A cross-slice literal collision made two slices green apart and red together, which no builder could see and the wave's own file-fence discipline did not prevent. And nothing in this wave was seen by a human eye in a browser: five person-facing rows shipped on source-order guards and static renders. That is the gap between A and A+. What the next wave should take The D307 guard's promotion. The surface ENUM and the BACKFILL of open rows are what turn the WARN tier hard. The scoping leg is a DESIGN BOUNDARY (46 tests / 1 failure on deletion, not the 23 the criterion predicted) — do not restate it as load-bearing. cch-w22-s7's remainder, still adjudicated against origin/main's bytes rather than rebuilt. D325 stamped the five criteria the tree had already settled. A BROWSER PASS over what this wave shipped. Click the domain re-check; look at the refusal panel's 230-character sentence in a .deploy-row at 320px; look at the amber '?' in the fleet strip. Three of the five person rows have never been seen by an eye. The instrument rows this wave opened: cch-w29-bl-safe-url-resolver-seam-unguarded (a seam nothing stops production from using), the refused-auto-deploy event dispatcher (the toggle must not land ahead of it), the Go CLI usage twin, and task-79aa75e4be7a0067's two remaining stale capacity quotes in router.ex and a Go test comment. Dispatch order: merge round 1 in any order — the eight -r branches are file-disjoint except for app.js (three slices, disjoint regions, merged and proven together at 814/0) and the notifications pair (proven together at 158/0). If anything else adds a CSS rule head before #9460 lands, RE-MEASURE the cssom baseline by running cssom-parity.mjs on the merge; never add up two deltas. An independent second reviewer is owed on #9455 before merge. This workflow spawns exactly one reviewer, so the dispatch is a manual lead step. The judgment to re-derive independently is the NO-MERGE-BASE corroborator: whether 'merge-base found no common ancestor' is genuinely inseparable from 'this store cannot place the commit'. It was measured once, and it decides whether an honest product FAIL can be silently downgraded to an environment excuse. TUI view Email view

reflow200.bodyText: Cloud Console Hardening — wave 29: “I could not look” gets a grammar, and the merge lane stops being someone else’s host Status: SURVEYING. Strategize is closed; 16 Opus surveyors are in flight. Digest appends the survey digest and the verify plan below before any verifier runs; Decide appends the decisions and the wave plan before any builder flies; Review closes this Paper as the debrief. Epic cloud-console-hardening-epic · predecessor wave Paper cloud-console-hardening-wave-28-2026-08-03 · charter .claude/workflows/bp-cloud-console-hardening-charter.md (read from origin/main, not the primary checkout, which is 401 commits behind). The wish Seven numbered instructions. Condensed, with the load-bearing corrections preserved: Finish the discrimination. cch-w28-s2-history-unavailable-discrimination is round 2 and #9356 has landed, so it is unblocked. Teach the git legs to tell rc 1 ("not an ancestor" — an honest answer about the PRODUCT) from rc 128 / missing object / shallow ("I could not look" — an honest answer about the ENVIRONMENT). Its hard constraint is already armed as a tripwire by s1: HISTORY-UNAVAILABLE must surface as a verdict-token LETTER at exit 1, never a process-level exit-2 INFRA-FAULT. The merge lane changed and every earlier brief is stale on this point. Live protection enforces FOUR contexts as of today. Console gate and Cloud gate are BLOCKING, not advisory. Required-check spec drift is GREEN on main for the first time this session. A required gate a third-party host can red is the same defect class as a guard no job runs. Wave 28 s3 documented that the now-REQUIRED Console gate depends on guerrilla.barkpark.cloud being reachable, and nobody fixed it. Tolerable while advisory; an outage on someone else’s host is now a repo-wide merge freeze. The D307 guard’s promotion. The guard is armed at the birth seat (#9405, a723ec0dd); the surface ENUM and the BACKFILL of open rows are what turn the WARN tier hard. The contested scoping criterion was re-measured by the lead: deleting only the scoping leg gives 46 tests / 1 failure, not the 23 the criterion predicted — so the scoping is a DESIGN BOUNDARY, not a load-bearing guard. Do not restate it as load-bearing. The s7 residue, person-facing. A re-check affordance for a TERMINAL unknown domain rail (the poll stops with no way back short of a navigation), plus domainRungChip’s missing unknown arm (task-1daff7bc1bf46ceb). cch-w22-s7’s remainder — finished or closed against origin/main’s bytes rather than rebuilt. .preview-url IS NOT A SLICE and the wish was wrong about it. Wave 28’s smoke killed it; that row reads DONE 10/10. Do not rebuild it. Ratio floor: at least four slices where a PERSON is misinformed or cannot reach a control. The standing test, now six clauses. A fix whose only guard is a sentence is not fixed; a guard no job runs is a sentence with a shebang; a guard that cannot lose is a sentence with an exit code; a guard whose FIXTURE cannot produce the defect is green by construction; a guard whose SELECTOR cannot reach the defect is green by construction even with a cruel fixture; and an instrument POINTED AT THE WRONG ROOT — or reading an object its clone does not have — reports defect-shaped prose for a condition that is only "I could not look". REGISTER NOTHING. Do not touch .github/required-checks.json — it now MATCHES live protection, and any edit re-opens a drift that is finally closed. Ground truth re-derived at Strategize Everything the lead handed down was treated as L6 and re-derived. Four measurements, each with its own command, all taken from a detached worktree at origin/main a723ec0dd — never from the primary checkout, which reads ## main...origin/main [ahead 48, behind 401]. CLAIM COMMAND RESULT Four contexts BLOCK merges gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches/main/protection CONFIRMED — Elixir gate, PR references an active task, Cloud gate, Console gate; enforce_admins: true; identical to the committed spec on context AND app_id (15368). The required Console gate depends on a foreign host BP_SERVER=http://127.0.0.1:1 node --test cloud/priv/static/__preview__/seal-predicate.test.mjs CONFIRMED, and located to one line. 65 tests / 64 pass / not ok 56 — wave 11: --ladder-only reaches the ladder the live refusals never can, failing at seal-predicate.test.mjs:1090 with 2 !== 1: the control demands NO_SEAL(1) and a dead server yields INFRA(2). The reaching line is :1089 — run(['--repo', REPO, '--successor', 'TERMINAL']), a LIVE run whose roster fetch precedes the TERMINAL refusal. That roster read is anonymous curl -G .../v1/data/query/production/task -H "Authorization: Bearer undefined" 200 in 340ms. CI has no BP_TEST-scoped secret and does not need one — the gate is green today purely because guerrilla is up and the roster is world-readable. An ACL change reds it as surely as an outage. The unknown domain rung lies to a screen reader cloud/priv/static/app.js:9598 domainRungChip vs :9500 domainStageRows CONFIRMED, and it is the epic’s exact disease. The pure fold computes an honest unknown role and its 60-line header explains at length why an unmeasured rung must never fall into the waiting bucket. The RENDER has no unknown arm: it falls through to · and state = "waiting", so the aria-label says "waiting" for a check nobody made. The model knows; the screen lies. Premise smoke. Every charter D-number this direction cites was git show-n from origin/main and read for coverage, not existence: D307 (Law 0’s filing half), D325 (the cch-w22-s7 split), D331 (the D307 seat moves to writer.ex, the presence requirement stays unarmed), D334 (Law 0 re-derived; .preview-url cleared 20/20 by measurement; D325’s kill of C9 REFUTED on both its stated reasons). All four exist and all four authorise what they are cited for. Two code sites confirmed present on origin/main: seal-predicate.mjs verifyCommit (the catch that collapses rc 1 and rc 128 into one sentence) and app.js:9598 domainRungChip. Roster at Strategize: 310 children — {done 201, open 73, cancelled 35, considering 1}. The seal predicate’s own denominator (published-only) will read lower; wave 28 quoted roster 307 at 52a80c7be. Both integers get re-derived at Decide. Direction "I could not look" gets a grammar — and the merge lane stops being someone else’s host. Wave 27 found the sentence at the ROOT. Wave 28 found it at the OBJECT and shipped it to two audiences — the instrument and the person. Wave 29’s claim is that the sentence now has three audiences, and that the third one arrived today, uninvited, when branch protection went hard: AUDIENCE THE SENTENCE, POINTED AT IT WHAT IT COSTS TODAY The predicate rc 1 is an honest answer about the PRODUCT; rc 128 / missing object / shallow / no origin/main ref is an honest answer about the ENVIRONMENT. HISTORY-UNAVAILABLE surfaces as a verdict-token LETTER at exit 1. Six verbatim false "not an ancestor" sentences at b=FAIL in any depth-1 clone. Two waves quoted output of that shape as this epic’s primary finding. The merge lane A context that BLOCKS a merge must be a function of the DIFF. It may red for this repo’s bytes and for nothing else — not for a host we do not own, not for history the clone was never given. One line under a REQUIRED gate reaches guerrilla.barkpark.cloud. When that host blinks, every PR in the repo stops merging — not just this epic’s. The person A screen may say "we could not check" or it may say what it measured. It may never spend the product’s vocabulary for a deliberate non-measurement on a measurement that crashed. A crashed usage meter reads unmetered — the same word the flow meters use for "we deliberately do not measure this". An unmeasurable domain rung tells a screen reader "waiting". A resolver blip leaves the rail TERMINAL with no way back short of a navigation. This is not three themes stapled together. It is one sentence that generates all three, which is the shape wave 28 already proved works — "one disease, two audiences", now three. The ratio floor is not a tax on this direction; four of the strongest person rows on the board ARE instances of it. What the finished wave looks like The seal predicate can be run anywhere and never invents a finding. In a full clone it says b=PASS with a byte-identical token. In a pristine git clone --depth 1, a grafted depth-1, and a simulated actions/checkout@v4 PR shape it says HISTORY-UNAVAILABLE with ZERO "is not an ancestor" sentences — at exit 1, as a letter, never as an exit-2 INFRA-FAULT that would red s1’s merged control. And on a full clone with a register entry retargeted to a present-but-genuinely-not-an-ancestor sha it still prints exactly ONE honest product sentence at b=FAIL. The discrimination is proved by clones, not by stubs. No merge-blocking job can reach a host this repo does not own, and something reds if one regains the ability. The predicate’s exit-2 on an unreachable server is CORRECT and stays exactly as it is — the wave does not green a red. What moves is the QUESTION: the live-network assertion leaves the required path for somewhere it can be honestly red without freezing the repo, and a hermetic control just as cruel keeps proving the contrast that test exists to prove. Backed by a ratchet in the console-path-escape-check.sh --selftest family that can lose. Four screens stop reporting a failed measurement as a fact about the product. A meter that crashed says so. An unmeasurable rung says so, in its aria-label as well as its glyph, and offers a re-check instead of a dead end. Copy stops naming a provider it never asked. A publish that silently refused to deploy leaves an event a person can find. The board is shorter and honest about it. cch-w22-s7’s remainder is rebuilt against origin/main’s bytes — including the C9 leg D334 resurrected, whose substantive defect (collecting ws and te but not overflow) has its own model arm 400 lines below it in the same file. What this wave deliberately does not take .preview-url — D334 measured it 20/20 clean from a clean detached worktree, rc 0, worst urlLost −6.44px inside the clipper. The row reads DONE 10/10. Named here so no surveyor re-opens it. Any edit to .github/required-checks.json. REGISTER NOTHING. The spec matches live protection on context and app_id today; Required-check spec drift is green on main for the first time. An edit re-opens a drift that took eleven waves to close. Arming the D307 ABSENT tier. D331 measured the backfill: a description classifier scores 47%, a structured classifier 40%, and a one-line constant return "instruments" scores 73% — both classifiers below the majority baseline, on a three-day-old convention absent from 91% of the live population. A refusal cannot be armed over rows nobody can classify. At most a narrow ENUM question; the survey decides whether even that is a slice. And the scoping leg is a design boundary, not a load-bearing guard — 46 tests / 1 failure, not 23. Direction debate Two rivals were developed far enough to be shippable, then argued against each other. Neither was a straw man; both are what a reasonable strategist would do with this wish. Rival A — SCREENS ONLY Spend the whole wave on person rows. Take s2 because it is mandated and nothing else instrumental. The argument is strong: the epic’s vision sentence is the console stops lying, the ratio floor exists because instrument work keeps crowding out screens, and the board carries at least a dozen live person rows. The finished wave would be six screens a person can actually reach, which is the most legible good this epic produces. Why it loses: it was true yesterday and stopped being true today. All eight round-1 slices are green; there were no deferred rounds this wave, so there is no sequenced-rounds dispatch to chase. The seal predicate's NO-MERGE-BASE corroborator rests on ONE measured corroboration. A register entry on a genuinely disjoint history would degrade to HISTORY-UNAVAILABLE rather than the honest 'not an ancestor'. Fail-closed — it can never become a false PASS — but it is a behavioural claim, and it is this wave's flip-risk row. The byte-identity test skips itself on a checkout with unreadable history, so in a depth-1 CI clone it contributes nothing. The alternative pinned CI to a shape it does not have, which is what redded the roster control. No browser was driven anywhere. The domain re-check's guard reads source order, not behaviour; the refusal panel's ~230-character sentence has never been seen wrapping in a .deploy-row; the usage strip's new glyph was rendered only through the preview smoke. The overflow guard's new term has no COMMITTED fixture that exercises it, because its fail-before requires shipping the defect in CSS. It is protected in CI only in the negative sense — inherent to the leg, not a deferred task. Ledger audit All eight slice tasks: published, claimed, criteria stamped AS THE BUILDERS WORKED (evidence carries run output, not assertions), lifecycle honest, and only the merge-gated criterion open on each — 12/13, 6/7, 9/10, 7/8, 7/8, 7/8, 6/7, 6/7. Several criteria carry the builder's own limitation written INTO the evidence rather than hidden: the seal predicate's full-clone byte-identity substitution, the usage raise not being driven through the gatherer, the domain re-check's source-order guard. That is the behaviour the epic wants. Reviewer ledger fixes: every now-line named the PRE-REVIEW branch (and one said 'not pushed'), so all eight were re-pulsed with the final -r branch, its PR number and the reviewer's fix. The four rows builders filed were verified published under the epic. No task outside this wave was touched. Grade — A Earned, not given. What is genuinely strong: the discrimination slice is the best instrument work this epic has produced — five probes, a fifth leg nobody asked for that turns out to be the false PASS hiding behind the false FAIL, an exit contract honoured rather than re-litigated, and four REAL clones instead of stubs. The overflow slice's four-part probe is a model of refusing a comfortable non-mutation. Every builder report named its own weakest claim before anyone asked, and two of them argued with their brief and said so. The wish's ratio was not just met but exceeded — five person-facing rows, including two of the epic's purest examples. What falls short: three of the eight shipped a defect of exactly the class the epic exists to close, and a reviewer had to catch them — a cue predicate that could not reach a defect one CSS axis over, a refusal predicate that would have re-cast a progress line as an explained decision, and a recovery control that ate itself on failure. A cross-slice literal collision made two slices green apart and red together, which no builder could see and the wave's own file-fence discipline did not prevent. And nothing in this wave was seen by a human eye in a browser: five person-facing rows shipped on source-order guards and static renders. That is the gap between A and A+. What the next wave should take The D307 guard's promotion. The surface ENUM and the BACKFILL of open rows are what turn the WARN tier hard. The scoping leg is a DESIGN BOUNDARY (46 tests / 1 failure on deletion, not the 23 the criterion predicted) — do not restate it as load-bearing. cch-w22-s7's remainder, still adjudicated against origin/main's bytes rather than rebuilt. D325 stamped the five criteria the tree had already settled. A BROWSER PASS over what this wave shipped. Click the domain re-check; look at the refusal panel's 230-character sentence in a .deploy-row at 320px; look at the amber '?' in the fleet strip. Three of the five person rows have never been seen by an eye. The instrument rows this wave opened: cch-w29-bl-safe-url-resolver-seam-unguarded (a seam nothing stops production from using), the refused-auto-deploy event dispatcher (the toggle must not land ahead of it), the Go CLI usage twin, and task-79aa75e4be7a0067's two remaining stale capacity quotes in router.ex and a Go test comment. Dispatch order: merge round 1 in any order — the eight -r branches are file-disjoint except for app.js (three slices, disjoint regions, merged and proven together at 814/0) and the notifications pair (proven together at 158/0). If anything else adds a CSS rule head before #9460 lands, RE-MEASURE the cssom baseline by running cssom-parity.mjs on the merge; never add up two deltas. The judgment to re-derive independently is the NO-MERGE-BASE corroborator: whether 'merge-base found no common ancestor' is genuinely inseparable from 'this store cannot place the commit'. GROUND TRUTH, DERIVED IN-PROCESS at origin/main ab8c86b05 in a detached worktree, never the primary checkout (which is stale at a31faa52d and dirty across eight charters). I ran scripts/pds-door-census.sh myself: rc=0, ERRORS 0, every program disposed. THE HEADLINE THE WISH DID NOT ASK FOR: the census runs in 4.13 s wall / 2.80 s CPU - so it CANNOT have taken the 40.33 s CPU / 68.24 s wall figure it prints. Every price and every disposition-evidence string is a hardcoded literal in PDS_DOOR_PRICES (:146-149) and PDS_DOOR_DISPOSITIONS (:123-137). The CLASS column became an instrument in wave 44. The PRICE column became a shell variable with a date stamp. And the denominator is 20 with 4 doors, not the 19 with 3 that both the wish and the lead notes carry - the census counts itself, and says so at :12-14. What I ran, and what it refuted Eleven consecutive waves have refuted their own dispatch from the artifact. This is the twelfth, and the refutations are load-bearing rather than cosmetic - three of the five figures the brief and the lead notes hand down are contradicted by the instrument on merged main. PREMISE, AS HANDED DOWN RE-DERIVED AT AB8C86B05 CONSEQUENCE "the door count is 3 of 19, not an unmeasured N" (lead notes, emphatic) THE COLUMN prints population 20 (18 .sh + 2 .exs), THROUGH 4 of 20 - pds-door-census.sh, pds-elixir-receipt-census.exs, pds-record-parity.test.sh, pds-status-only-residue.exs The census entered its own denominator by design (:12-14: "a census that hid itself would be the first thing it exists to catch"). 3-of-19 was true before #9380 merged. Do not quote it. "prints a class + a MEASURED PRICE or a named blocker with file:line" (wish item, the wave's whole claim) HALF TRUE. LEDGER AUDIT — three fixes, and one defect the audit itself surfaced Every slice task was claimed before work, stamped mid-claim with real evidence rather than batched at the end, and left in_progress with only the merge-gated row open — with one exception, now fixed. Tasks outside this wave were not touched. pds-w45-criterion-venue sat at lifecycle_status=open while HOLDING a live claim with 7 criteria stamped — a worked, claimed row reading as unstarted on every board. Re-claimed as the reviewer (epoch 9) so the lifecycle matches reality: in_progress, 8/9 met. pds-w45-criterion-venue[4] ("The lead-owned merge-gated row ... is EXPLICITLY EXEMPTED and is left byte-identical") was PROVEN but UNSTAMPED: bp task stamp refuses any --criterion-text containing the substring "merge-gated", so a row that DESCRIBES the gated row is refused as though it WERE one. Re-derived independently (cmp on the two lines: IDENTICAL, 189 bytes; full-file diff one hunk 137a138) and stamped with the override, with that provenance in the evidence. pds-w45-census-row-check-evidence — filed by the sweep builder as follow-up work — was DONE by the reviewer commit on the sweep branch. Claimed, its single criterion stamped with the new row verbatim plus four runs, and left in_progress: it closes when #9441 merges. The stamp-guard defect is NOT newly filed: it duplicates pds-w27-bl-stamp-guard-substring-false-positive (wave 27, still open, root-caused to internal/cli/tasks_stamp_cmd.go). A new task was created, the server flagged the duplicate, and it was DELETED rather than left to double-count the backlog. The recurrence is recorded here instead. Three follow-ups filed BY THE BUILDERS are published children of the epic and honest: pds-w45-argspan-sigil-and-silent-bound (sigil-blind blanking, the silent 40-line bound), task-ac55ff2388510d67 (the ladder's :stale arm is a NO-OP and nothing proves it), pds-w45-census-row-check-evidence (above). GRADE — A WHAT EARNS IT. The wave paid all three items the wish named and paid them in the order the dependencies allow. The second-review debt on #9377 is now discharged BY THE MERGING ARTIFACT rather than by a reviewer's hand mutation — that was the live gap on merged code, and it is the difference between "someone proved it once" and "the repo proves it every run". The ladder slice is the wave's best work: it recognised that its own headline number is evidence of nothing, said so in the printed output, and shipped the only discriminator that exists as a selftest case verified in both directions. The sweep slice reproduced its fail-open with the CORRECT oracle after the criterion named the wrong one, and closed it with the discriminator that was already on the wire. Four of five slices refuted something in their own dispatch by run — the eleventh, twelfth and thirteenth consecutive refutations — and each wrote the correction into the artifact instead of quietly satisfying a figure that does not exist. WHAT KEEPS IT OFF A+. Two of the five needed a reviewer fix to a predicate that had just been tightened, and in both cases the defect was one step past where the builder stopped looking: the first occurrence rather than the only occurrence, the closing line rather than the closing paren. Both slices had green, honest, non-vacuous selftests through the defect. The wave also left three real UNPROVEN arms shipping green by print rather than by mutation — the ladder's :stale filter, arg_span's "every call opening on the line" clause, and its 40-line bound — each filed, none closed, and each is exactly the shape this epic exists to refuse. And every price and timing in this wave is LOCAL: no PDS door has yet run on a foreign runner, so the price column remains an instrument calibrated against one host. NOT A CRITICISM, ON THE RECORD: the wish's item 4 (the unbuilt "?" variable-bound decline) was RULED OUT with a reason, not quietly dropped — PDS-D661 — and the ladder slice printed declined_live=0 as a BOUND on the sentence instead, derived THROUGH lvs_joinable?/1 so the number cannot drift from the predicate it describes. Ruling it out was the right half of "finish it or rule it out". WHAT THE NEXT WAVE TAKES MERGE ORDER FIRST. The five round-1 PRs are file-disjoint except that #9434 and #9441 both touch scripts/pds-door-census.sh — #9434 in the classifier and the selftest, #9441 at line 123 of PDS_DOOR_DISPOSITIONS only — so either order merges without a conflict. Then dispatch the deferred slices STRICTLY in dependency order, re-deriving every anchor at each merged base, because each one moves the file the next one reads. order slice dispatches after why the order is not negotiable 1 pds-w45-census-ledger-integrity #9434 merges Same file; the leg-A repair moves ~180 lines and every anchor in its brief is a line number. 2 pds-w45-price-provenance round 2 merges Built on top of the retire shape and the orphan check; the elided-key design assumes them. 3 pds-w44-hetzner-offline-door rounds 2 AND 3 merge It needs --measure to add its price row and the retire shape to dispose the orphaned ENVIRONMENT row. BOTH LEGS OR NEITHER: the instrument AND its ELIXIR_TEST_ONLY_PATHS entry, or it is #9290/#9292 a third time. THEN WAVE 46'S OWN WORK, in the order the census's printed output ranks it: adjudicate the sweep's 59 unresolved-claim arrivals (the vocabulary is mined from the charter and THIS wave's charter PR moved it again, which is precisely why it could not be done here); price the receipt census's UNMEASURED-LOCAL expensive arm; and either justify or tier pds-ledger-census_test.sh at 40.33 s CPU on a 2-4 vCPU runner rather than shrugging at it. One standing debt outranks all of them for credibility: NO pds door has ever been measured on a foreign runner, so every figure in the price column is a loaded local mac. THE SECOND-REVIEWER DEBT, NAMED RATHER THAN ASSUMED DISCHARGED. #9433 is a HIGH-FLIP-RISK slice on a live grant/tenancy door, and this workflow spawns exactly ONE reviewer — so the independent second pass is a MANUAL LEAD STEP before merge. I re-derived the substitution from source and mutation-proved my own guard, but a genuinely independent pair of eyes on the authorization judgment is still owed. Every PR here also carries an open MERGE-GATED criterion that is the lead's to close on merge: #9433[8], #9434[10], #9438[14], #9441[9], #9442[8].

320.title: PDS wave 45 - the price column learns to expire

390.bodyText: PDS wave 45 - the price column learns to expire STRATEGIZE COMPLETE - the survey fleet is flying. GROUND TRUTH, DERIVED IN-PROCESS at origin/main ab8c86b05 in a detached worktree, never the primary checkout (which is stale at a31faa52d and dirty across eight charters). I ran scripts/pds-door-census.sh myself: rc=0, ERRORS 0, every program disposed. THE HEADLINE THE WISH DID NOT ASK FOR: the census runs in 4.13 s wall / 2.80 s CPU - so it CANNOT have taken the 40.33 s CPU / 68.24 s wall figure it prints. Every price and every disposition-evidence string is a hardcoded literal in PDS_DOOR_PRICES (:146-149) and PDS_DOOR_DISPOSITIONS (:123-137). The CLASS column became an instrument in wave 44. The PRICE column became a shell variable with a date stamp. And the denominator is 20 with 4 doors, not the 19 with 3 that both the wish and the lead notes carry - the census counts itself, and says so at :12-14. What I ran, and what it refuted Eleven consecutive waves have refuted their own dispatch from the artifact. This is the twelfth, and the refutations are load-bearing rather than cosmetic - three of the five figures the brief and the lead notes hand down are contradicted by the instrument on merged main. PREMISE, AS HANDED DOWN RE-DERIVED AT AB8C86B05 CONSEQUENCE "the door count is 3 of 19, not an unmeasured N" (lead notes, emphatic) THE COLUMN prints population 20 (18 .sh + 2 .exs), THROUGH 4 of 20 - pds-door-census.sh, pds-elixir-receipt-census.exs, pds-record-parity.test.sh, pds-status-only-residue.exs The census entered its own denominator by design (:12-14: "a census that hid itself would be the first thing it exists to catch"). 3-of-19 was true before #9380 merged. Do not quote it. "prints a class + a MEASURED PRICE or a named blocker with file:line" (wish item, the wave's whole claim) HALF TRUE. Class is computed: leg A is three mechanical predicates over the tree, leg B is evaluated by EXECUTING elixir-path-escape-check.sh. Price is a string literal. Timed: real 4,13 / user 0,81 / sys 1,99 for the entire run. THE WAVE'S SPINE. A 4-second program cannot have measured a 68-second row. "my 'exactly three refusal reasons' is FIVE by run plus a sixth (HUMAN-GATE)" The VOCABULARY is six (:105-115). The classes actually USED by a row on main are five: ENVIRONMENT (11), PRICE (2), CONTENT-RED (1), RED-BY-DESIGN-REPORTER (1), NOT-YET-BUILT (1). HUMAN-GATE is used by ZERO rows. The correction is right in direction and still not the run's number. A vocabulary entry no row exercises is itself an untested arm. "pds-live-hetzner-placement-group.sh - ENVIRONMENT, needs HCLOUD_TOKEN" (shipped disposition, :128) The CLASS is defensible; the EVIDENCE is about the wrong arm. It cites `--selftest` rc=3. The script's own header at :12-13 and :964 declares `--selftest-offline` "the CREDENTIAL-FREE arm and the CI-able gate". I ran it: rc=0, CPU 1.06+1.09 = 2.15 s at load1 15.44. A LIVE FALSEHOOD-BY-OMISSION in the shipped instrument, and the second-cheapest arm in the whole inventory sitting behind it. "pds-charter-ledger-sweep.sh is CONTENT-RED, rc=1 today" (wish item 3) Confirmed as printed - but the census does not RUN it. The string "by run 2026-08-03 ... rc=1" is a literal at :123. The wish's own slice 3 takes this row to rc=0. The census will keep printing CONTENT-RED. The three blind spots, and why two of them are this wave's own doing The census has exactly one rot check, at :585-602, and it tests EXISTENCE: a ledger row naming a file that is no longer on disk is an error. That catches deletion. It cannot catch the three shapes that actually rot a price column. STALE PRICE. No content hash, no date arithmetic, no re-measurement. pds-record-parity.test.sh will print CPU=4.45s after someone doubles the harness's work, forever, and nothing reds. STALE DISPOSITION EVIDENCE. Five rows cite "by run 2026-08-03: <cmd> rc=N". The census never re-takes any of them. A disposition survives its own repair. ORPHANED DISPOSITION. Read the cond at :519-540: legA=yes AND legB=true short-circuits to THROUGH and the ledger is NEVER consulted. A disposition row for a now-THROUGH instrument is silently unread - not an error, not a warning, not printed. THE COUPLING THAT MAKES THIS THE SPINE RATHER THAN A TANGENT: two of the three deferred slices the wish orders will make the census lie the day they land. pds-w44-hetzner-offline-door puts --selftest-offline through a rider plus ELIXIR_TEST_ONLY_PATHS - legA/legB then compute THROUGH and the ENVIRONMENT row at :128 becomes an unflagged orphan asserting a refusal that is no longer the disposition. pds-w44-charter-sweep-adjudication takes the sweep from rc=1 to rc=0 - and CONTENT-RED, evidenced by a run nobody re-takes, outlives the red it names. Price provenance is a PREREQUISITE for the wish's own item 2, not an addition to it. The direction The epic's law has walked one rung per wave. A receipt lies when the value it emits does not descend from the write return. A class lies when it does not descend from its substitution (wave 42). A gate lies when its green costs nothing to produce (wave 43). Wave 45's sentence is the one the new instrument earns: A PRICE LIES WHEN IT DOES NOT DESCEND FROM A METER THE INSTRUMENT ITSELF DROVE - AND A DISPOSITION LIES WHEN ITS EVIDENCE NAMES A RUN THE INSTRUMENT NEVER RE-TAKES. What the finished wave looks like: ./scripts/pds-door-census.sh still exits 0 on main and still costs seconds - it is a door, and its own 3.32 s row is its own gate cost, so any design that prices it out of its own door is disqualified before it is written. But every number it prints is now either taken by a meter it drove in THIS run, or a cached measurement carrying the content hash of the instrument it prices, so that a changed instrument turns the row PRICE-STALE and reds. A --measure verb takes the measurement and emits the exact ledger row, so re-pricing is one command rather than a hand ritual - the number descends from a meter the instrument drove, and anyone can re-take it. Dispositions whose evidence is a RUN get re-run under an opt-in, threshold-printed tier, so CONTENT-RED cannot survive its own repair. And an orphaned ledger row is an ERROR, because that is the exact shape both of this wave's own slices create. Around that spine, the debts get paid at the new base. Priority order, and the reasoning behind it: # WHAT WHY IT SITS HERE 1 #9377's SHIPPED non-vacuity test is a stub - make it real, then review The only item on this list that is a LIVE GAP ON MERGED CODE. Wave 44's reviewer re-proved the narrowing by hand-mutation; the merging artifact cannot reproduce that proof. A security fix whose non-vacuity cannot be re-run is a stamped receipt that overstates. This outranks the spine on urgency, not on scope. 2 Price provenance, expiry, and orphan detection in pds-door-census.sh The spine. Unblocks slices 4 and 5 from corrupting the instrument. 3 #9380's genuinely independent second review - 37 KB of shell, one pair of eyes D649 declared leg A's three predicates HIGH-FLIP-RISK and named the comment mutation as the oracle. It never got its builder's own review dispatch. 4 pds-w44-hetzner-offline-door - BOTH LEGS OR NEITHER, plus its census row I measured the arm today: rc=0, 2.15 s CPU. The cheapest unclaimed door in the inventory. It also carries the wave's sharpest overlap risk. 5 pds-w44-charter-sweep-adjudication - 45 rulings, and the fail-open at :203 Vocabulary is mined from the charter, which has now landed - and wave 44's own wave-log entry moved it again. Its bp_json(allow_error=True) fail-open is this epic's law broken inside the instrument that enforces it. 6 pds-w44-judgment-coverage-ladder at the new base #9378 shifted every line number. PROVEN-BACKED must be ONE Enum.count over ONE MapSet.union, taken once, never leg_a + leg_b. Its numbers have been dead three times. 7 lv_verdict/5's '?' variable-bound decline - finish properly or rule out with a reason Wave 44 recorded a non-build rather than shipping a cond reorder it could not justify. That was correct. It is still owed a disposition. 8 The criterion-venue rubric fix Cheap, and it prevents a whole class of unmeetable criteria: name the CLAIM, accept any durable venue. The direction debate Three directions were developed far enough to cost something, then argued against each other. Rival A - pay the debts, period Do exactly the wish's items 1 through 5: three deferred slices, two owed reviews, the lv_verdict half, the criterion lesson. Do not touch the census - it exits 0, wave 44 declared it done, and reopening it is a fifth wave of arguing about a column. This is the disciplined reading of the brief and it has a real claim on the wave. WHY IT LOSES: it hands the wave a false floor. Two of its own three slices silently corrupt the instrument, so "pay the debts" manufactures the next wave's finding. And it violates the mandate the user restates every single wave - DERIVE, NEVER TRANSCRIBE, INCLUDING FROM THIS BRIEF - by inheriting "the price column is an instrument now" as a premise instead of running it. I ran it. It is half an instrument, and the half that is prose is the half the column is named after. Rival B - measure every price, every run The pure fix: no cache, no ledger, no staleness possible. The census drives the meter for every row on every invocation and the price column is a measurement by construction. WHY IT LOSES, on the epic's own evidence: D648 proved wall is not a property of a door on a shared host - a fixed workload's wall spanned 5.8x at constant load while its user CPU spanned 27 percent. A re-measuring census becomes the most expensive program in its own denominator: 40.33 s for pds-ledger-census_test.sh alone, plus the receipt census whose expensive arm D646 showed conceals ~140 s minimum from any outer meter. It would also have to price ITSELF - a fixpoint. Worst of all it converts a 4 s door into an ungateable one, killing the census's own THROUGH row, which is the single most self-defeating outcome available to this wave. The honest design is not "always measure" but "never assert a measurement you cannot re-take, and know when it expired." Rival C - spend the column, gate the cheap doors Take the census output at face value and do the obvious thing the wish's title demands - SPEND IT. Put every affordable row through the required gate: hetzner offline at 2.15 s, pds-record-parity.test.sh at 4.45 s, pds-scratch-target_test.sh at 8.91 s. Maximum visible progress, and it is exactly what four waves of arguing were FOR. WHY IT LOSES AS A WHOLE DIRECTION, and why it is absorbed as a part: gating on unverified prices is D633's sin at one remove. pds-scratch-target_test.sh's own shipped row says "Hermeticity on a runner WITHOUT local Postgres is unproven here" - gating it is a day-one red on a foreign runner, the identical trap wave 44 documented for sheet-grid-js.yml. Rival C survives as exactly ONE new door: the one whose price and green I measured myself today. Why the winner won The spine plus the debts, with hetzner-offline as the one new door, is the only direction in which the wish's own item 2 does not manufacture the next wave's finding. It applies the epic's law to the epic's newest artifact, which is what every wave of this epic has actually been about. And it converts "spend the column" from a slogan into something that is safe to do more than once. The sharpest attack on the winner, and how the wave absorbs it THE ATTACK: "You are reopening a slice that shipped 11/12 with run evidence and rc=0 on main, on a distinction - 'measured' versus 'cached with provenance' - that is philosophy, not a defect. Nobody is harmed by a three-day-old CPU figure. This is the fifth consecutive wave arguing about a column, which is precisely what wave 44 ended." That attack has real force, and the wave absorbs it by refusing to argue and making it a RUN. The spine ships only if the verify round can demonstrate, by mutation against a real tree, a case where the shipped census prints a number or a class the tree contradicts. I already hold one candidate - the hetzner row's wrong-arm evidence - and this wave's own slices manufacture two more. IF THE VERIFIERS CANNOT MAKE THE SHIPPED CENSUS PRINT A FALSEHOOD AGAINST A REAL TREE, THE SPINE IS CUT AND THIS WAVE BECOMES RIVAL A. That is the fail-before condition, declared before the fleet flies, and it is the honest version of "derive, never transcribe" turned on my own direction. Second-order absorption, as a criterion rather than a hope: the design must not balloon the census's own price. A content hash per row is one shasum across 20 files - milliseconds. Re-running cheap dispositions is opt-in and threshold-printed, never on --check's default path. Standing hazards this wave carries THE FORMATTER VERSION TRAP, newly measured in wave 44: CI pins Elixir 1.18.1; this host runs 1.19.5. #9380 reddened Format while mix format --check-formatted exited 0 locally on the SAME commit. Apply CI's own suggested output verbatim and verify BOTH formatters accept it, or the red only moves. OVERLAP RISK, declared: #9380 now owns scripts/elixir-path-escape-check.sh and the hetzner slice edits the same declared set. Cloud Console wave 28 runs concurrently and owns .github/workflows/**. Coordinate before touching either. BOTH LEGS OR NEITHER on the hetzner slice - the instrument AND its ELIXIR_TEST_ONLY_PATHS entry, or it is wave 42's #9290/#9292 a third time. The primary checkout is stale at a31faa52d and dirty across eight charter files. Read the charter via git show origin/main:<path>; build in worktrees only. A slice PR citing a D-number must not merge before the charter PR that defines it - the D643 rule, bought at the cost of 13 shipped citations pointing at decisions main did not define. PUSH EARLY AND OPEN THE PR ON THE FIRST GREEN COMMIT. Wave 43 lost four branches because nothing was pushed until review, and review never ran. The survey plan Fifteen Opus surveyors at medium effort. Width now buys precision later: every load-bearing assumption in the direction above is a question below, and the first three are aimed squarely at the spine's own fail-before condition. KEY QUESTION WHY IT CHANGES THE PLAN price-provenance-audit Re-derive independently whether pds-door-census.sh MEASURES or QUOTES its prices. Time the full run; trace every value in THE COLUMN back to either a computation or a literal at scripts/pds-door-census.sh:123-149. Which columns are computed, which are quoted? This is the wave's spine. If any price is genuinely re-measured the direction narrows sharply. census-rot-mutation Mutation-prove the three claimed blind spots against a real tree: (a) change a priced instrument's bytes and show the price still prints; (b) repair a CONTENT-RED row's cause and show CONTENT-RED still prints; (c) make a disposed instrument satisfy legA+legB and show its disposition row goes silently unread. Which actually fire? THE FAIL-BEFORE. If none of the three can be made to print a falsehood, the spine is CUT. hetzner-offline-door Verify --selftest-offline is genuinely credential-free and hermetic (env -i, no network, no HCLOUD_*), re-measure its CPU, and map EXACTLY what the rider plus ELIXIR_TEST_ONLY_PATHS entry must contain. What does the census then print for that row, and does the ENVIRONMENT disposition become an orphan? Door number five and the live orphan demonstration in one slice. 9377-stub-nonvacuity Read api/test/barkpark_web/live/studio/pds_w44_grant_door_test.exs in full. Which case is the non-vacuity or mutation proof, and is it a stub? What would a REAL one assert, and does shared/paper.ex's narrowing survive an independent re-derivation from source? A live gap on merged security code - the highest-urgency item in the wave. 9380-independent-review Genuinely independent review of pds-door-census.sh's leg A: do the three predicates admit a fraudulent THROUGH? Run D649's comment mutation as the oracle. Also audit the --selftest fixture tree and whether the E1-E4 execution encodings are all covered. The second owed review; D649 declared it HIGH-FLIP-RISK. charter-sweep-adjudication Map scripts/pds-charter-ledger-sweep.sh and pds-charter-ledger-adjudication.md: how many unresolved-claim arrivals against the CURRENT charter blob (D652 said 45), what the adjudication row format is, and the exact shape of the fail-open at :203 with bp_json allow_error=True. Slice five's scope and its own law-breach; the count moved once already. judgment-coverage-ladder Re-derive the ladder's anchors in scripts/pds-elixir-receipt-census.exs at the post-#9378 base. Where does PROVEN-BACKED belong, what are leg A and leg B, and why is the disposition sum near :4033 NOT a safe model for it? Slice six. Its numbers have been dead three times; every line number shifted. lv-verdict-unresolved-arm Read lv_verdict/5 at census.exs:4766 and lv_chain_verdict. Is the '?' variable-bound decline reachable through the residual? Wave 44 confirmed from source that the arm ordering does not admit the specified reorder - is there a semantically-honest route, or is the right answer a recorded rule-out? Item four. Finish properly or rule out with a reason - both are acceptable outcomes. receipt-census-unmeasured pds-elixir-receipt-census.exs is THROUGH but UNMEASURED-LOCAL. What IS the gated arm's real price (the rider, not --selftest), and can it be measured without hitting D646's fan-out blindness? Wish item three's first honest gap; determines whether a price is even obtainable. ledger-census-tiering Justify or refuse pds-ledger-census_test.sh at 40.33 s CPU and 68.24 s wall on a 2-4 vCPU runner. Re-measure. What are its 144 checks, is it decomposable into a cheap arm and an expensive one, and is the D647 figure reproducible? Wish item three's second gap; a shrug is explicitly not acceptable. scratch-target-hermeticity pds-scratch-target_test.sh is PRICE at 8.91 s with hermeticity unproven without local Postgres. Prove or refute hermeticity on a Postgres-free environment. Is it a further candidate door or a genuine PRICE refusal? The third PRICE row, unexamined by the brief - either a cheap win or a documented refusal. gate-plumbing-and-formatter Map elixir.yml's required legs, ELIXIR_TEST_ONLY_PATHS and ELIXIR_COMPILE_PATHS semantics, and reproduce the 1.18.1-vs-1.19.5 formatter divergence. What is the exact procedure that satisfies BOTH formatters? Every slice touching a rider crosses this; wave 44 lost time to it twice. prior-art-sweep Search bp papers and tasks, and the epic tree under task-2ac1f95237c4a8e5, for prior art on price staleness, ledger expiry, content-hash freshness, and orphaned allowlist rows - anywhere in this repo, not only PDS. Has any of this been built and stranded? D645's lesson: git-based greps structurally cannot see stranded work. Check the ledger too. criterion-venue-rubric Find where slice criteria are authored (the cycle skill, the task-authoring rubric, prior wave criteria). Which shipped criteria presume a PR body, a push, or any workflow the builders do not have? Propose the venue-neutral phrasing. Item five - and it is cheap to build in only if the authoring surface is actually locatable. concurrency-and-fences What is actually in flight right now - open PRs, foreign claims on the epic tree, live worktrees, and Cloud Console wave 28's fence? Where exactly do scripts/pds-*, elixir-path-escape-check.sh and .github/workflows/** collide? The concurrent-session dup hazard, plus the declared overlap on the hetzner slice's file. Where the wave stands STRATEGIZE COMPLETE. Fifteen surveyors flying. This Paper is the wave's living story: Digest appends the survey digest and the verify plan before the verifiers fly; Decide appends the decisions and the wave plan before the builders fly; Review closes it as the debrief. Epic task: task-2ac1f95237c4a8e5. Deferred slices this wave inherits: pds-w44-judgment-coverage-ladder, pds-w44-hetzner-offline-door, pds-w44-charter-sweep-adjudication, pds-w44-lv-verdict-unresolved-spec-arm. Owed reviews: #9377 (b83501922) and #9380 (ab8c86b05). Slice task ids are filed at Decide and named here when they exist. Survey digest - 15 reports, and the fail-before is already satisfied DIGEST COMPLETE. The wave's declared FAIL-BEFORE - 'if the verify round cannot make the shipped census print a falsehood against a real tree, the spine is CUT' - was satisfied TWICE during the SURVEY, independently, by two agents who did not talk to each other. price-provenance-audit replaced the 610-line scripts/pds-record-parity.test.sh with a two-line 'exit 0' and the BYTE-IDENTICAL shipped census still printed 'THROUGH CPU=1.45+3.00=4.45s ...
