390.title: Cloud Console Hardening — wave 28: the instrument fixed “I could not look” at the root and left it standing at the object

desktop.bodyText: Cloud Console Hardening — wave 28: the instrument fixed “I could not look” at the ROOT and left it standing at the OBJECT — and the environment it runs in is the one place it cannot look Wave 27 was the best-argued wave this epic has run. It refuted both of the lead's headline findings, paid Standing Law 0 by hand with 57 re-parented rows, and proved that the instrument certifying this epic's health was manufacturing false defect reports out of a directory it could not read. Five of its six person-facing slices are on main. One PR is open — #9356 — and it is the one everything else reads through. The lead offered this wave a binary: (a) give the CI job the history the instrument needs, or (b) restructure the red control to assert clause (a) alone. Both are defensible. Both are also incomplete, and this Paper's headline finding is why: measured live, in this session, the WAVE-27-FIXED predicate — the one on #9356, with both of its new refusals armed — still emits six verbatim “commit … is not an ancestor of origin/main” sentences inside a shallow clone. Same disease, same prose, one condition over, in the exact environment the instrument runs in automatically. The wish, and what is already true about each item # THE WISH MEASURED ON ORIGIN/MAIN DFDC31DB9, 2026-08-03T12:35Z 1 #9356 is red because console-harness.yml checks out at fetch-depth:1; decide (a) fetch-depth:0 or (b) restructure the control CONFIRMED and ENLARGED. Depth-1 clone of this repo: origin/main RESOLVES as a ref, but every registered commit is rc 128 “Not a valid object name”. The #9356 predicate passes BOTH of its new refusal legs there and prints six false ancestry sentences at b=FAIL. The binary is false — the fix is the DISCRIMINATION, and it makes both (a) and (b) correct rather than either being a workaround. 2 the D307 door guard is now a wave, not a slice; budget for a `surface` ENUM and a BACKFILL CONFIRMED as filed: cchi-w27-bl-d307-create-time-door-guard, open, 0/5, parent cch-instruments-epic, files [api/lib/barkpark/content/mutations.ex]. apply_mutations is public (mutations.ex:31) and reachable non-admin through MutateController → POST /v1/data/mutate/:dataset (router.ex:2322). The BACKFILL is a ledger write, not code — wave 27 proved the lead's hands are the right instrument for that class. 3 re-derive orphans with the fixed instrument, from a real git tree, quoting UTC stamp + tree sha + RESOLVED ROOT DONE, in this Paper. 2026-08-03T12:35:45Z · tree dfdc31db96b85b66515a1cba3f92a9e9bd81b09b · root <scratchpad>/wt-w28 → NO-SEAL a=FAIL b=PASS c=PASS orphans=57 considering=1 residue=60 (live 59). Wave 27's debrief read 62; five rows have left since. 4 person-facing residue: .preview-url deploy-row siblings; the desktop band; the render-path bypass remainder ONE PREMISE FAILS SMOKE. `.preview-url` is a DOM CHILD of `.deploy-ref` (app.js:10289 emits `<div class="deploy-ref">branch → <a class="preview-url mono">`), and #9357 landed `.deploy-ref { overflow-wrap: anywhere }` at app.css:1847 — whose own committed comment at :1841-1843 says it covers `.preview-url` inside it by inheritance. The next silent clip is NOT there. The desktop band is D323, a measured negative, correctly closed. 5 cch-w22-s7 was split and five criteria stamped by D325; finish or close the remainder against origin/main's bytes D325 is explicit: stamp C6/C7/C8/C12/C14, DROP C9 (its symbol `cuePaints` has zero occurrences under cloud/ and its second anchor file does not exist), close C15/C16 `n/a — split`. This is a LEDGER action for the lead at Decide, not a builder slice. `bp task get cch-w22-s7` returns nothing under that id — resolving the real id is survey work. THE FINDING: wave 27 named the shallow clone in its own fix's header comment, and did not close it seal-predicate.mjs:453 is one line: `try { execFileSync('git', ['-C', REPO, 'merge-base', '--is-ancestor', commit, 'origin/main'], …); } catch { problems.push(`commit ${commit} is not an ancestor of origin/main`); }`. The catch is unconditional. Charter D318 enumerated exactly what it swallows — “not-a-git-repo / no-origin-main / shallow-clone / unknown-sha” — and wave 27's fix closed the first two and wrote the other two into a comment. The wave-27 header comment says it out loud, verbatim: “the ancestry `catch` at the top of `verifyCommit` swallows not-a-git-repo, no origin/main, a shallow clone and an unknown sha into one identical claim about the PRODUCT.” The remedy that follows checks that `.github/workflows/cloud.yml` exists and that `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` resolves to REPO. A depth-1 CI clone satisfies both. Measured live in this session, controlled pair, same live ledger, same minute, nothing varied but the clone: CLONE GIT STATE PREDICATE RESULT full worktree at origin/main not shallow, all objects present origin/main's (pre-#9356) rc 1 · NO-SEAL a=FAIL b=PASS c=PASS orphans=57 `git clone --depth 1` of the same repo is-shallow-repository = true; origin/main RESOLVES; `merge-base --is-ancestor a78fd4e8c origin/main` → rc 128 `fatal: Not a valid object name` #9356's FIXED predicate, both new refusals armed rc 1 · NO-SEAL a=FAIL b=FAIL c=PASS · SIX false “commit … is not an ancestor of origin/main” sentences The instrument that certifies this epic reports “I could not look” as “I found a defect” — the exact sin wave 27 fixed — in the one environment where it runs without a human present. That is not a test failure. It is the sixth standing-test clause, live, on the very instrument that authored it. THE DIRECTION: one disease, two audiences — the console and its instrument both stop asserting what they did not measure This wave has one sentence and it points in both directions at once. A system that could not determine something must say so. It must not substitute a plausible guess, a default, or the negative branch of a two-way test it was unable to run. Pointed at the INSTRUMENT, that sentence resolves the lead's binary by refusing it. Option (a) alone leaves the predicate lying in every other shallow environment — a container, a fork PR, an agent's `--depth 1`, any future job. Option (b) alone leaves standing the fact the lead correctly identified as bigger than the test: that every seal run under this workflow is structurally unable to evaluate clause (b). The answer that pays both is the DISCRIMINATION: teach the git legs to tell rc 1 (“not an ancestor”, an honest answer about the product) from rc 128 / missing object / shallow repository (“I could not look”, an honest answer about the environment). Once the predicate can tell those apart, (b) becomes the correct shape for the control — it asserts the floor it is actually about — and (a) becomes a verified environment declaration rather than a workaround, because a regression back to depth-1 would then produce an honest INFRA-FAULT the job can assert on. Pointed at the PERSON, the same sentence is already sitting in the ledger as open rows. A refused connection is reported as “A network step timed out. Retry usually fixes this.” — the console did not classify the failure, so it guessed, and the guess carries ADVICE. A person switches on “Deployment failed” alerts across email and every chat channel, and the event has zero producers anywhere in the repository — the console tells them they are subscribed to something that cannot arrive. These are not clipping bugs. They are the epic's founding vision, in its purest form, and they are the wave's person bodies. What the finished wave looks like #9356 is MERGED, first and alone, and it merged because its control was restructured to assert clause (a) — the floor it exists to test — not because anything red was weakened. Nothing about the depth-1 environment changed to get it green. The seal predicate has a THIRD refusal in the same discipline as its first two: HISTORY-UNAVAILABLE. Run it in a shallow clone and it exits 2 with a named code and zero invented findings, exactly as it now does in a git-archive extraction. Mutation-proved with a REAL `git clone --depth 1`, not a stub — the wave-27 lesson is that stubbing the leg only moves the failure. console-harness.yml stops being an environment the instrument cannot work in. The seal job declares the history it needs, and a self-check reds if that declaration silently reverts — a guard on the guard's environment, which is the class of defect this whole wave is about. The D307 door guard is ARMED, not ruled on for a third wave. `surface` becomes an enum; the open rows are backfilled BY THE LEAD'S HAND at Decide (wave 27 proved that pattern with 57 re-parents); the fence widening is a numbered charter decision written before a builder touches mutations.ex; and the refusal is scoped to this epic's parent_id so its blast radius is this epic, not the whole task system. At least four — target five — slices where a PERSON is misinformed or cannot reach a control, led by the two rows where the console gives a confident wrong answer to a question it never asked. What this wave deliberately does NOT do It does not spend a slice on `.preview-url`. That premise failed smoke: #9357 already covers it by inheritance and the committed CSS comment says so. Booking it would be paying twice for one fix. It does not chase orphans to zero. 57 is stated with all three provenance facts and repaid only by rows that leave honestly. Wave 27 already made the largest Law-0 payment in the epic's history; a wave spent on ledger hygiene is the disease the charter names at waves 9/10/11. It does not touch .github/required-checks.json, and it registers nothing. The direction debate: three candidates, argued, one committed Rival A — “Finish the instrument, build the door” (the wish read literally) Take the lead's binary, pick one leg, and spend the rest of the wave on the D307 door guard as a full multi-slice build: the `surface` enum, the backfill, the fence ruling, the refusal, the mutation proof. Clean, obedient, and it retires the highest-leverage row in the epic. WHY IT LOSES. Three counts. First, arithmetic: four instrument slices against a floor of four person bodies means eight slices minimum, and this epic's own history says a wave that spends 4-of-6 on instruments moves the row count the wrong way (waves 9/10/11: +11, +16, +7). Second, the door guard's dependency chain — enum → backfill → fence ruling → refusal — is SERIAL and cannot fan out to parallel builders, so it converts a fan-out wave into a queue. Third and worst, it accepts the false binary. Picking (a) or (b) at speed leaves the predicate lying in every shallow environment that is not this one workflow, and this Paper has now proved live that such an environment exists and that the epic's own instrument is in it. Rival B — “Pay Law 0 to zero and drive at the seal” orphans is 57 and a=FAIL is the only clause failing. Spend the wave closing, forwarding and adjudicating residue — including the cch-w22-s7 split D325 already ruled — and get the epic within sight of an honest SEAL. WHY IT LOSES. It is the epic's stated disease wearing a productivity costume. The charter's vision is that the CONSOLE stops lying; a wave with zero person bodies fails the ratio outright and would be the fourth restatement of a law rather than a payment of it. It also mistakes the seal for the goal — D318 proved the predicate could SEAL an epic that does not exist, which means a falling orphan count was never the thing worth optimising. HARVESTED ANYWAY: this Paper quotes the reading with all three provenance facts, and the cch-w22-s7 adjudication is booked as a Decide-phase ledger action for the lead, costing zero builders. Rival C — “One disease, two audiences” — COMMITTED Two instrument slices that pay the environment question properly plus the discrimination that generalises it; one door-guard slice made buildable by moving its backfill dependency onto the lead's hands at Decide; and four-to-five person bodies chosen so that at least two of them are literally the same defect the instrument has — a system asserting a fact it did not measure. WHY IT WINS. It is the only candidate where the instrument work and the person work are the SAME argument, which means the wave's finding transfers: the sentence that fixes the seal predicate is the sentence a builder applies to `connection refused`. It keeps the ratio at four-plus without inventing filler. It refuses the lead's binary on evidence rather than on preference — the depth-1 run is measured, not reasoned. And it ships the door guard ARMED this wave by removing the dependency that blocked it, rather than ruling on it for a third consecutive wave. The sharpest attack on the winner, and how the wave absorbs it “You are deferring the D307 door guard AGAIN. Wave 26 ruled on it, wave 27 filed it, and ‘build the enum, defer the refusal’ is exactly the shape that lets wave 29 defer it a fourth time. Meanwhile you have talked yourself into a THIRD instrument slice nobody asked for.” TAKEN, and it changes the plan rather than being argued away. The wave does not ship the enum and defer the refusal — it ships the refusal ARMED, and it removes the blocker by re-classifying it. D324 gave four honest reasons the guard could not ship: (i) no classifier, (ii) the fence widening is not a builder's call, (iii) CI is post-hoc detection not refusal, (iv) shipping before the backfill makes the guard's first act on main a refusal of legitimate filings. Reasons (i) and (iv) are LEDGER work, and wave 27 proved conclusively that ledger work belongs to the lead's hands at Decide — 57 re-parents, executed in minutes, with the post-condition asserted on the destination roster. Reason (ii) is a numbered charter decision, which is also a Decide-phase artifact. Reason (iii) argues FOR the door, not against it. So the builder's slice is what remains: the enum validation and the refusal, scoped to one parent_id, with a mutation proof that shows it can both refuse and pass. If survey finds the backfill is larger or messier than wave 27's re-parent — a real risk, since `surface` is populated on 24 of 343 rows and is free prose — the wave scopes the guard's population to rows the backfill actually reached and says so, rather than arming a refusal over rows it cannot classify. On the third instrument slice: it is not a third, it is the CORRECT first. Without the discrimination, both of the lead's options are workarounds, and this Paper has the run output proving it. The wave's own ratio discipline still binds — if the discrimination and the environment declaration cannot be shown to be one coherent slice at Decide, the environment half merges with #9356 and the wave spends the recovered budget on a fifth person body. Premise smoke — every inherited premise this direction leans on, run rather than quoted PREMISE (SOURCE) THE CHECK THAT WAS RUN RESULT Wave 27's five slices are on main; only #9356 is open (lead notes, L6) `git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> origin/main` for all six named shas; `gh pr view 9356` CONFIRMED. a78fd4e8c, c4a359d0c, 713795305, 7c8fa229a, 271d4a244, dfdc31db9 all ancestors. #9356 OPEN; `Console gate` and `Console client unit harness` both FAILURE. console-harness.yml checks out at fetch-depth 1 (wish item 1) `git show origin/main:.github/workflows/console-harness.yml` CONFIRMED for console-unit (bare `actions/checkout@v4`, v4's default depth is 1). NUANCE the wish does not carry: the `changes` job at :104 DOES set fetch-depth: 0, so the file already contains the remedy pattern for a different job. A depth-1 clone “has neither origin/main nor those commits” (wish item 1) `git clone --depth 1`; `git branch -r`; `git merge-base --is-ancestor a78fd4e8c origin/main` HALF REFUTED, and the half that fails matters. origin/main DOES exist as a ref in a depth-1 clone. Only the OBJECTS are missing (rc 128 `Not a valid object name`). A remedy that checks “does origin/main resolve?” would therefore pass and change nothing. #9356's fix closes the wrong-root class (D318, wave 27) Copied #9356's predicate into the depth-1 clone and ran it live CONFIRMED for the ROOT class and REFUTED as a general fix. Both new refusal legs PASS in a shallow clone; six false ancestry sentences print anyway. b=FAIL from a clone, b=PASS from a full tree, same ledger, same minute. `.preview-url` is the next silent clip (wish item 4) `git show origin/main:cloud/priv/static/app.css | grep`; `app.js` previewRow FAILS SMOKE — a FINDING, not a foundation. app.css:1847 `.deploy-ref { … overflow-wrap: anywhere }` (landed #9357) and app.js emits `.preview-url` INSIDE `.deploy-ref`. The committed comment at :1841-1843 states the inheritance explicitly. Already paid. The D307 door guard's target is reachable through a real non-admin write path `git grep apply_mutations`; router.ex route table CONFIRMED. `Content.apply_mutations/3` is public at mutations.ex:31; callers are MutateController (POST /v1/data/mutate/:dataset, router.ex:2322), Sync.Applier and papers/value_writeback. Not an admin-only path. mutations.ex:470-545 already hosts a create-time door guard, so the pattern exists in-file. cch-w26-bl-deploy-row-siblings-unwrapped is residue `bp task get` REFUTED. It is DONE at 10/10 — that IS #9357. The residual row the wish is reaching for does not exist under that id. Every code site the direction names still exists on origin/main `git cat-file -e origin/main:<path>` × 9 ALL PRESENT: mutations.ex, sites/deploy.ex, app.js, app.css, scenarios.mjs, overflow-guard.mjs, console-harness.yml, and both wave-27 ledger recipes under tooling/grip/ledger/. Charter D-numbers this direction cites (D307, D317, D318, D319, D321, D322, D324, D325) exist AND cover what they are cited for `git show origin/main:.claude/workflows/…charter.md`, read verbatim ALL PRESENT AND COVERING. D324 in particular authorises exactly the four-reason deferral this direction dismantles, and names `surface` at 24/343 free prose — the number the direction budgets against. Two premises failed smoke and both are stated rather than dropped: `.preview-url` is already paid, and “a depth-1 clone has no origin/main” is false in the half that would have shaped the remedy. One premise was ENLARGED: the wrong-root fix does not generalise, and the proof is a live run rather than an argument. The shape the wave is aiming at — seven named, five expected Tentative. Decide finalises after two exploration rounds; survey may kill any of these and is expected to promote at least one replacement on its own evidence, as wave 27's flick-to-bottom and progressbar bodies were. # CANDIDATE CLASS NOTE 1 #9356 unhostaged — the empty-roster control asserts CLAUSE (a), not the overall verdict instrument Merges FIRST and ALONE. Nothing red is weakened; the control stops being hostage to clauses it does not test. 2 HISTORY-UNAVAILABLE — the git legs tell “not an ancestor” from “I could not look”, mutation-proved in a real `--depth 1` clone instrument The crown. Generalises wave 27's fix to the condition its own comment names. 3 The seal job's environment is DECLARED and its regression is detectable instrument May merge into #2 at Decide if they are one coherent change; the wave's ratio recovers a slice if so. 4 A refused connection stops being reported as a timeout with retry advice PERSON `cch-w27-bl-connection-refused-classified-as-timeout`, open, 0/4. If s4's guard cannot be shown to REFUSE and to PASS over HTTP, and to leave the two D53 pinning tests green ONLY because of its parent scoping, then the door was never armed. And if s7's `unknown` does not set terminal:true in the shipped app.js, the console keeps polling a dead resolver forever and the person is no better off than before -- a server-only fix here is a regression wearing a decision's clothes. DEBRIEF — the wave as it will merge, and the grade it earned Seven round-1 slices were briefed, seven were built, seven are green, and all seven are PUSHED with a PR open — six new PRs (#9404-#9409) plus #9356, whose head was fast-forwarded to carry cch-w28-s1 so the fix rides the PR it was written for rather than duplicating it. cch-w28-s2 is round 2 by design and correctly sits `open` on the ledger. The reviewer re-ran every slice gate on the FINAL branch, fixed four things in place rather than reporting them, and proved the wave coheres by merging all seven onto origin/main in one probe branch: the FULL cloud suite is 2693 tests / 0 failures there, and __app.test.mjs is 797/797. No fixes needed. The four things the reviewer FIXED rather than reported 1. THE FALSE SENTENCE IN THE D307 GUARD'S HEADER (commit 73438f573). The shipped comment claimed that deleting the scoping arm takes mutate_controller_test.exs “from 36/36 to 23 failures, including the D53 create-family pins”. The builder had already measured 1 failure and stamped an honest --miss on the criterion — but left the brief's number standing in the code. Re-run independently at review (delete `not cch_epic_child?(parent) -> :ok`, change nothing else): 46 tests / 1 failure, and that failure is this slice's own scoping test. The comment now states the measured result and says plainly that the scoping is a DESIGN boundary, not a load-bearing leg under today's corpus. An epic whose thesis is “stop asserting what you did not measure” cannot ship a header comment that does exactly that. 2. `:nxdomain` IS AN ANSWER, NOT A FAULT (commits 90ab9999a + 438495a96) — a REVIEW DECISION superseding the letter of D332. The s7 builder built D332 as written, measured that one fifth of it was wrong, and filed task-3fbfff8c97b50c8f at priority 0 rather than quietly re-deciding. He was right on both counts. Re-measured at review on this host: `:inet.getaddrs` of a non-existent name returns `{:error, :nxdomain}` on BOTH families — which is precisely what a freshly attached, still-propagating domain looks like through the real transport. Shipped literally, D332 would have turned the MOST COMMON waiting state into “we could not check” and stripped its propagation advice: one lie swapped for another, in the very rung the slice existed to make honest. NXDOMAIN means the resolver ANSWERED. Fixed with `@answered_empty [:nxdomain]`, and — the half that matters for the standing test — the DNS test fakes now RETURN nxdomain for a missing record instead of `{:ok, []}`, a shape production never produces. task-3fbfff8c97b50c8f is closed with the ruling, its measurement and its residual gap on the record. 3. THE REAP ALERT CAP IS NOW DRIVEN (commit ab2a6dce5). `@reap_alert_cap 25` decides that the 26th owner in a cluster incident hears nothing by email — a person-facing SUPPRESSION that no fixture crossed. The builder flagged it against himself; the review paid it: a test fails 27 deployments in one sweep and asserts exactly 25 emails plus the suppression log line, with `Registry.reap_alert_cap/0` exposed so the test reads the real constant instead of a copy. Mutation-proved: replacing `Enum.split(alerts, @reap_alert_cap)` with `{alerts, []}` reds exactly that test and nothing else. 4. THE MUTATION ANCHORS IN s1's CONTROL (commit 52a80c7be). `String.prototype.replace` on an anchor that has drifted is a SILENT no-op, and `mutatedRun`'s own `notEqual(out, src)` guard would have been satisfied by the roster mutation alone — so a future refactor of seal-predicate.mjs could have left the floor mutation un-applied and the control passing vacuously. Each anchor is now asserted present before use. Orphans, re-derived with the fixed instrument from a real git tree All three things the wish demanded are quoted, not paraphrased. UTC 2026-08-03T14:43:51Z · tree sha 52a80c7be · RESOLVED REPO ROOT /Volumes/SATECHI/github/barkpark/.claude/worktrees/wf_e660e3b7-480-40. VERDICT-TOKEN: SEAL-PREDICATE NO-SEAL a=FAIL b=PASS c=PASS orphans=75 considering=1 successor=cch-instruments-epic epic=cloud-console-hardening-epic mode=live stubbed=0 waived=0 roster=307 head=52a80c7be Roster 307 {done 195, in_progress 7, open 70, cancelled 34, considering 1}. Residue 78 (live 77, considering 1); forwarded under the successor 0; the three permanent human gates all resolve in-roster. b=PASS here because this is a FULL clone. That is the wave's whole finding restated: the same predicate under console-harness.yml still cannot evaluate clause (b) at all, and nothing in CI has changed about that. D306's two integers, as deltas against wave 27's 117 / roster 343 {189, 119, 34, 1} at c2affd445 — RE-PARENTED OUT OF THIS ROSTER = 36 (343 → 307), CLOSED = +6 done (189 → 195). The 36 does not equal wave 27's 57 hand re-parents, and the reconciliation is stated rather than smoothed: 343 − 57 = 286, and ~21 rows were filed INTO the epic since (wave 28's 8 slice rows plus follow-ups), which lands at 307. Orphans fell 117 → 75. Ledger audit Honest across the board, with no corrections owed. Every built slice is `in_progress`, published, with evidence stamped as the builder worked and the merge-gated criterion left open for the lead — s1 6/7, s3 6/7, s4 7/8 (criterion 4 an honest --miss carrying the refuting numbers), s5 7/8, s6 9/10, s7 10/11, s8 7/8. cch-w28-s2 correctly sits `open` as a deferred round-2 slice. Backlog rows filed by builders are published and open. The ONLY ledger mutation this review made was closing task-3fbfff8c97b50c8f with the nxdomain ruling (criteria 0 and 1 stamped with evidence, criterion 2 recorded as an honest --miss and closed over with a written criteria_override rather than graded by its own closer). Grade: A− WHAT EARNS IT. The wave's headline question was a judgment call between two defensible options and it was decided cleanly, then executed without cheating: #9356 is green in a REAL depth-1 clone with the thing that was red still red-able, the fabrication sentences relocated rather than deleted, and an unanchored regex that discriminated nothing repaired on the way past. Three builders reported measurements that CONTRADICTED their own briefs — the 23-failure prediction, the `returning:` prescription, the nxdomain classification — and each filed the contradiction instead of reinterpreting the criterion into something passable. That is the behaviour this epic exists to produce, and it is why the review caught real defects instead of typos. Four person-facing bodies landed with genuine fail-before proofs, and the cross-slice integration is proved by a 2693/0 full-suite run rather than asserted. WHAT HOLDS IT BACK. The instrument is still structurally blind in the only place it runs automatically — s2 was deferred by the sequenced-rounds law, which is correct process, but it means the epic is still certified by a predicate that can only give a partial verdict in CI, and s3 turned that from an unstated fact into a DOCUMENTED one, which by the wave's own standing test is a sentence, not a fix. The D307 door guard shipped armed but its hard tier can reach almost nothing (no fixture outside its own block carries a `surface` key) and its absence tier is a warn, so the filing law still holds because people are careful, not because a door refuses. s7 shipped a person-facing regression in the most common domain state that only review caught — the builder measured it and escalated correctly, but a wave that ships a decision it knows may be wrong is one review away from shipping it for real. And the domain rail now goes TERMINAL on `unknown` with no re-check affordance, which trades a spinning lie for a frozen truth. What the next wave should take MERGE ORDER, and it matters: round 1 first (#9356, then #9404-#9409, which are file-disjoint and all merge cleanly onto main in one probe). ONLY THEN cch-w28-s2 — it rewrites the same file #9356 rewrites and must mutate the discrimination out of #9356's fail-before controls. cch-w28-s2's hard constraint, armed as a tripwire by s1: HISTORY-UNAVAILABLE must surface as a verdict-token LETTER at exit 1, never a process-level exit-2 INFRA-FAULT. An INFRA-FAULT prints a=UNKNOWN and will red s1's control — deliberately. The REQUIRED `Console gate` depends on guerrilla.barkpark.cloud being reachable (one live spawn, test 56). s3 documented it; nobody has fixed it. A required gate that a third-party host can red is the same defect class as a guard no job runs. The D307 guard's promotion: the `surface` ENUM plus the backfill of open rows, which is what turns the warn tier hard. Until then “every epic row declares a surface” is false and the code says so. The s7 residue: a re-check affordance for a TERMINAL `unknown` rail, and domainRungChip's missing `unknown` arm (task-1daff7bc1bf46ceb) — a screen reader is still told “waiting” one layer below a rung that says it could not be checked. cch-w22-s7's remainder, finished or closed against origin/main's bytes rather than rebuilt. THE WAVE'S OWN SIXTH CLAUSE, PAID TWICE MORE. Wave 27 added it: an instrument pointed at the wrong ROOT reports defect-shaped prose for a condition that is only “I could not look”. Wave 28 found the same shape in two more places — a test bound to an exit code it does not test, which reported a DEFECT for an ENVIRONMENT, and a resolver classification that would have reported “we could not check” for a domain that was simply still propagating. The fix in both cases was the same move: separate the measurement from the absence of one, and say which you have.

reflow200.bodyText: Cloud Console Hardening — wave 28: the instrument fixed “I could not look” at the ROOT and left it standing at the OBJECT — and the environment it runs in is the one place it cannot look Wave 27 was the best-argued wave this epic has run. It refuted both of the lead's headline findings, paid Standing Law 0 by hand with 57 re-parented rows, and proved that the instrument certifying this epic's health was manufacturing false defect reports out of a directory it could not read. Five of its six person-facing slices are on main. One PR is open — #9356 — and it is the one everything else reads through. The lead offered this wave a binary: (a) give the CI job the history the instrument needs, or (b) restructure the red control to assert clause (a) alone. Both are defensible. Both are also incomplete, and this Paper's headline finding is why: measured live, in this session, the WAVE-27-FIXED predicate — the one on #9356, with both of its new refusals armed — still emits six verbatim “commit … is not an ancestor of origin/main” sentences inside a shallow clone. Same disease, same prose, one condition over, in the exact environment the instrument runs in automatically. The wish, and what is already true about each item # THE WISH MEASURED ON ORIGIN/MAIN DFDC31DB9, 2026-08-03T12:35Z 1 #9356 is red because console-harness.yml checks out at fetch-depth:1; decide (a) fetch-depth:0 or (b) restructure the control CONFIRMED and ENLARGED. Depth-1 clone of this repo: origin/main RESOLVES as a ref, but every registered commit is rc 128 “Not a valid object name”. The #9356 predicate passes BOTH of its new refusal legs there and prints six false ancestry sentences at b=FAIL. The binary is false — the fix is the DISCRIMINATION, and it makes both (a) and (b) correct rather than either being a workaround. 2 the D307 door guard is now a wave, not a slice; budget for a `surface` ENUM and a BACKFILL CONFIRMED as filed: cchi-w27-bl-d307-create-time-door-guard, open, 0/5, parent cch-instruments-epic, files [api/lib/barkpark/content/mutations.ex]. apply_mutations is public (mutations.ex:31) and reachable non-admin through MutateController → POST /v1/data/mutate/:dataset (router.ex:2322). The BACKFILL is a ledger write, not code — wave 27 proved the lead's hands are the right instrument for that class. 3 re-derive orphans with the fixed instrument, from a real git tree, quoting UTC stamp + tree sha + RESOLVED ROOT DONE, in this Paper. 2026-08-03T12:35:45Z · tree dfdc31db96b85b66515a1cba3f92a9e9bd81b09b · root <scratchpad>/wt-w28 → NO-SEAL a=FAIL b=PASS c=PASS orphans=57 considering=1 residue=60 (live 59). Wave 27's debrief read 62; five rows have left since. 4 person-facing residue: .preview-url deploy-row siblings; the desktop band; the render-path bypass remainder ONE PREMISE FAILS SMOKE. `.preview-url` is a DOM CHILD of `.deploy-ref` (app.js:10289 emits `<div class="deploy-ref">branch → <a class="preview-url mono">`), and #9357 landed `.deploy-ref { overflow-wrap: anywhere }` at app.css:1847 — whose own committed comment at :1841-1843 says it covers `.preview-url` inside it by inheritance. The next silent clip is NOT there. The desktop band is D323, a measured negative, correctly closed. 5 cch-w22-s7 was split and five criteria stamped by D325; finish or close the remainder against origin/main's bytes D325 is explicit: stamp C6/C7/C8/C12/C14, DROP C9 (its symbol `cuePaints` has zero occurrences under cloud/ and its second anchor file does not exist), close C15/C16 `n/a — split`. This is a LEDGER action for the lead at Decide, not a builder slice. `bp task get cch-w22-s7` returns nothing under that id — resolving the real id is survey work. THE FINDING: wave 27 named the shallow clone in its own fix's header comment, and did not close it seal-predicate.mjs:453 is one line: `try { execFileSync('git', ['-C', REPO, 'merge-base', '--is-ancestor', commit, 'origin/main'], …); } catch { problems.push(`commit ${commit} is not an ancestor of origin/main`); }`. The catch is unconditional. Charter D318 enumerated exactly what it swallows — “not-a-git-repo / no-origin-main / shallow-clone / unknown-sha” — and wave 27's fix closed the first two and wrote the other two into a comment. The wave-27 header comment says it out loud, verbatim: “the ancestry `catch` at the top of `verifyCommit` swallows not-a-git-repo, no origin/main, a shallow clone and an unknown sha into one identical claim about the PRODUCT.” The remedy that follows checks that `.github/workflows/cloud.yml` exists and that `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` resolves to REPO. A depth-1 CI clone satisfies both. Measured live in this session, controlled pair, same live ledger, same minute, nothing varied but the clone: CLONE GIT STATE PREDICATE RESULT full worktree at origin/main not shallow, all objects present origin/main's (pre-#9356) rc 1 · NO-SEAL a=FAIL b=PASS c=PASS orphans=57 `git clone --depth 1` of the same repo is-shallow-repository = true; origin/main RESOLVES; `merge-base --is-ancestor a78fd4e8c origin/main` → rc 128 `fatal: Not a valid object name` #9356's FIXED predicate, both new refusals armed rc 1 · NO-SEAL a=FAIL b=FAIL c=PASS · SIX false “commit … is not an ancestor of origin/main” sentences The instrument that certifies this epic reports “I could not look” as “I found a defect” — the exact sin wave 27 fixed — in the one environment where it runs without a human present. That is not a test failure. It is the sixth standing-test clause, live, on the very instrument that authored it. THE DIRECTION: one disease, two audiences — the console and its instrument both stop asserting what they did not measure This wave has one sentence and it points in both directions at once. A system that could not determine something must say so. It must not substitute a plausible guess, a default, or the negative branch of a two-way test it was unable to run. Pointed at the INSTRUMENT, that sentence resolves the lead's binary by refusing it. Option (a) alone leaves the predicate lying in every other shallow environment — a container, a fork PR, an agent's `--depth 1`, any future job. Option (b) alone leaves standing the fact the lead correctly identified as bigger than the test: that every seal run under this workflow is structurally unable to evaluate clause (b). The answer that pays both is the DISCRIMINATION: teach the git legs to tell rc 1 (“not an ancestor”, an honest answer about the product) from rc 128 / missing object / shallow repository (“I could not look”, an honest answer about the environment). Once the predicate can tell those apart, (b) becomes the correct shape for the control — it asserts the floor it is actually about — and (a) becomes a verified environment declaration rather than a workaround, because a regression back to depth-1 would then produce an honest INFRA-FAULT the job can assert on. Pointed at the PERSON, the same sentence is already sitting in the ledger as open rows. A refused connection is reported as “A network step timed out. Retry usually fixes this.” — the console did not classify the failure, so it guessed, and the guess carries ADVICE. A person switches on “Deployment failed” alerts across email and every chat channel, and the event has zero producers anywhere in the repository — the console tells them they are subscribed to something that cannot arrive. These are not clipping bugs. They are the epic's founding vision, in its purest form, and they are the wave's person bodies. What the finished wave looks like #9356 is MERGED, first and alone, and it merged because its control was restructured to assert clause (a) — the floor it exists to test — not because anything red was weakened. Nothing about the depth-1 environment changed to get it green. The seal predicate has a THIRD refusal in the same discipline as its first two: HISTORY-UNAVAILABLE. Run it in a shallow clone and it exits 2 with a named code and zero invented findings, exactly as it now does in a git-archive extraction. Mutation-proved with a REAL `git clone --depth 1`, not a stub — the wave-27 lesson is that stubbing the leg only moves the failure. console-harness.yml stops being an environment the instrument cannot work in. The seal job declares the history it needs, and a self-check reds if that declaration silently reverts — a guard on the guard's environment, which is the class of defect this whole wave is about. The D307 door guard is ARMED, not ruled on for a third wave. `surface` becomes an enum; the open rows are backfilled BY THE LEAD'S HAND at Decide (wave 27 proved that pattern with 57 re-parents); the fence widening is a numbered charter decision written before a builder touches mutations.ex; and the refusal is scoped to this epic's parent_id so its blast radius is this epic, not the whole task system. At least four — target five — slices where a PERSON is misinformed or cannot reach a control, led by the two rows where the console gives a confident wrong answer to a question it never asked. What this wave deliberately does NOT do It does not spend a slice on `.preview-url`. That premise failed smoke: #9357 already covers it by inheritance and the committed CSS comment says so. Booking it would be paying twice for one fix. It does not chase orphans to zero. 57 is stated with all three provenance facts and repaid only by rows that leave honestly. DEBRIEF — the wave as it will merge, and the grade it earned Seven round-1 slices were briefed, seven were built, seven are green, and all seven are PUSHED with a PR open — six new PRs (#9404-#9409) plus #9356, whose head was fast-forwarded to carry cch-w28-s1 so the fix rides the PR it was written for rather than duplicating it. cch-w28-s2 is round 2 by design and correctly sits `open` on the ledger. The reviewer re-ran every slice gate on the FINAL branch, fixed four things in place rather than reporting them, and proved the wave coheres by merging all seven onto origin/main in one probe branch: the FULL cloud suite is 2693 tests / 0 failures there, and __app.test.mjs is 797/797. What shipped, per slice SLICE FINAL BRANCH / PR GATE RE-RUN AT REVIEW VERDICT cch-w28-s1 — the empty-roster control asserts clause (a) loop-epic/9356-goes-green-without-weakening-the-th-0-r → fast-forwarded onto #9356 FULL clone 65/65 rc 0; REAL --depth 1 --no-local clone 65/65 rc 0 (shallowness proved inside it: all-refs log = 1 commit, `git rev-parse origin/main` exits 128) Option (b) exactly as decided: no fetch-depth, no stubbed git leg, required-checks.json untouched. No fixes needed. The four things the reviewer FIXED rather than reported 1. THE FALSE SENTENCE IN THE D307 GUARD'S HEADER (commit 73438f573). The shipped comment claimed that deleting the scoping arm takes mutate_controller_test.exs “from 36/36 to 23 failures, including the D53 create-family pins”. The builder had already measured 1 failure and stamped an honest --miss on the criterion — but left the brief's number standing in the code. Re-run independently at review (delete `not cch_epic_child?(parent) -> :ok`, change nothing else): 46 tests / 1 failure, and that failure is this slice's own scoping test. The comment now states the measured result and says plainly that the scoping is a DESIGN boundary, not a load-bearing leg under today's corpus. An epic whose thesis is “stop asserting what you did not measure” cannot ship a header comment that does exactly that. 2. `:nxdomain` IS AN ANSWER, NOT A FAULT (commits 90ab9999a + 438495a96) — a REVIEW DECISION superseding the letter of D332. The s7 builder built D332 as written, measured that one fifth of it was wrong, and filed task-3fbfff8c97b50c8f at priority 0 rather than quietly re-deciding. He was right on both counts. Re-measured at review on this host: `:inet.getaddrs` of a non-existent name returns `{:error, :nxdomain}` on BOTH families — which is precisely what a freshly attached, still-propagating domain looks like through the real transport. Shipped literally, D332 would have turned the MOST COMMON waiting state into “we could not check” and stripped its propagation advice: one lie swapped for another, in the very rung the slice existed to make honest. NXDOMAIN means the resolver ANSWERED. Fixed with `@answered_empty [:nxdomain]`, and — the half that matters for the standing test — the DNS test fakes now RETURN nxdomain for a missing record instead of `{:ok, []}`, a shape production never produces. task-3fbfff8c97b50c8f is closed with the ruling, its measurement and its residual gap on the record. 3. THE REAP ALERT CAP IS NOW DRIVEN (commit ab2a6dce5). `@reap_alert_cap 25` decides that the 26th owner in a cluster incident hears nothing by email — a person-facing SUPPRESSION that no fixture crossed. The builder flagged it against himself; the review paid it: a test fails 27 deployments in one sweep and asserts exactly 25 emails plus the suppression log line, with `Registry.reap_alert_cap/0` exposed so the test reads the real constant instead of a copy. Mutation-proved: replacing `Enum.split(alerts, @reap_alert_cap)` with `{alerts, []}` reds exactly that test and nothing else. 4. Each anchor is now asserted present before use. Orphans, re-derived with the fixed instrument from a real git tree All three things the wish demanded are quoted, not paraphrased. VERDICT-TOKEN: SEAL-PREDICATE NO-SEAL a=FAIL b=PASS c=PASS orphans=75 considering=1 successor=cch-instruments-epic epic=cloud-console-hardening-epic mode=live stubbed=0 waived=0 roster=307 head=52a80c7be Roster 307 {done 195, in_progress 7, open 70, cancelled 34, considering 1}. Residue 78 (live 77, considering 1); forwarded under the successor 0; the three permanent human gates all resolve in-roster. b=PASS here because this is a FULL clone. That is the wave's whole finding restated: the same predicate under console-harness.yml still cannot evaluate clause (b) at all, and nothing in CI has changed about that. D306's two integers, as deltas against wave 27's 117 / roster 343 {189, 119, 34, 1} at c2affd445 — RE-PARENTED OUT OF THIS ROSTER = 36 (343 → 307), CLOSED = +6 done (189 → 195). The 36 does not equal wave 27's 57 hand re-parents, and the reconciliation is stated rather than smoothed: 343 − 57 = 286, and ~21 rows were filed INTO the epic since (wave 28's 8 slice rows plus follow-ups), which lands at 307. Orphans fell 117 → 75. Ledger audit Honest across the board, with no corrections owed. Every built slice is `in_progress`, published, with evidence stamped as the builder worked and the merge-gated criterion left open for the lead — s1 6/7, s3 6/7, s4 7/8 (criterion 4 an honest --miss carrying the refuting numbers), s5 7/8, s6 9/10, s7 10/11, s8 7/8. cch-w28-s2 correctly sits `open` as a deferred round-2 slice. Backlog rows filed by builders are published and open. The ONLY ledger mutation this review made was closing task-3fbfff8c97b50c8f with the nxdomain ruling (criteria 0 and 1 stamped with evidence, criterion 2 recorded as an honest --miss and closed over with a written criteria_override rather than graded by its own closer). Grade: A− WHAT EARNS IT. The wave's headline question was a judgment call between two defensible options and it was decided cleanly, then executed without cheating: #9356 is green in a REAL depth-1 clone with the thing that was red still red-able, the fabrication sentences relocated rather than deleted, and an unanchored regex that discriminated nothing repaired on the way past. Three builders reported measurements that CONTRADICTED their own briefs — the 23-failure prediction, the `returning:` prescription, the nxdomain classification — and each filed the contradiction instead of reinterpreting the criterion into something passable. That is the behaviour this epic exists to produce, and it is why the review caught real defects instead of typos. Four person-facing bodies landed with genuine fail-before proofs, and the cross-slice integration is proved by a 2693/0 full-suite run rather than asserted. WHAT HOLDS IT BACK. The instrument is still structurally blind in the only place it runs automatically — s2 was deferred by the sequenced-rounds law, which is correct process, but it means the epic is still certified by a predicate that can only give a partial verdict in CI, and s3 turned that from an unstated fact into a DOCUMENTED one, which by the wave's own standing test is a sentence, not a fix. The D307 door guard shipped armed but its hard tier can reach almost nothing (no fixture outside its own block carries a `surface` key) and its absence tier is a warn, so the filing law still holds because people are careful, not because a door refuses. s7 shipped a person-facing regression in the most common domain state that only review caught — the builder measured it and escalated correctly, but a wave that ships a decision it knows may be wrong is one review away from shipping it for real. And the domain rail now goes TERMINAL on `unknown` with no re-check affordance, which trades a spinning lie for a frozen truth. What the next wave should take MERGE ORDER, and it matters: round 1 first (#9356, then #9404-#9409, which are file-disjoint and all merge cleanly onto main in one probe). ONLY THEN cch-w28-s2 — it rewrites the same file #9356 rewrites and must mutate the discrimination out of #9356's fail-before controls. cch-w28-s2's hard constraint, armed as a tripwire by s1: HISTORY-UNAVAILABLE must surface as a verdict-token LETTER at exit 1, never a process-level exit-2 INFRA-FAULT. An INFRA-FAULT prints a=UNKNOWN and will red s1's control — deliberately. The REQUIRED `Console gate` depends on guerrilla.barkpark.cloud being reachable (one live spawn, test 56). s3 documented it; nobody has fixed it. A required gate that a third-party host can red is the same defect class as a guard no job runs. The D307 guard's promotion: the `surface` ENUM plus the backfill of open rows, which is what turns the warn tier hard. Until then “every epic row declares a surface” is false and the code says so. The s7 residue: a re-check affordance for a TERMINAL `unknown` rail, and domainRungChip's missing `unknown` arm (task-1daff7bc1bf46ceb) — a screen reader is still told “waiting” one layer below a rung that says it could not be checked. cch-w22-s7's remainder, finished or closed against origin/main's bytes rather than rebuilt. THE WAVE'S OWN SIXTH CLAUSE, PAID TWICE MORE. Wave 27 added it: an instrument pointed at the wrong ROOT reports defect-shaped prose for a condition that is only “I could not look”. Wave 28 found the same shape in two more places — a test bound to an exit code it does not test, which reported a DEFECT for an ENVIRONMENT, and a resolver classification that would have reported “we could not check” for a domain that was simply still propagating. The fix in both cases was the same move: separate the measurement from the absence of one, and say which you have.

320.bodyText: Cloud Console Hardening — wave 28: the instrument fixed “I could not look” at the ROOT and left it standing at the OBJECT — and the environment it runs in is the one place it cannot look Wave 27 was the best-argued wave this epic has run. It refuted both of the lead's headline findings, paid Standing Law 0 by hand with 57 re-parented rows, and proved that the instrument certifying this epic's health was manufacturing false defect reports out of a directory it could not read. Five of its six person-facing slices are on main. One PR is open — #9356 — and it is the one everything else reads through. The lead offered this wave a binary: (a) give the CI job the history the instrument needs, or (b) restructure the red control to assert clause (a) alone. Both are defensible. Both are also incomplete, and this Paper's headline finding is why: measured live, in this session, the WAVE-27-FIXED predicate — the one on #9356, with both of its new refusals armed — still emits six verbatim “commit … is not an ancestor of origin/main” sentences inside a shallow clone. Same disease, same prose, one condition over, in the exact environment the instrument runs in automatically. Every built slice is `in_progress`, published, with evidence stamped as the builder worked and the merge-gated criterion left open for the lead — s1 6/7, s3 6/7, s4 7/8 (criterion 4 an honest --miss carrying the refuting numbers), s5 7/8, s6 9/10, s7 10/11, s8 7/8. cch-w28-s2 correctly sits `open` as a deferred round-2 slice. Backlog rows filed by builders are published and open. The ONLY ledger mutation this review made was closing task-3fbfff8c97b50c8f with the nxdomain ruling (criteria 0 and 1 stamped with evidence, criterion 2 recorded as an honest --miss and closed over with a written criteria_override rather than graded by its own closer). Grade: A− WHAT EARNS IT. The wave's headline question was a judgment call between two defensible options and it was decided cleanly, then executed without cheating: #9356 is green in a REAL depth-1 clone with the thing that was red still red-able, the fabrication sentences relocated rather than deleted, and an unanchored regex that discriminated nothing repaired on the way past. Three builders reported measurements that CONTRADICTED their own briefs — the 23-failure prediction, the `returning:` prescription, the nxdomain classification — and each filed the contradiction instead of reinterpreting the criterion into something passable. That is the behaviour this epic exists to produce, and it is why the review caught real defects instead of typos. Four person-facing bodies landed with genuine fail-before proofs, and the cross-slice integration is proved by a 2693/0 full-suite run rather than asserted. WHAT HOLDS IT BACK. The instrument is still structurally blind in the only place it runs automatically — s2 was deferred by the sequenced-rounds law, which is correct process, but it means the epic is still certified by a predicate that can only give a partial verdict in CI, and s3 turned that from an unstated fact into a DOCUMENTED one, which by the wave's own standing test is a sentence, not a fix. The D307 door guard shipped armed but its hard tier can reach almost nothing (no fixture outside its own block carries a `surface` key) and its absence tier is a warn, so the filing law still holds because people are careful, not because a door refuses. s7 shipped a person-facing regression in the most common domain state that only review caught — the builder measured it and escalated correctly, but a wave that ships a decision it knows may be wrong is one review away from shipping it for real. And the domain rail now goes TERMINAL on `unknown` with no re-check affordance, which trades a spinning lie for a frozen truth. What the next wave should take MERGE ORDER, and it matters: round 1 first (#9356, then #9404-#9409, which are file-disjoint and all merge cleanly onto main in one probe). ONLY THEN cch-w28-s2 — it rewrites the same file #9356 rewrites and must mutate the discrimination out of #9356's fail-before controls. cch-w28-s2's hard constraint, armed as a tripwire by s1: HISTORY-UNAVAILABLE must surface as a verdict-token LETTER at exit 1, never a process-level exit-2 INFRA-FAULT. An INFRA-FAULT prints a=UNKNOWN and will red s1's control — deliberately. The REQUIRED `Console gate` depends on guerrilla.barkpark.cloud being reachable (one live spawn, test 56). s3 documented it; nobody has fixed it. A required gate that a third-party host can red is the same defect class as a guard no job runs. The D307 guard's promotion: the `surface` ENUM plus the backfill of open rows, which is what turns the warn tier hard. Until then “every epic row declares a surface” is false and the code says so. The s7 residue: a re-check affordance for a TERMINAL `unknown` rail, and domainRungChip's missing `unknown` arm (task-1daff7bc1bf46ceb) — a screen reader is still told “waiting” one layer below a rung that says it could not be checked. cch-w22-s7's remainder, finished or closed against origin/main's bytes rather than rebuilt. THE WAVE'S OWN SIXTH CLAUSE, PAID TWICE MORE. Wave 27 added it: an instrument pointed at the wrong ROOT reports defect-shaped prose for a condition that is only “I could not look”. Wave 28 found the same shape in two more places — a test bound to an exit code it does not test, which reported a DEFECT for an ENVIRONMENT, and a resolver classification that would have reported “we could not check” for a domain that was simply still propagating. The fix in both cases was the same move: separate the measurement from the absence of one, and say which you have. TUI view Email view

390.bodyText: Cloud Console Hardening — wave 28: the instrument fixed “I could not look” at the ROOT and left it standing at the OBJECT — and the environment it runs in is the one place it cannot look Wave 27 was the best-argued wave this epic has run. It refuted both of the lead's headline findings, paid Standing Law 0 by hand with 57 re-parented rows, and proved that the instrument certifying this epic's health was manufacturing false defect reports out of a directory it could not read. Five of its six person-facing slices are on main. One PR is open — #9356 — and it is the one everything else reads through. The lead offered this wave a binary: (a) give the CI job the history the instrument needs, or (b) restructure the red control to assert clause (a) alone. Both are defensible. Both are also incomplete, and this Paper's headline finding is why: measured live, in this session, the WAVE-27-FIXED predicate — the one on #9356, with both of its new refusals armed — still emits six verbatim “commit … is not an ancestor of origin/main” sentences inside a shallow clone. Same disease, same prose, one condition over, in the exact environment the instrument runs in automatically. The wish, and what is already true about each item # THE WISH MEASURED ON ORIGIN/MAIN DFDC31DB9, 2026-08-03T12:35Z 1 #9356 is red because console-harness.yml checks out at fetch-depth:1; decide (a) fetch-depth:0 or (b) restructure the control CONFIRMED and ENLARGED. Depth-1 clone of this repo: origin/main RESOLVES as a ref, but every registered commit is rc 128 “Not a valid object name”. The #9356 predicate passes BOTH of its new refusal legs there and prints six false ancestry sentences at b=FAIL. The binary is false — the fix is the DISCRIMINATION, and it makes both (a) and (b) correct rather than either being a workaround. 2 the D307 door guard is now a wave, not a slice; budget for a `surface` ENUM and a BACKFILL CONFIRMED as filed: cchi-w27-bl-d307-create-time-door-guard, open, 0/5, parent cch-instruments-epic, files [api/lib/barkpark/content/mutations.ex]. apply_mutations is public (mutations.ex:31) and reachable non-admin through MutateController → POST /v1/data/mutate/:dataset (router.ex:2322). The BACKFILL is a ledger write, not code — wave 27 proved the lead's hands are the right instrument for that class. 3 re-derive orphans with the fixed instrument, from a real git tree, quoting UTC stamp + tree sha + RESOLVED ROOT DONE, in this Paper. 2026-08-03T12:35:45Z · tree dfdc31db96b85b66515a1cba3f92a9e9bd81b09b · root <scratchpad>/wt-w28 → NO-SEAL a=FAIL b=PASS c=PASS orphans=57 considering=1 residue=60 (live 59). Wave 27's debrief read 62; five rows have left since. 4 person-facing residue: .preview-url deploy-row siblings; the desktop band; the render-path bypass remainder ONE PREMISE FAILS SMOKE. `.preview-url` is a DOM CHILD of `.deploy-ref` (app.js:10289 emits `<div class="deploy-ref">branch → <a class="preview-url mono">`), and #9357 landed `.deploy-ref { overflow-wrap: anywhere }` at app.css:1847 — whose own committed comment at :1841-1843 says it covers `.preview-url` inside it by inheritance. The next silent clip is NOT there. The desktop band is D323, a measured negative, correctly closed. 5 cch-w22-s7 was split and five criteria stamped by D325; finish or close the remainder against origin/main's bytes D325 is explicit: stamp C6/C7/C8/C12/C14, DROP C9 (its symbol `cuePaints` has zero occurrences under cloud/ and its second anchor file does not exist), close C15/C16 `n/a — split`. This is a LEDGER action for the lead at Decide, not a builder slice. `bp task get cch-w22-s7` returns nothing under that id — resolving the real id is survey work. THE FINDING: wave 27 named the shallow clone in its own fix's header comment, and did not close it seal-predicate.mjs:453 is one line: `try { execFileSync('git', ['-C', REPO, 'merge-base', '--is-ancestor', commit, 'origin/main'], …); } catch { problems.push(`commit ${commit} is not an ancestor of origin/main`); }`. The catch is unconditional. Charter D318 enumerated exactly what it swallows — “not-a-git-repo / no-origin-main / shallow-clone / unknown-sha” — and wave 27's fix closed the first two and wrote the other two into a comment. The wave-27 header comment says it out loud, verbatim: “the ancestry `catch` at the top of `verifyCommit` swallows not-a-git-repo, no origin/main, a shallow clone and an unknown sha into one identical claim about the PRODUCT.” The remedy that follows checks that `.github/workflows/cloud.yml` exists and that `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` resolves to REPO. A depth-1 CI clone satisfies both. Measured live in this session, controlled pair, same live ledger, same minute, nothing varied but the clone: CLONE GIT STATE PREDICATE RESULT full worktree at origin/main not shallow, all objects present origin/main's (pre-#9356) rc 1 · NO-SEAL a=FAIL b=PASS c=PASS orphans=57 `git clone --depth 1` of the same repo is-shallow-repository = true; origin/main RESOLVES; `merge-base --is-ancestor a78fd4e8c origin/main` → rc 128 `fatal: Not a valid object name` #9356's FIXED predicate, both new refusals armed rc 1 · NO-SEAL a=FAIL b=FAIL c=PASS · SIX false “commit … is not an ancestor of origin/main” sentences The instrument that certifies this epic reports “I could not look” as “I found a defect” — the exact sin wave 27 fixed — in the one environment where it runs without a human present. That is not a test failure. It is the sixth standing-test clause, live, on the very instrument that authored it. THE DIRECTION: one disease, two audiences — the console and its instrument both stop asserting what they did not measure This wave has one sentence and it points in both directions at once. A system that could not determine something must say so. It must not substitute a plausible guess, a default, or the negative branch of a two-way test it was unable to run. Pointed at the INSTRUMENT, that sentence resolves the lead's binary by refusing it. Option (a) alone leaves the predicate lying in every other shallow environment — a container, a fork PR, an agent's `--depth 1`, any future job. Option (b) alone leaves standing the fact the lead correctly identified as bigger than the test: that every seal run under this workflow is structurally unable to evaluate clause (b). The answer that pays both is the DISCRIMINATION: teach the git legs to tell rc 1 (“not an ancestor”, an honest answer about the product) from rc 128 / missing object / shallow repository (“I could not look”, an honest answer about the environment). Once the predicate can tell those apart, (b) becomes the correct shape for the control — it asserts the floor it is actually about — and (a) becomes a verified environment declaration rather than a workaround, because a regression back to depth-1 would then produce an honest INFRA-FAULT the job can assert on. Pointed at the PERSON, the same sentence is already sitting in the ledger as open rows. A refused connection is reported as “A network step timed out. Retry usually fixes this.” — the console did not classify the failure, so it guessed, and the guess carries ADVICE. A person switches on “Deployment failed” alerts across email and every chat channel, and the event has zero producers anywhere in the repository — the console tells them they are subscribed to something that cannot arrive. These are not clipping bugs. They are the epic's founding vision, in its purest form, and they are the wave's person bodies. What the finished wave looks like #9356 is MERGED, first and alone, and it merged because its control was restructured to assert clause (a) — the floor it exists to test — not because anything red was weakened. Nothing about the depth-1 environment changed to get it green. The seal predicate has a THIRD refusal in the same discipline as its first two: HISTORY-UNAVAILABLE. Run it in a shallow clone and it exits 2 with a named code and zero invented findings, exactly as it now does in a git-archive extraction. Mutation-proved with a REAL `git clone --depth 1`, not a stub — the wave-27 lesson is that stubbing the leg only moves the failure. console-harness.yml stops being an environment the instrument cannot work in. The seal job declares the history it needs, and a self-check reds if that declaration silently reverts — a guard on the guard's environment, which is the class of defect this whole wave is about. The D307 door guard is ARMED, not ruled on for a third wave. `surface` becomes an enum; the open rows are backfilled BY THE LEAD'S HAND at Decide (wave 27 proved that pattern with 57 re-parents); the fence widening is a numbered charter decision written before a builder touches mutations.ex; and the refusal is scoped to this epic's parent_id so its blast radius is this epic, not the whole task system. At least four — target five — slices where a PERSON is misinformed or cannot reach a control, led by the two rows where the console gives a confident wrong answer to a question it never asked. What this wave deliberately does NOT do It does not spend a slice on `.preview-url`. That premise failed smoke: #9357 already covers it by inheritance and the committed CSS comment says so. Booking it would be paying twice for one fix. It does not chase orphans to zero. 57 is stated with all three provenance facts and repaid only by rows that leave honestly. Wave 27 already made the largest Law-0 payment in the epic's history; a wave spent on ledger hygiene is the disease the charter names at waves 9/10/11. It does not touch .github/required-checks.json, and it registers nothing. The direction debate: three candidates, argued, one committed Rival A — “Finish the instrument, build the door” (the wish read literally) Take the lead's binary, pick one leg, and spend the rest of the wave on the D307 door guard as a full multi-slice build: the `surface` enum, the backfill, the fence ruling, the refusal, the mutation proof. Clean, obedient, and it retires the highest-leverage row in the epic. WHY IT LOSES. Three counts. First, arithmetic: four instrument slices against a floor of four person bodies means eight slices minimum, and this epic's own history says a wave that spends 4-of-6 on instruments moves the row count the wrong way (waves 9/10/11: +11, +16, +7). Second, the door guard's dependency chain — enum → backfill → fence ruling → refusal — is SERIAL and cannot fan out to parallel builders, so it converts a fan-out wave into a queue. Third and worst, it accepts the false binary. Picking (a) or (b) at speed leaves the predicate lying in every shallow environment that is not this one workflow, and this Paper has now proved live that such an environment exists and that the epic's own instrument is in it. Rival B — “Pay Law 0 to zero and drive at the seal” orphans is 57 and a=FAIL is the only clause failing. Spend the wave closing, forwarding and adjudicating residue — including the cch-w22-s7 split D325 already ruled — and get the epic within sight of an honest SEAL. WHY IT LOSES. It is the epic's stated disease wearing a productivity costume. The charter's vision is that the CONSOLE stops lying; a wave with zero person bodies fails the ratio outright and would be the fourth restatement of a law rather than a payment of it. It also mistakes the seal for the goal — D318 proved the predicate could SEAL an epic that does not exist, which means a falling orphan count was never the thing worth optimising. HARVESTED ANYWAY: this Paper quotes the reading with all three provenance facts, and the cch-w22-s7 adjudication is booked as a Decide-phase ledger action for the lead, costing zero builders. Rival C — “One disease, two audiences” — COMMITTED Two instrument slices that pay the environment question properly plus the discrimination that generalises it; one door-guard slice made buildable by moving its backfill dependency onto the lead's hands at Decide; and four-to-five person bodies chosen so that at least two of them are literally the same defect the instrument has — a system asserting a fact it did not measure. WHY IT WINS. It is the only candidate where the instrument work and the person work are the SAME argument, which means the wave's finding transfers: the sentence that fixes the seal predicate is the sentence a builder applies to `connection refused`. It keeps the ratio at four-plus without inventing filler. It refuses the lead's binary on evidence rather than on preference — the depth-1 run is measured, not reasoned. And it ships the door guard ARMED this wave by removing the dependency that blocked it, rather than ruling on it for a third consecutive wave. The sharpest attack on the winner, and how the wave absorbs it “You are deferring the D307 door guard AGAIN. Wave 26 ruled on it, wave 27 filed it, and ‘build the enum, defer the refusal’ is exactly the shape that lets wave 29 defer it a fourth time. Meanwhile you have talked yourself into a THIRD instrument slice nobody asked for.” TAKEN, and it changes the plan rather than being argued away. The wave does not ship the enum and defer the refusal — it ships the refusal ARMED, and it removes the blocker by re-classifying it. D324 gave four honest reasons the guard could not ship: (i) no classifier, (ii) the fence widening is not a builder's call, (iii) CI is post-hoc detection not refusal, (iv) shipping before the backfill makes the guard's first act on main a refusal of legitimate filings. Reasons (i) and (iv) are LEDGER work, and wave 27 proved conclusively that ledger work belongs to the lead's hands at Decide — 57 re-parents, executed in minutes, with the post-condition asserted on the destination roster. Reason (ii) is a numbered charter decision, which is also a Decide-phase artifact. Reason (iii) argues FOR the door, not against it. So the builder's slice is what remains: the enum validation and the refusal, scoped to one parent_id, with a mutation proof that shows it can both refuse and pass. If survey finds the backfill is larger or messier than wave 27's re-parent — a real risk, since `surface` is populated on 24 of 343 rows and is free prose — the wave scopes the guard's population to rows the backfill actually reached and says so, rather than arming a refusal over rows it cannot classify. On the third instrument slice: it is not a third, it is the CORRECT first. Without the discrimination, both of the lead's options are workarounds, and this Paper has the run output proving it. The wave's own ratio discipline still binds — if the discrimination and the environment declaration cannot be shown to be one coherent slice at Decide, the environment half merges with #9356 and the wave spends the recovered budget on a fifth person body. Premise smoke — every inherited premise this direction leans on, run rather than quoted PREMISE (SOURCE) THE CHECK THAT WAS RUN RESULT Wave 27's five slices are on main; only #9356 is open (lead notes, L6) `git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> origin/main` for all six named shas; `gh pr view 9356` CONFIRMED. a78fd4e8c, c4a359d0c, 713795305, 7c8fa229a, 271d4a244, dfdc31db9 all ancestors. #9356 OPEN; `Console gate` and `Console client unit harness` both FAILURE. console-harness.yml checks out at fetch-depth 1 (wish item 1) `git show origin/main:.github/workflows/console-harness.yml` CONFIRMED for console-unit (bare `actions/checkout@v4`, v4's default depth is 1). NUANCE the wish does not carry: the `changes` job at :104 DOES set fetch-depth: 0, so the file already contains the remedy pattern for a different job. A depth-1 clone “has neither origin/main nor those commits” (wish item 1) `git clone --depth 1`; `git branch -r`; `git merge-base --is-ancestor a78fd4e8c origin/main` HALF REFUTED, and the half that fails matters. origin/main DOES exist as a ref in a depth-1 clone. Only the OBJECTS are missing (rc 128 `Not a valid object name`). Both new refusal legs PASS in a shallow clone; six false ancestry sentences print anyway. b=FAIL from a clone, b=PASS from a full tree, same ledger, same minute. `.preview-url` is the next silent clip (wish item 4) `git show origin/main:cloud/priv/static/app.css | grep`; `app.js` previewRow FAILS SMOKE — a FINDING, not a foundation. app.css:1847 `.deploy-ref { … overflow-wrap: anywhere }` (landed #9357) and app.js emits `.preview-url` INSIDE `.deploy-ref`. The committed comment at :1841-1843 states the inheritance explicitly. Already paid. The D307 door guard's target is reachable through a real non-admin write path `git grep apply_mutations`; router.ex route table CONFIRMED. `Content.apply_mutations/3` is public at mutations.ex:31; callers are MutateController (POST /v1/data/mutate/:dataset, router.ex:2322), Sync.Applier and papers/value_writeback. Not an admin-only path. mutations.ex:470-545 already hosts a create-time door guard, so the pattern exists in-file. cch-w26-bl-deploy-row-siblings-unwrapped is residue `bp task get` REFUTED. It is DONE at 10/10 — that IS #9357. The residual row the wish is reaching for does not exist under that id. Every code site the direction names still exists on origin/main `git cat-file -e origin/main:<path>` × 9 ALL PRESENT: mutations.ex, sites/deploy.ex, app.js, app.css, scenarios.mjs, overflow-guard.mjs, console-harness.yml, and both wave-27 ledger recipes under tooling/grip/ledger/. Charter D-numbers this direction cites (D307, D317, D318, D319, D321, D322, D324, D325) exist AND cover what they are cited for `git show origin/main:.claude/workflows/…charter.md`, read verbatim ALL PRESENT AND COVERING. D324 in particular authorises exactly the four-reason deferral this direction dismantles, and names `surface` at 24/343 free prose — the number the direction budgets against. Two premises failed smoke and both are stated rather than dropped: `.preview-url` is already paid, and “a depth-1 clone has no origin/main” is false in the half that would have shaped the remedy. One premise was ENLARGED: the wrong-root fix does not generalise, and the proof is a live run rather than an argument. The shape the wave is aiming at — seven named, five expected Tentative. Decide finalises after two exploration rounds; survey may kill any of these and is expected to promote at least one replacement on its own evidence, as wave 27's flick-to-bottom and progressbar bodies were. # CANDIDATE CLASS NOTE 1 #9356 unhostaged — the empty-roster control asserts CLAUSE (a), not the overall verdict instrument Merges FIRST and ALONE. Nothing red is weakened; the control stops being hostage to clauses it does not test. 2 HISTORY-UNAVAILABLE — the git legs tell “not an ancestor” from “I could not look”, mutation-proved in a real `--depth 1` clone instrument The crown. Generalises wave 27's fix to the condition its own comment names. 3 The seal job's environment is DECLARED and its regression is detectable instrument May merge into #2 at Decide if they are one coherent change; the wave's ratio recovers a slice if so. 4 A refused connection stops being reported as a timeout with retry advice PERSON `cch-w27-bl-connection-refused-classified-as-timeout`, open, 0/4. The console guesses a classification and attaches ADVICE to the guess. 5 The “Deployment failed” toggle stops promising alerts nothing can send PERSON `cch-w27-bl-deployment-failed-toggle-fires-nothing`, open, 0/6. Default-ON across email and every chat channel; D321 measured ZERO dispatch sites. Needs a policy ruling at Decide: remove the control or wire the producer. 6 The deploy-stage `detail` remainder — what #9355 actually closed and what is still raw PERSON D321(3)/(4): `Sites.Deploy.fail/2` writes one reason to BOTH `failure_reason:` and `detail:`; deploy.ex:842 `detail: stage.detail || stage_line(stage)` is a second path. Survey must establish what remains after #9355. 7 The D307 door guard, ARMED — `surface` enum + create-time refusal scoped to this epic's parent_id instrument Backfill and fence ruling are LEAD work at Decide, not builder work. Builder ships enum + refusal + a mutation proof that can both refuse and pass. — A fifth person body PERSON Held open deliberately. D311's `#cred-back` finding (four of five exits fail to resume, fix is path-asymmetric) is the leading candidate to check for whether it was ever built. RATIO: at least four slices where a PERSON is misinformed or cannot reach a control. Items 4, 5, 6 and one survey-promoted body are the four; the wave does not ship if fewer than four survive. The survey plan — 17 assignments, and why each one can change the plan Width is deliberate. Every load-bearing assumption in the direction above appears below as a question a surveyor can answer with a run. KEY THE QUESTION WHY IT CHANGES THE PLAN shallow-clone-discrimination Enumerate EVERY git read seal-predicate.mjs makes (merge-base --is-ancestor :453, git show --format= :429, git show --name-only :432, rev-parse --show-toplevel in assertReadableRepoRoot) and for each establish which exit codes/conditions are an HONEST ANSWER ABOUT THE PRODUCT versus 'I could not look'. Run each under: full clone, `git clone --depth 1`, `--depth 50` where the commit exists but history is grafted, a `--filter=blob:none` partial clone, and a clone with no `origin` remote. Does `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` combined with `git cat-file -e <sha>^{commit}` fully discriminate, or is there a residual case where rc 1 from --is-ancestor is UNTRUSTWORTHY because history is truncated? This is the crown slice's entire design. If rc 1 is untrustworthy in a grafted clone, the refusal must key on shallowness itself and not only on object presence — a materially different guard. ci-fetch-depth-blast-radius What does `fetch-depth: 0` actually cost the `console-unit` job — clone wall-clock, runner disk — and what already pays it in this repo (console-harness.yml's `changes` job at :104 sets it; find every other)? Which OTHER jobs or workflows anywhere in .github/ invoke seal-predicate.mjs or any other git-reading instrument, and at what depth?
