BACKLOG FILED THIS WAVE, six rows, all published under the epic: cch-w28-bl-capacity-arm-blames-hetzner-for-azure (a bare `quota` token tells an Azure-failed person Hetzner ran out of servers); cch-w28-bl-overflow-guard-clipper-blames-the-wrong-panel (D322's latent false attribution, plus two further defects found in the same six lines -- a 40-char truncated dedupe key and a filler that degrades to the first panel in document order); cch-w28-bl-usage-meters-say-unmetered-when-they-could-not-measure (the same shape as D332, weaker, honestly priced); cch-w28-bl-w22s7-split-stamps-never-landed-and-c9-kill-is-refuted (the ledger work, with corrected anchors and the unrun mutation that would settle C9); cch-w28-bl-orphans-swallows-the-disclosed-considering-row (a row printed on two mutually exclusive lines, plus three draft twins the predicate cannot see); cch-w28-bl-auto-deploy-refusal-has-no-event-at-all. WHAT WOULD FALSIFY THIS WAVE. If s2's four probes cannot be shown to answer correctly in a REAL grafted clone and a REAL simulated pull_request checkout -- not a stub, not a JSON fixture -- then the discrimination is a sentence with an exit code and s1's green was bought rather than earned. If s4's guard cannot be shown to REFUSE and to PASS over HTTP, and to leave the two D53 pinning tests green ONLY because of its parent scoping, then the door was never armed. And if s7's `unknown` does not set terminal:true in the shipped app.js, the console keeps polling a dead resolver forever and the person is no better off than before -- a server-only fix here is a regression wearing a decision's clothes. DEBRIEF — the wave as it will merge, and the grade it earned Seven round-1 slices were briefed, seven were built, seven are green, and all seven are PUSHED with a PR open — six new PRs (#9404-#9409) plus #9356, whose head was fast-forwarded to carry cch-w28-s1 so the fix rides the PR it was written for rather than duplicating it. cch-w28-s2 is round 2 by design and correctly sits `open` on the ledger. The reviewer re-ran every slice gate on the FINAL branch, fixed four things in place rather than reporting them, and proved the wave coheres by merging all seven onto origin/main in one probe branch: the FULL cloud suite is 2693 tests / 0 failures there, and __app.test.mjs is 797/797. What shipped, per slice SLICE FINAL BRANCH / PR GATE RE-RUN AT REVIEW VERDICT cch-w28-s1 — the empty-roster control asserts clause (a) loop-epic/9356-goes-green-without-weakening-the-th-0-r → fast-forwarded onto #9356 FULL clone 65/65 rc 0; REAL --depth 1 --no-local clone 65/65 rc 0 (shallowness proved inside it: all-refs log = 1 commit, `git rev-parse origin/main` exits 128) Option (b) exactly as decided: no fetch-depth, no stubbed git leg, required-checks.json untouched. Reviewer hardened the mutation anchors. cch-w28-s3 — console-harness hermeticity prose loop-epic/console-harness-yml-stops-asserting-thre-1 → #9404 YAML parses rc 0; the non-comment-diff grep finds NOTHING; suite on main re-derived at 59/59; BP_SERVER on a dead port reds EXACTLY `not ok 56` Comment-only and every sentence true of the bytes beside it. No fixes needed. cch-w28-s4 — the D307 door guard, armed loop-epic/the-d307-filing-law-door-guard-ships-arm-2-r → #9405 mutate_controller_test.exs 46/0 rc 0; tasks+content 1554/0 rc 0; mix format clean HIGH-FLIP-RISK, independently re-derived. Reviewer deleted a FALSE sentence from the shipped comment (see below). cch-w28-s5 — a refused connection is not a timeout loop-epic/person-a-refused-connection-stops-being--3 → #9406 failure_copy_test.exs 83/0 rc 0; the six-file sweep 202/0 rc 0 Both halves mutation-proved by the builder; the test that PINNED the defect as correct was corrected, not kept. No fixes needed. cch-w28-s6 — :deployment_failed actually dispatches loop-epic/person-the-deployment-failed-toggle-stop-4-r → #9407 router_notifications + deployment_failed_dispatch 29/0 rc 0; mix format clean HIGH-FLIP-RISK census re-derived. Reviewer added the missing cap test — the wave's own clause 4, turned on the wave. cch-w28-s7 — an unreachable resolver is `unknown` loop-epic/person-an-unreachable-resolver-stops-bei-5-r → #9408 domain_status_test.exs 47/0 rc 0; node --check rc 0; __app.test.mjs 796/796 rc 0; mix format clean Reviewer DECIDED the open P0 question the builder correctly escalated instead of deciding (see below). cch-w28-s8 — a never-deployed row says “Not deployed” loop-epic/person-a-never-deployed-site-row-in-the--6 → #9409 node --check rc 0; __app.test.mjs 793/793 rc 0; diff is exactly the two owned files Fail-before proved by stash, fixture asserts its own honesty, no new CSS. No fixes needed. The four things the reviewer FIXED rather than reported 1. THE FALSE SENTENCE IN THE D307 GUARD'S HEADER (commit 73438f573). The shipped comment claimed that deleting the scoping arm takes mutate_controller_test.exs “from 36/36 to 23 failures, including the D53 create-family pins”. The builder had already measured 1 failure and stamped an honest --miss on the criterion — but left the brief's number standing in the code. Re-run independently at review (delete `not cch_epic_child?(parent) -> :ok`, change nothing else): 46 tests / 1 failure, and that failure is this slice's own scoping test. The comment now states the measured result and says plainly that the scoping is a DESIGN boundary, not a load-bearing leg under today's corpus. An epic whose thesis is “stop asserting what you did not measure” cannot ship a header comment that does exactly that. 2. `:nxdomain` IS AN ANSWER, NOT A FAULT (commits 90ab9999a + 438495a96) — a REVIEW DECISION superseding the letter of D332. The s7 builder built D332 as written, measured that one fifth of it was wrong, and filed task-3fbfff8c97b50c8f at priority 0 rather than quietly re-deciding. He was right on both counts. Re-measured at review on this host: `:inet.getaddrs` of a non-existent name returns `{:error, :nxdomain}` on BOTH families — which is precisely what a freshly attached, still-propagating domain looks like through the real transport. Shipped literally, D332 would have turned the MOST COMMON waiting state into “we could not check” and stripped its propagation advice: one lie swapped for another, in the very rung the slice existed to make honest. NXDOMAIN means the resolver ANSWERED. Fixed with `@answered_empty [:nxdomain]`, and — the half that matters for the standing test — the DNS test fakes now RETURN nxdomain for a missing record instead of `{:ok, []}`, a shape production never produces. task-3fbfff8c97b50c8f is closed with the ruling, its measurement and its residual gap on the record. 3. THE REAP ALERT CAP IS NOW DRIVEN (commit ab2a6dce5). `@reap_alert_cap 25` decides that the 26th owner in a cluster incident hears nothing by email — a person-facing SUPPRESSION that no fixture crossed. The builder flagged it against himself; the review paid it: a test fails 27 deployments in one sweep and asserts exactly 25 emails plus the suppression log line, with `Registry.reap_alert_cap/0` exposed so the test reads the real constant instead of a copy. Mutation-proved: replacing `Enum.split(alerts, @reap_alert_cap)` with `{alerts, []}` reds exactly that test and nothing else. 4. THE MUTATION ANCHORS IN s1's CONTROL (commit 52a80c7be). `String.prototype.replace` on an anchor that has drifted is a SILENT no-op, and `mutatedRun`'s own `notEqual(out, src)` guard would have been satisfied by the roster mutation alone — so a future refactor of seal-predicate.mjs could have left the floor mutation un-applied and the control passing vacuously. Each anchor is now asserted present before use. Orphans, re-derived with the fixed instrument from a real git tree All three things the wish demanded are quoted, not paraphrased. UTC 2026-08-03T14:43:51Z · tree sha 52a80c7be · RESOLVED REPO ROOT /Volumes/SATECHI/github/barkpark/.claude/worktrees/wf_e660e3b7-480-40. VERDICT-TOKEN: SEAL-PREDICATE NO-SEAL a=FAIL b=PASS c=PASS orphans=75 considering=1 successor=cch-instruments-epic epic=cloud-console-hardening-epic mode=live stubbed=0 waived=0 roster=307 head=52a80c7be Roster 307 {done 195, in_progress 7, open 70, cancelled 34, considering 1}. Residue 78 (live 77, considering 1); forwarded under the successor 0; the three permanent human gates all resolve in-roster. b=PASS here because this is a FULL clone. That is the wave's whole finding restated: the same predicate under console-harness.yml still cannot evaluate clause (b) at all, and nothing in CI has changed about that. D306's two integers, as deltas against wave 27's 117 / roster 343 {189, 119, 34, 1} at c2affd445 — RE-PARENTED OUT OF THIS ROSTER = 36 (343 → 307), CLOSED = +6 done (189 → 195). The 36 does not equal wave 27's 57 hand re-parents, and the reconciliation is stated rather than smoothed: 343 − 57 = 286, and ~21 rows were filed INTO the epic since (wave 28's 8 slice rows plus follow-ups), which lands at 307. Orphans fell 117 → 75. Ledger audit Honest across the board, with no corrections owed. Every built slice is `in_progress`, published, with evidence stamped as the builder worked and the merge-gated criterion left open for the lead — s1 6/7, s3 6/7, s4 7/8 (criterion 4 an honest --miss carrying the refuting numbers), s5 7/8, s6 9/10, s7 10/11, s8 7/8. cch-w28-s2 correctly sits `open` as a deferred round-2 slice. Backlog rows filed by builders are published and open. The ONLY ledger mutation this review made was closing task-3fbfff8c97b50c8f with the nxdomain ruling (criteria 0 and 1 stamped with evidence, criterion 2 recorded as an honest --miss and closed over with a written criteria_override rather than graded by its own closer). Grade: A− WHAT EARNS IT. The wave's headline question was a judgment call between two defensible options and it was decided cleanly, then executed without cheating: #9356 is green in a REAL depth-1 clone with the thing that was red still red-able, the fabrication sentences relocated rather than deleted, and an unanchored regex that discriminated nothing repaired on the way past. Three builders reported measurements that CONTRADICTED their own briefs — the 23-failure prediction, the `returning:` prescription, the nxdomain classification — and each filed the contradiction instead of reinterpreting the criterion into something passable. That is the behaviour this epic exists to produce, and it is why the review caught real defects instead of typos. Four person-facing bodies landed with genuine fail-before proofs, and the cross-slice integration is proved by a 2693/0 full-suite run rather than asserted. WHAT HOLDS IT BACK. The instrument is still structurally blind in the only place it runs automatically — s2 was deferred by the sequenced-rounds law, which is correct process, but it means the epic is still certified by a predicate that can only give a partial verdict in CI, and s3 turned that from an unstated fact into a DOCUMENTED one, which by the wave's own standing test is a sentence, not a fix. The D307 door guard shipped armed but its hard tier can reach almost nothing (no fixture outside its own block carries a `surface` key) and its absence tier is a warn, so the filing law still holds because people are careful, not because a door refuses. s7 shipped a person-facing regression in the most common domain state that only review caught — the builder measured it and escalated correctly, but a wave that ships a decision it knows may be wrong is one review away from shipping it for real. And the domain rail now goes TERMINAL on `unknown` with no re-check affordance, which trades a spinning lie for a frozen truth. What the next wave should take MERGE ORDER, and it matters: round 1 first (#9356, then #9404-#9409, which are file-disjoint and all merge cleanly onto main in one probe). ONLY THEN cch-w28-s2 — it rewrites the same file #9356 rewrites and must mutate the discrimination out of #9356's fail-before controls. cch-w28-s2's hard constraint, armed as a tripwire by s1: HISTORY-UNAVAILABLE must surface as a verdict-token LETTER at exit 1, never a process-level exit-2 INFRA-FAULT. An INFRA-FAULT prints a=UNKNOWN and will red s1's control — deliberately. The REQUIRED `Console gate` depends on guerrilla.barkpark.cloud being reachable (one live spawn, test 56). s3 documented it; nobody has fixed it. A required gate that a third-party host can red is the same defect class as a guard no job runs. The D307 guard's promotion: the `surface` ENUM plus the backfill of open rows, which is what turns the warn tier hard. Until then “every epic row declares a surface” is false and the code says so. The s7 residue: a re-check affordance for a TERMINAL `unknown` rail, and domainRungChip's missing `unknown` arm (task-1daff7bc1bf46ceb) — a screen reader is still told “waiting” one layer below a rung that says it could not be checked. cch-w22-s7's remainder, finished or closed against origin/main's bytes rather than rebuilt. THE WAVE'S OWN SIXTH CLAUSE, PAID TWICE MORE. Wave 27 added it: an instrument pointed at the wrong ROOT reports defect-shaped prose for a condition that is only “I could not look”. Wave 28 found the same shape in two more places — a test bound to an exit code it does not test, which reported a DEFECT for an ENVIRONMENT, and a resolver classification that would have reported “we could not check” for a domain that was simply still propagating. The fix in both cases was the same move: separate the measurement from the absence of one, and say which you have. TUI view Email view

desktop.bodyText: Cloud Console Hardening — wave 28: the instrument fixed “I could not look” at the ROOT and left it standing at the OBJECT — and the environment it runs in is the one place it cannot look Wave 27 was the best-argued wave this epic has run. It refuted both of the lead's headline findings, paid Standing Law 0 by hand with 57 re-parented rows, and proved that the instrument certifying this epic's health was manufacturing false defect reports out of a directory it could not read. Five of its six person-facing slices are on main. One PR is open — #9356 — and it is the one everything else reads through. The lead offered this wave a binary: (a) give the CI job the history the instrument needs, or (b) restructure the red control to assert clause (a) alone. Both are defensible. Both are also incomplete, and this Paper's headline finding is why: measured live, in this session, the WAVE-27-FIXED predicate — the one on #9356, with both of its new refusals armed — still emits six verbatim “commit … is not an ancestor of origin/main” sentences inside a shallow clone. Same disease, same prose, one condition over, in the exact environment the instrument runs in automatically. The wish, and what is already true about each item # THE WISH MEASURED ON ORIGIN/MAIN DFDC31DB9, 2026-08-03T12:35Z 1 #9356 is red because console-harness.yml checks out at fetch-depth:1; decide (a) fetch-depth:0 or (b) restructure the control CONFIRMED and ENLARGED. Depth-1 clone of this repo: origin/main RESOLVES as a ref, but every registered commit is rc 128 “Not a valid object name”. The #9356 predicate passes BOTH of its new refusal legs there and prints six false ancestry sentences at b=FAIL. The binary is false — the fix is the DISCRIMINATION, and it makes both (a) and (b) correct rather than either being a workaround. 2 the D307 door guard is now a wave, not a slice; budget for a `surface` ENUM and a BACKFILL CONFIRMED as filed: cchi-w27-bl-d307-create-time-door-guard, open, 0/5, parent cch-instruments-epic, files [api/lib/barkpark/content/mutations.ex]. apply_mutations is public (mutations.ex:31) and reachable non-admin through MutateController → POST /v1/data/mutate/:dataset (router.ex:2322). The BACKFILL is a ledger write, not code — wave 27 proved the lead's hands are the right instrument for that class. 3 re-derive orphans with the fixed instrument, from a real git tree, quoting UTC stamp + tree sha + RESOLVED ROOT DONE, in this Paper. 2026-08-03T12:35:45Z · tree dfdc31db96b85b66515a1cba3f92a9e9bd81b09b · root <scratchpad>/wt-w28 → NO-SEAL a=FAIL b=PASS c=PASS orphans=57 considering=1 residue=60 (live 59). Wave 27's debrief read 62; five rows have left since. 4 person-facing residue: .preview-url deploy-row siblings; the desktop band; the render-path bypass remainder ONE PREMISE FAILS SMOKE. `.preview-url` is a DOM CHILD of `.deploy-ref` (app.js:10289 emits `<div class="deploy-ref">branch → <a class="preview-url mono">`), and #9357 landed `.deploy-ref { overflow-wrap: anywhere }` at app.css:1847 — whose own committed comment at :1841-1843 says it covers `.preview-url` inside it by inheritance. The next silent clip is NOT there. The desktop band is D323, a measured negative, correctly closed. 5 cch-w22-s7 was split and five criteria stamped by D325; finish or close the remainder against origin/main's bytes D325 is explicit: stamp C6/C7/C8/C12/C14, DROP C9 (its symbol `cuePaints` has zero occurrences under cloud/ and its second anchor file does not exist), close C15/C16 `n/a — split`. This is a LEDGER action for the lead at Decide, not a builder slice. `bp task get cch-w22-s7` returns nothing under that id — resolving the real id is survey work. THE FINDING: wave 27 named the shallow clone in its own fix's header comment, and did not close it seal-predicate.mjs:453 is one line: `try { execFileSync('git', ['-C', REPO, 'merge-base', '--is-ancestor', commit, 'origin/main'], …); } catch { problems.push(`commit ${commit} is not an ancestor of origin/main`); }`. The catch is unconditional. Charter D318 enumerated exactly what it swallows — “not-a-git-repo / no-origin-main / shallow-clone / unknown-sha” — and wave 27's fix closed the first two and wrote the other two into a comment. The wave-27 header comment says it out loud, verbatim: “the ancestry `catch` at the top of `verifyCommit` swallows not-a-git-repo, no origin/main, a shallow clone and an unknown sha into one identical claim about the PRODUCT.” The remedy that follows checks that `.github/workflows/cloud.yml` exists and that `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` resolves to REPO. A depth-1 CI clone satisfies both. Measured live in this session, controlled pair, same live ledger, same minute, nothing varied but the clone: CLONE GIT STATE PREDICATE RESULT full worktree at origin/main not shallow, all objects present origin/main's (pre-#9356) rc 1 · NO-SEAL a=FAIL b=PASS c=PASS orphans=57 `git clone --depth 1` of the same repo is-shallow-repository = true; origin/main RESOLVES; `merge-base --is-ancestor a78fd4e8c origin/main` → rc 128 `fatal: Not a valid object name` #9356's FIXED predicate, both new refusals armed rc 1 · NO-SEAL a=FAIL b=FAIL c=PASS · SIX false “commit … is not an ancestor of origin/main” sentences The instrument that certifies this epic reports “I could not look” as “I found a defect” — the exact sin wave 27 fixed — in the one environment where it runs without a human present. That is not a test failure. It is the sixth standing-test clause, live, on the very instrument that authored it. THE DIRECTION: one disease, two audiences — the console and its instrument both stop asserting what they did not measure This wave has one sentence and it points in both directions at once. A system that could not determine something must say so. It must not substitute a plausible guess, a default, or the negative branch of a two-way test it was unable to run. Pointed at the INSTRUMENT, that sentence resolves the lead's binary by refusing it. Option (a) alone leaves the predicate lying in every other shallow environment — a container, a fork PR, an agent's `--depth 1`, any future job. Option (b) alone leaves standing the fact the lead correctly identified as bigger than the test: that every seal run under this workflow is structurally unable to evaluate clause (b). The answer that pays both is the DISCRIMINATION: teach the git legs to tell rc 1 (“not an ancestor”, an honest answer about the product) from rc 128 / missing object / shallow repository (“I could not look”, an honest answer about the environment). Once the predicate can tell those apart, (b) becomes the correct shape for the control — it asserts the floor it is actually about — and (a) becomes a verified environment declaration rather than a workaround, because a regression back to depth-1 would then produce an honest INFRA-FAULT the job can assert on. Pointed at the PERSON, the same sentence is already sitting in the ledger as open rows. A refused connection is reported as “A network step timed out. Retry usually fixes this.” — the console did not classify the failure, so it guessed, and the guess carries ADVICE. A person switches on “Deployment failed” alerts across email and every chat channel, and the event has zero producers anywhere in the repository — the console tells them they are subscribed to something that cannot arrive. These are not clipping bugs. They are the epic's founding vision, in its purest form, and they are the wave's person bodies. What the finished wave looks like #9356 is MERGED, first and alone, and it merged because its control was restructured to assert clause (a) — the floor it exists to test — not because anything red was weakened. Nothing about the depth-1 environment changed to get it green. The seal predicate has a THIRD refusal in the same discipline as its first two: HISTORY-UNAVAILABLE. Run it in a shallow clone and it exits 2 with a named code and zero invented findings, exactly as it now does in a git-archive extraction. Mutation-proved with a REAL `git clone --depth 1`, not a stub — the wave-27 lesson is that stubbing the leg only moves the failure. console-harness.yml stops being an environment the instrument cannot work in. The seal job declares the history it needs, and a self-check reds if that declaration silently reverts — a guard on the guard's environment, which is the class of defect this whole wave is about. The D307 door guard is ARMED, not ruled on for a third wave. `surface` becomes an enum; the open rows are backfilled BY THE LEAD'S HAND at Decide (wave 27 proved that pattern with 57 re-parents); the fence widening is a numbered charter decision written before a builder touches mutations.ex; and the refusal is scoped to this epic's parent_id so its blast radius is this epic, not the whole task system. At least four — target five — slices where a PERSON is misinformed or cannot reach a control, led by the two rows where the console gives a confident wrong answer to a question it never asked. What this wave deliberately does NOT do It does not spend a slice on `.preview-url`. That premise failed smoke: #9357 already covers it by inheritance and the committed CSS comment says so. Booking it would be paying twice for one fix. It does not chase orphans to zero. 57 is stated with all three provenance facts and repaid only by rows that leave honestly. Wave 27 already made the largest Law-0 payment in the epic's history; a wave spent on ledger hygiene is the disease the charter names at waves 9/10/11. It does not touch .github/required-checks.json, and it registers nothing. The direction debate: three candidates, argued, one committed Rival A — “Finish the instrument, build the door” (the wish read literally) Take the lead's binary, pick one leg, and spend the rest of the wave on the D307 door guard as a full multi-slice build: the `surface` enum, the backfill, the fence ruling, the refusal, the mutation proof. Clean, obedient, and it retires the highest-leverage row in the epic. WHY IT LOSES. Three counts. First, arithmetic: four instrument slices against a floor of four person bodies means eight slices minimum, and this epic's own history says a wave that spends 4-of-6 on instruments moves the row count the wrong way (waves 9/10/11: +11, +16, +7). Second, the door guard's dependency chain — enum → backfill → fence ruling → refusal — is SERIAL and cannot fan out to parallel builders, so it converts a fan-out wave into a queue. Third and worst, it accepts the false binary. Picking (a) or (b) at speed leaves the predicate lying in every shallow environment that is not this one workflow, and this Paper has now proved live that such an environment exists and that the epic's own instrument is in it. Rival B — “Pay Law 0 to zero and drive at the seal” orphans is 57 and a=FAIL is the only clause failing. Spend the wave closing, forwarding and adjudicating residue — including the cch-w22-s7 split D325 already ruled — and get the epic within sight of an honest SEAL. WHY IT LOSES. It is the epic's stated disease wearing a productivity costume. The charter's vision is that the CONSOLE stops lying; a wave with zero person bodies fails the ratio outright and would be the fourth restatement of a law rather than a payment of it. It also mistakes the seal for the goal — D318 proved the predicate could SEAL an epic that does not exist, which means a falling orphan count was never the thing worth optimising. HARVESTED ANYWAY: this Paper quotes the reading with all three provenance facts, and the cch-w22-s7 adjudication is booked as a Decide-phase ledger action for the lead, costing zero builders. Rival C — “One disease, two audiences” — COMMITTED Two instrument slices that pay the environment question properly plus the discrimination that generalises it; one door-guard slice made buildable by moving its backfill dependency onto the lead's hands at Decide; and four-to-five person bodies chosen so that at least two of them are literally the same defect the instrument has — a system asserting a fact it did not measure. WHY IT WINS. It is the only candidate where the instrument work and the person work are the SAME argument, which means the wave's finding transfers: the sentence that fixes the seal predicate is the sentence a builder applies to `connection refused`. D306's two integers, as deltas against wave 27's 117 / roster 343 {189, 119, 34, 1} at c2affd445 — RE-PARENTED OUT OF THIS ROSTER = 36 (343 → 307), CLOSED = +6 done (189 → 195). The 36 does not equal wave 27's 57 hand re-parents, and the reconciliation is stated rather than smoothed: 343 − 57 = 286, and ~21 rows were filed INTO the epic since (wave 28's 8 slice rows plus follow-ups), which lands at 307. Orphans fell 117 → 75. Ledger audit Honest across the board, with no corrections owed. Every built slice is `in_progress`, published, with evidence stamped as the builder worked and the merge-gated criterion left open for the lead — s1 6/7, s3 6/7, s4 7/8 (criterion 4 an honest --miss carrying the refuting numbers), s5 7/8, s6 9/10, s7 10/11, s8 7/8. cch-w28-s2 correctly sits `open` as a deferred round-2 slice. Backlog rows filed by builders are published and open. The ONLY ledger mutation this review made was closing task-3fbfff8c97b50c8f with the nxdomain ruling (criteria 0 and 1 stamped with evidence, criterion 2 recorded as an honest --miss and closed over with a written criteria_override rather than graded by its own closer). Grade: A− WHAT EARNS IT. The wave's headline question was a judgment call between two defensible options and it was decided cleanly, then executed without cheating: #9356 is green in a REAL depth-1 clone with the thing that was red still red-able, the fabrication sentences relocated rather than deleted, and an unanchored regex that discriminated nothing repaired on the way past. Three builders reported measurements that CONTRADICTED their own briefs — the 23-failure prediction, the `returning:` prescription, the nxdomain classification — and each filed the contradiction instead of reinterpreting the criterion into something passable. That is the behaviour this epic exists to produce, and it is why the review caught real defects instead of typos. Four person-facing bodies landed with genuine fail-before proofs, and the cross-slice integration is proved by a 2693/0 full-suite run rather than asserted. WHAT HOLDS IT BACK. The instrument is still structurally blind in the only place it runs automatically — s2 was deferred by the sequenced-rounds law, which is correct process, but it means the epic is still certified by a predicate that can only give a partial verdict in CI, and s3 turned that from an unstated fact into a DOCUMENTED one, which by the wave's own standing test is a sentence, not a fix. The D307 door guard shipped armed but its hard tier can reach almost nothing (no fixture outside its own block carries a `surface` key) and its absence tier is a warn, so the filing law still holds because people are careful, not because a door refuses. s7 shipped a person-facing regression in the most common domain state that only review caught — the builder measured it and escalated correctly, but a wave that ships a decision it knows may be wrong is one review away from shipping it for real. And the domain rail now goes TERMINAL on `unknown` with no re-check affordance, which trades a spinning lie for a frozen truth. What the next wave should take MERGE ORDER, and it matters: round 1 first (#9356, then #9404-#9409, which are file-disjoint and all merge cleanly onto main in one probe). ONLY THEN cch-w28-s2 — it rewrites the same file #9356 rewrites and must mutate the discrimination out of #9356's fail-before controls. cch-w28-s2's hard constraint, armed as a tripwire by s1: HISTORY-UNAVAILABLE must surface as a verdict-token LETTER at exit 1, never a process-level exit-2 INFRA-FAULT. An INFRA-FAULT prints a=UNKNOWN and will red s1's control — deliberately. The REQUIRED `Console gate` depends on guerrilla.barkpark.cloud being reachable (one live spawn, test 56). s3 documented it; nobody has fixed it. A required gate that a third-party host can red is the same defect class as a guard no job runs. The D307 guard's promotion: the `surface` ENUM plus the backfill of open rows, which is what turns the warn tier hard. Until then “every epic row declares a surface” is false and the code says so. The s7 residue: a re-check affordance for a TERMINAL `unknown` rail, and domainRungChip's missing `unknown` arm (task-1daff7bc1bf46ceb) — a screen reader is still told “waiting” one layer below a rung that says it could not be checked. cch-w22-s7's remainder, finished or closed against origin/main's bytes rather than rebuilt. THE WAVE'S OWN SIXTH CLAUSE, PAID TWICE MORE. Wave 27 added it: an instrument pointed at the wrong ROOT reports defect-shaped prose for a condition that is only “I could not look”. Wave 28 found the same shape in two more places — a test bound to an exit code it does not test, which reported a DEFECT for an ENVIRONMENT, and a resolver classification that would have reported “we could not check” for a domain that was simply still propagating. The fix in both cases was the same move: separate the measurement from the absence of one, and say which you have. TUI view Email view

reflow200.bodyText: Cloud Console Hardening — wave 28: the instrument fixed “I could not look” at the ROOT and left it standing at the OBJECT — and the environment it runs in is the one place it cannot look Wave 27 was the best-argued wave this epic has run. It refuted both of the lead's headline findings, paid Standing Law 0 by hand with 57 re-parented rows, and proved that the instrument certifying this epic's health was manufacturing false defect reports out of a directory it could not read. Five of its six person-facing slices are on main. One PR is open — #9356 — and it is the one everything else reads through. The lead offered this wave a binary: (a) give the CI job the history the instrument needs, or (b) restructure the red control to assert clause (a) alone. Both are defensible. Both are also incomplete, and this Paper's headline finding is why: measured live, in this session, the WAVE-27-FIXED predicate — the one on #9356, with both of its new refusals armed — still emits six verbatim “commit … is not an ancestor of origin/main” sentences inside a shallow clone. Same disease, same prose, one condition over, in the exact environment the instrument runs in automatically. The wish, and what is already true about each item # THE WISH MEASURED ON ORIGIN/MAIN DFDC31DB9, 2026-08-03T12:35Z 1 #9356 is red because console-harness.yml checks out at fetch-depth:1; decide (a) fetch-depth:0 or (b) restructure the control CONFIRMED and ENLARGED. Depth-1 clone of this repo: origin/main RESOLVES as a ref, but every registered commit is rc 128 “Not a valid object name”. The #9356 predicate passes BOTH of its new refusal legs there and prints six false ancestry sentences at b=FAIL. The binary is false — the fix is the DISCRIMINATION, and it makes both (a) and (b) correct rather than either being a workaround. 2 the D307 door guard is now a wave, not a slice; budget for a `surface` ENUM and a BACKFILL CONFIRMED as filed: cchi-w27-bl-d307-create-time-door-guard, open, 0/5, parent cch-instruments-epic, files [api/lib/barkpark/content/mutations.ex]. apply_mutations is public (mutations.ex:31) and reachable non-admin through MutateController → POST /v1/data/mutate/:dataset (router.ex:2322). The BACKFILL is a ledger write, not code — wave 27 proved the lead's hands are the right instrument for that class. 3 re-derive orphans with the fixed instrument, from a real git tree, quoting UTC stamp + tree sha + RESOLVED ROOT DONE, in this Paper. 2026-08-03T12:35:45Z · tree dfdc31db96b85b66515a1cba3f92a9e9bd81b09b · root <scratchpad>/wt-w28 → NO-SEAL a=FAIL b=PASS c=PASS orphans=57 considering=1 residue=60 (live 59). Wave 27's debrief read 62; five rows have left since. 4 person-facing residue: .preview-url deploy-row siblings; the desktop band; the render-path bypass remainder ONE PREMISE FAILS SMOKE. `.preview-url` is a DOM CHILD of `.deploy-ref` (app.js:10289 emits `<div class="deploy-ref">branch → <a class="preview-url mono">`), and #9357 landed `.deploy-ref { overflow-wrap: anywhere }` at app.css:1847 — whose own committed comment at :1841-1843 says it covers `.preview-url` inside it by inheritance. ONLY THEN cch-w28-s2 — it rewrites the same file #9356 rewrites and must mutate the discrimination out of #9356's fail-before controls. cch-w28-s2's hard constraint, armed as a tripwire by s1: HISTORY-UNAVAILABLE must surface as a verdict-token LETTER at exit 1, never a process-level exit-2 INFRA-FAULT. An INFRA-FAULT prints a=UNKNOWN and will red s1's control — deliberately. The REQUIRED `Console gate` depends on guerrilla.barkpark.cloud being reachable (one live spawn, test 56). s3 documented it; nobody has fixed it. A required gate that a third-party host can red is the same defect class as a guard no job runs. The D307 guard's promotion: the `surface` ENUM plus the backfill of open rows, which is what turns the warn tier hard. Until then “every epic row declares a surface” is false and the code says so. The s7 residue: a re-check affordance for a TERMINAL `unknown` rail, and domainRungChip's missing `unknown` arm (task-1daff7bc1bf46ceb) — a screen reader is still told “waiting” one layer below a rung that says it could not be checked. cch-w22-s7's remainder, finished or closed against origin/main's bytes rather than rebuilt. THE WAVE'S OWN SIXTH CLAUSE, PAID TWICE MORE. Wave 27 added it: an instrument pointed at the wrong ROOT reports defect-shaped prose for a condition that is only “I could not look”. Wave 28 found the same shape in two more places — a test bound to an exit code it does not test, which reported a DEFECT for an ENVIRONMENT, and a resolver classification that would have reported “we could not check” for a domain that was simply still propagating. The fix in both cases was the same move: separate the measurement from the absence of one, and say which you have. TUI view Email view

320.bodyText: PDS wave 44 - recover wave 43's unlanded work, re-derive its one security claim, and make the price column RUN STRATEGIZE COMPLETE - the survey fleet is flying. PREMISE SMOKE RUN IN-PROCESS against `git show origin/main:<path>` at origin/main head c2affd445, never the primary checkout (300+ commits behind, 220 foreign modified files). VERIFIED: the charter on origin/main tops out at PDS-D632 - D633-D642 are NOT on main, they live only on PR #9312, so NO builder may carry a D633+ citation until that PR lands. VERIFIED: PDS-D578 exists at charter:11830 and says verbatim 'PROVEN-BACKED is 23/252 = 9.1%' - D640's citation of it COVERS what it is cited for. VERIFIED: api/lib/barkpark_web/studio/caps.ex on origin/main has write_capable?/2 at :283 with `Map.get(caps, :write) == true -> true` as the FIRST cond arm and `restricted?(assigns) -> false` as the SECOND, and restricted?/1 at :295 already contains `share_access == :read` - the ORDER defect #9332 claims is REAL AT SOURCE. Reachability is not yet proven and is survey question 1. VERIFIED: scripts/elixir-path-escape-check.sh is the SINGLE source of truth for ELIXIR_TEST_ONLY_PATHS - the name appears in NO workflow yml; elixir.yml consumes it through --print-set / --match. #9333 edits the right file. VERIFIED on origin/main: scripts/pds-ledger-census_test.sh, scripts/pds-live-hetzner-placement-group.sh, scripts/pds-scratch-target_test.sh, scripts/pds-charter-ledger-sweep.sh and api/test/barkpark/pds_residue_lens_test.exs all exist. VERIFIED: LiveScope.authorize_read/4 is a PRIVATE function at api/lib/barkpark_web/live_scope.ex:114, called from :88 - the non-admin reachability story runs through LiveScope.assign_scope, so the CALLER is what a verifier must pin. The wish, and the four things it asks for Wave 43 died mid-flight on a weekly account limit, not on a defect. It completed 36 of 41 agents, produced ten charter decisions (PDS-D633-D642), and pushed NOTHING. The lead recovered four branches out of their worktrees by hand and opened #9332, #9333, #9334, #9335 at 12:15 today. Wave 43's reviewer never ran; its debrief was never written. Those four PRs are UNREVIEWED BY ANYONE, and their commit messages are an author's own account of their own work. The wish asks for four things: (1) re-derive #9332's live write bypass from source before trusting a word of it; (2) verify the other three the same way; (3) confirm PDS-D633's measurement law - the in-BEAM meter is blind to port children and errs in the one direction a price column must not - and ship its blind-spot sentence in the meter's own moduledoc AND printed output; (4) finish the price column: N of 19 instruments under a required gate, every remaining refusal carrying a measured price, a named environment, or NOT-YET-BUILT. REFUTATION - the first one, and it is in the wish's own item 4 The wish states the price column's reason vocabulary is 'exactly three reasons: PRICE, ENVIRONMENT, NOT-YET-BUILT' and that 'the fence' is not an available answer. Wave 43's own PDS-D637 - which the wish is paraphrasing - found by RUN that three is not enough. It names FIVE classes: PRICE, ENVIRONMENT, NOT-YET-BUILT, plus CONTENT-RED (pds-charter-ledger-sweep.sh --selftest is rc=1 on main today at 2.36s user, refusing because an UNRESOLVED-CLAIM ARRIVAL is unadjudicated - neither a price nor an environment) and RED-BY-DESIGN / REPORTER (pds-record-parity.sh's live axis B exits 1 on 59 leaf rows, 48 of them belonging to twelve OTHER epics that never consented to the instrument; the arm is a reporter and must never carry a required check name). A related sixth, HUMAN-GATE, governs the sheet-grid harness, whose own workflow header says it only gates once a human registers it as a required check. The wish also says pds-record-parity.sh --selftest exits rc=3 with 'unknown argument' and calls that an ENVIRONMENT blocker. Wave 43 did not accept that framing - it walked a DIFFERENT door. #9333 gates scripts/pds-record-parity.test.sh, the instrument's own hermetic two-sided mutation harness (76 checks, zero of which read a live ledger row), at 1.30-1.47s user - the cheapest door in the inventory. So record-parity is not an ENVIRONMENT refusal; its HARNESS is a THROUGH and its LIVE arm is RED-BY-DESIGN. The wish's item 4 is the tenth consecutive dispatch this epic has refuted from the artifact, and it is refuted in the direction of GOOD NEWS. Direction - three movements, and the third is what makes this a wave and not a cleanup The finished experience: at the end of wave 44 a cold reader runs ONE command and gets the epic's honesty column back COMPUTED rather than quoted - every scripts/pds-* instrument, its gate status derived from the two things that actually make a door (a test file that shells it, and a matching ELIXIR_TEST_ONLY_PATHS line), its refusal class, and its price in the unit PDS-D633 says is legal. A new pds-* script arrives as an UNDISPOSED row and the thing goes red. A door that quietly stops running goes red. And the number that appears in the charter next wave is a number nobody typed. Movement 1 - LAND THE RECOVERED WORK, WITH INDEPENDENCE THAT IS REAL Charter #9312 merges FIRST and alone, because until it does every D633+ citation a builder would carry points at nothing on origin/main. Then the four slice PRs, each with an independent re-derivation that does NOT read the branch's own test as its oracle. #9332 gets the full treatment: the source-level order defect is already confirmed (cond arm 1 = caps.write, arm 2 = restricted?, and restricted? already contains share_access == :read), so the open question is REACHABILITY - can a real signed-in NON-MEMBER, through a real non-admin route, hold share_access: :read and caps.write == true simultaneously? That is the whole claim, and it must be re-derived through LiveScope.assign_scope -> authorize_read/4, not asserted from a fixture the branch authored. One suspected defect the wave carries in already, found while reading the diff and NOT yet proven: #9332's membership collapse routes through loadable_principal?/1, which accepts only %ApiToken{} and %User{}. Tenancy.Auth.authorize/3 on origin/main has a THIRD clause at :200 for %Barkpark.Content.CallerContext{}. If a socket's principals list can ever carry a CallerContext, the collapse silently drops a principal that authorize/3 would have decided - a behaviour change dressed as a round-trip saving, in the same slice as a security fix. Survey question 3 exists to settle it before a builder inherits it. Movement 2 - FINISH WHAT WAVE 43 PRICED Two of wave 43's six slices never got a builder at all. The LiveView residual 32-fold (PDS-D639: one missing lvs_walk/3 clause takes RESIDUAL 32 -> 0 and makes the headline deny fraction WORSE, 70.6% -> 60.9%, which is the strongest available evidence it is real) is unbuilt - no branch exists for it. The judgment-coverage ladder (PDS-D640: PROVEN-BACKED is 23 routed-write MEMBERS as an Enum.count over a MapSet.union/2, never an addition, with OVERLAP printed beside it) is its round-2 dependent and has had its numbers die three times. Both ship this wave, the fold first, with D639's three named obligations non-negotiable - especially (a), the plugin fixture, because without it the new clause is STRUCTURALLY unexercised and the class does not descend from its substitution. And the door walks D637 explicitly deferred to wave 44: pds-ledger-census_test.sh (PRICE ~20-23s, viable, python3 confirmed present on the Elixir runner by wave 43's own three-leg ledger note) and the best unexamined candidate, pds-live-hetzner-placement-group.sh --selftest-offline, NOT-YET-MEASURED. Each measured by the ONLY legal method: an OS meter around a SHELL, never from inside a BEAM parent. Movement 3 - THE DOOR CENSUS: the price column stops being prose This is the bold one. PDS-D637's column is, today, forty lines of charter prose sitting on an unmerged PR - and PDS-D633's own closing sentence is that a number from a meter must live in the instrument's moduledoc and printed output, NEVER in prose a copy-paste can drop. The column violates the law that produced it. Wave 44 turns it into an instrument: enumerate scripts/pds-*.{sh,exs} for the denominator; for each row DERIVE the gate status from two independent legs - leg A, a '../../../scripts/...' string literal in an api/test/** file that actually shells it; leg B, that same path present in elixir-path-escape-check.sh's declared set - and report THROUGH only when BOTH hold. One leg without the other is exactly the wave-42 #9290/#9292 defect (Test skipped while Elixir gate passed in 3s on the skip shim), and this makes that defect impossible to reintroduce quietly rather than merely remembered. Every non-THROUGH row carries a class from D637's FIVE (not three) and, for PRICE rows, a figure with the meter named. An instrument with no disposition is UNDISPOSED and the census exits non-zero - the same fail-closed shape the receipt census already uses. It prints D633's blind-spot sentence in its own output. And it rides its own door: it is an instrument, so it gets a test file and a path-set line like every other, which is the self-referential proof that the derivation works. The wave plan, provisionally # MOVEMENT WHY NOW STATE TODAY 0 merge charter #9312 alone, first D633-D642 are not on origin/main; every downstream citation is a phantom until it lands PR open, BLOCKED 1 independently re-derive + land #9332 (caps read-only share write bypass + derive collapse) a live authorization bypass reviewed by nobody; source-level order defect already confirmed PR open, unreviewed 2 independently re-derive + land #9333 (census + record-parity doors, 1 -> 3 of 19) carries the ELIXIR_TEST_ONLY_PATHS lesson wave 42 lost PR open, unreviewed 3 independently re-derive + land #9334 (ledger-lapse expiry arm, three shapes) ledger lapse is endemic; the lesson has been a paragraph in three debriefs PR open, unreviewed 4 independently re-derive + land #9335 (sheet-grid read mode) the one standing user-facing harm: a selection frozen at A1 that nothing can move PR open, unreviewed 5 BUILD the LiveView residual 32-fold (D639) with its three obligations never got a builder; blocks the ladder unbuilt, no branch 6 BUILD the judgment-coverage ladder (D640) after the fold merges numbers dead three times; union not addition deferred round 2 7 BUILD the DOOR CENSUS - the price column as a running instrument the honesty column violates the law that produced it new this wave 8 walk two more doors: pds-ledger-census_test.sh, pds-live-hetzner-placement-group.sh D637 named both for wave 44 by number and by name new this wave Direction debate - the rivals, and why this one won Rival A - RECOVERY ONLY Spend the whole wave making wave 43's four branches independently bulletproof and merged, plus the charter, and ship nothing new. The case for it is strong and honest: an unreviewed authorization change is the single riskiest object in the repo right now, and a wave that merges it carelessly while chasing new capability has failed at the only thing that mattered. It was rejected because it under-uses the wave, not because it is wrong: four PRs of independent re-derivation is roughly one round, and the fold plus the ladder are DESIGNED work with their obligations already derived by run - leaving them unbuilt for a second consecutive wave is how wave 43's best output rots. Rival A's real contribution survives: movement 1 goes first, alone, and no slice PR merges on its own author's oracle. Rival B - ADVANCE ONLY Treat the four branches as inherited fact, merge them on their green, and spend the wave taking the door from 3 of 19 to 6 or 7. Rejected outright: it is precisely the move the wish forbids, and the epic's own law forbids it too. A commit message is an exit code with better prose. Merging #9332 on its own test's word is 'a gate lies when its green costs nothing to produce', committed by the wave that coined the sentence. Rival C - THE DOOR CENSUS (winner, as movement 3 of three) The winning insight is that the epic has spent four waves arguing about a column it has never computed. Every wave restates the roster, re-prices some rows, and writes the total into the charter by hand - and PDS-D636 records that the census itself carries a FALSE SENTENCE about its own gating on main today. That is the exact failure mode this epic exists to end, committed by the epic, about the epic. Making the column an instrument is the epic's own law turned inward one more notch, and it is cheap: the derivation is two greps over files that already exist, and the prior art is already on main (api/test/barkpark/pds_residue_lens_test.exs). The sharpest attack on the winner, and how the wave absorbs it THE ATTACK: the door census is a THIRD census. This epic already has a receipt census, a residue lens, a ledger census, a record-parity arm and a charter-ledger sweep - nineteen instruments, three of which run anywhere. Building a twentieth instrument to count the nineteen is the purest possible instance of an epic measuring itself instead of shipping. And it will be WRONG on day one: leg A ('a test file shells it') has at least three encodings in the repo already (System.cmd with a module attribute, Code.require_file, a bare relative path), so a naive derivation will under-count and print a number LOWER than the truth - a different lie, in a friendlier direction. HOW THE WAVE ABSORBS IT. First, the door census is movement THREE of three - it ships only if movements 1 and 2 are honest, and the wave is graded on the security fix and the merges regardless. Second, the under-count objection becomes the instrument's design: the census is FAIL-CLOSED on ambiguity - a pds-* script it cannot dispose is UNDISPOSED and reds, and a test-side reference it cannot classify is an ERROR, never a silent 'not gated'. That makes the day-one wrongness LOUD instead of quiet, and the surveyors are tasked (question 4) with enumerating every encoding of leg A that exists on main before a builder writes a regex. Third, if the survey shows the derivation cannot be made honest cheaply, the fallback is smaller and still real: a self-check that the two legs AGREE for every already-gated instrument - which alone would have caught #9290 and #9292. The survey plan - 20 assignments, and what each one changes Width is the point. Each surveyor is one Opus at medium effort; the digest distils. Every load-bearing assumption in the direction above appears below as a question, including the ones that would kill it. Round-1 file sets are disjoint - the census, the escape-check, shared/paper.ex and the palette harness are each owned by exactly one slice. # Slice Task id Round Model Gate 1 The grant-graded doc escalation is closed at the door it rides pds-w44-grant-door-narrowing 1 fable (remapped to opus - fable unavailable) CC=clang mix test on the new LiveView test + the studio directory, rc captured to a variable 2 Residual-32 fold recovered + D605's unit + D633's blind spot IN the instrument pds-w44-census-fold-and-blindspot 1 fable (remapped) elixir scripts/pds-elixir-receipt-census.exs and its --selftest, both rc=0 3 The door census: the price column becomes an instrument pds-w44-door-census-instrument 1 fable (remapped) bash scripts/pds-door-census.sh + bash scripts/elixir-path-escape-check.sh --check + CC=clang mix test the new rider 4 The palette harness repaired against generated tokens pds-w44-palette-harness-repair 1 opus node each __*.test.mjs in api/assets/sheet-grid, every rc captured and zero 5 The judgment-coverage ladder: PROVEN-BACKED 23 as a union pds-w44-judgment-coverage-ladder 2 (after 2) opus elixir census + --selftest + the doc byte-budget check 6 The hetzner offline arm becomes the next door pds-w44-hetzner-offline-door 2 (after 3) opus CC=clang mix test the new rider + escape-check --check at rc=0 7 The charter sweep adjudicated and its fail-open closed pds-w44-charter-sweep-adjudication 2 (after THIS charter merges) opus bash scripts/pds-charter-ledger-sweep.sh and --selftest, both rc=0 HIGH-FLIP-RISK, declared, and the line is in each task's own brief so the reviewer reads it there: SLICE 1 - whether the grant grade's narrowing belongs in the door or the gate, and whether narrowing it denies a legitimate grantee. This is an authorization judgment on a bypass that is LIVE ON MAIN, and it is the species that flipped twice in wave 43. SLICE 3 - whether leg A's three predicates admit a fraudulent THROUGH; the comment mutation is the oracle, and wave 44's own prototype PASSED IT. Both warrant a genuinely independent second reviewer before merge. This workflow spawns one reviewer, so that dispatch is a manual lead step - review's job is to NAME when independence is owed. BACKLOG FILED NOW, six published child rows, so the ledger shows the future: pds-w44-bl-ledger-census-door-repriced, pds-w44-bl-ops-controller-apply-ops-ungated, pds-w44-bl-vacuous-reader-toggle-oracle, pds-w44-bl-sheetgrid-write-landing-unproven, pds-w44-bl-stranded-work-is-invisible-to-git-grep, pds-w44-bl-citation-precedes-merge-check. THE WAVE'S OWN LAW, TURNED ON ITSELF. A gate lies when its green costs nothing to produce - and this wave found that sentence violated three times by the epic that coined it: #9334's zero-second Test shim, the two-leg agreement check that cannot red, and the charter sweep's second read that prints CONFIRMED while its read failed. Wave 44's grade rests on slices 1 and 2, not on the door count. DEBRIEF - wave 44 reviewed, 4 PRs pushed, grade A- Every branch this wave produced is on origin with a PR open. Nothing is merged - the lead merges. Three slices were handed to review as built and green; a FOURTH was found stranded, fully built and fully gated, with zero commits on its branch, and was recovered here. What shipped, per slice TASK FINAL BRANCH PR GATE RE-RUN ON THE FINAL STATE VERDICT pds-w44-grant-door-narrowing loop-epic/a-doc-scoped-write-grant-stops-writing-a-0-r #9377 slice test rc=0, 5 tests 0 failures; studio suite rc=0, 1547 tests 0 failures STRONG. The bypass is real and the fix is what closes it - proven by the reviewer's OWN mutation, not the builder's: neutering grant_target_denied?/3 gives rc=2 with two failures printing left: %{"amount" => "ESCALATED"} read back from the store. pds-w44-census-fold-and-blindspot loop-epic/the-residual-32-gets-judged-and-the-mete-1 #9378 census rc=0, RESIDUAL 0/322, sum 322 == population 322, CENSUS OK STRONG. A/B re-derived independently: 32 -> 0, reachable_unconditional 194 -> 225, DENIES numerator HELD at 137, so the headline fraction gets WORSE (70.6% -> 60.9%). That is a fold, not a rubber stamp. pds-w44-palette-harness-repair loop-epic/the-sheet-grid-palette-harness-stops-com-3-r #9379 all four __*.test.mjs rc=0; palette reports 18 contrast checks STRONG, plus two reviewer fixes. The 4-week red was a harness attribution bug, never a WCAG defect - and the bug lied in BOTH directions (#14532d is invisible in dark mode at 2.18:1 and the old harness would have PASSED it at 9.11:1 vs white). pds-w44-door-census-instrument loop-epic/the-price-column-stops-being-charter-pro-2-r #9380 door-census rc=0 (UNDISPOSED 0 of 20, ERRORS 0); --selftest rc=0 (8 PASS / 0 FAIL); escape-check rc=0; rider rc=0 (8 tests) RECOVERED BY REVIEW, not builder-delivered. Complete and green - it simply never got committed. One pair of eyes on a 37 KB shell instrument; an independent second reviewer is owed. What the review FOUND that the wave did not report PDS-D653 - A TASK CAN BE 11/12 STAMPED AND ITS BRANCH EMPTY. pds-w44-door-census-instrument stamped eleven criteria with real run evidence, its now-line read 'committing: ... branching loop-epic/the-price-column-stops-being-charter-pro-2', and git diff origin/main...that-branch is EMPTY. It was in NEITHER the built handoff nor the not-green list. The rule this buys: the LEDGER is the sweep index, not the handoff - diff every wave task's stated branch against origin/main and treat an empty diff as STRANDED, because a report cannot describe the builder that stopped before writing it. PDS-D654 - A GATE THAT DOES NOT TRIGGER ON ITS OWN SUBJECT IS GREEN FOR FREE. sheet-grid-js.yml runs a harness that parses root.html.heex, presence_state.ex and tokens_gen.ex, and triggered on NONE of them - so the contrast gate never ran on a PR that changed a hue, a background token, or the presence palette. D633's law in its cheapest form yet: no skip shim, no vacuous assertion, just a paths: list that omits the subject. Repaired in #9379. PDS-D655 - TWO INSTRUMENTS SHIPPED CONTRADICTORY PROSE ABOUT THE SAME FINDING, IN THE SAME WAVE. pds-door-census.sh printed the meter blindness as a 236x real/user RATIO; pds-elixir-receipt-census.exs refuted exactly that on its own runs (113x, then 123x, for the SAME fan-out, because real counts WAITING). Reconciled in review onto the load-independent leaf-metered FLOOR. The rule: when a finding ships inside more than one instrument, ONE owns the sentence and the others cite it - the same argument the census's own @blind_spot attribute makes, one level up. A FLAKE, FILED RATHER THAN SWALLOWED. The first full studio-suite run scored 1 failure in ChatRenderGoldenTest's sidebar byte-lock (golden 6554 bytes, region 6554 bytes, first diff at 723 - a same-length CONTENT SWAP). It passes in isolation and passed on re-run of the identical tree. Filed as task-441f5a5669e0ab6b. A golden that reds only sometimes trains reviewers to re-run until green, which is this epic's own defect class. THE HOST WAS NOT QUIET, AND THAT PROVED D605 BY ACCIDENT. The reviewer's census read user cpu 17330 ms against wall clock 95801 ms on a box carrying 24 stray busy-loop processes four days old. The wall figure is the LOAD; the CPU figure is the CODE. Dated corrections to earlier sections of this Paper 2026-08-03, correcting the Direction section's 'Charter #9312 merges FIRST and alone': INVERTED IN PRACTICE. #9332/#9333/#9334 merged at 10:49-10:50Z and the charter at 11:29:57Z - forty minutes after the code citing it. Already recorded as PDS-D643; noted here so a reader of the Direction section does not carry the plan as the outcome. 2026-08-03, correcting 'The wave plan - 7 slices, 4 in round 1': FOUR round-1 slices were dispatched and only THREE reached review as built. The fourth (pds-w44-door-census-instrument) completed its work and its gate and died before committing; it is delivered by this review as #9380. The plan's round-1 count is right; its delivery path is not what the plan describes. 2026-08-03, on the wish's item 3 ('measured at 236x'): REFUTED BY THE ARTIFACT, and the refutation is now the shipped sentence in BOTH instruments. real/user is load-dependent; the load-independent statement is the DIRECTION plus a leaf-metered floor. Ledger audit All four slice tasks are lifecycle in_progress with merge-gated criteria left OPEN for the lead - correct, none closed early. Evidence was stamped AS THE BUILDERS WORKED, not batched: each carries per-criterion evidence quoting run output, and two carry honest --miss records rather than fabricated flips (pds-w44-census-fold-and-blindspot criterion 8, the lv_verdict/5 cond reorder; pds-w44-palette-harness-repair criterion 7, the PR body a builder cannot write because builders do not push). ONE LEDGER LIE CORRECTED: pds-w44-door-census-instrument's claim now-line implied a committed branch that does not exist. A review_status field now records the correction, the recovery, and the re-run gate; re-published and read back. Each of the other three tasks gained a review_status naming its final branch, its PR, and which gate legs the REVIEWER re-ran (as distinct from which the builder claimed). No task outside this wave was mutated. One NEW task was filed and published: task-441f5a5669e0ab6b (the golden byte-lock flake), parented to the epic. Grade - A- EARNED, not awarded. What is genuinely strong: three of four slices closed a defect that was REAL and proved it by substitution rather than by reading, and every one of them refuted part of its own brief from the artifact - the palette slice found a THIRD stale coupling nobody had priced (--fg-muted was matched for an hsl() both themes author as var(--muted-text), so that check had found zero declarations and could never have run), and the census slice refused the ratio its dispatch demanded. The security slice is the wave's best work: it declined the obvious fix (widening Caps.write_capable?/2, which is shared with the SheetGrid prop and has no target), declined the obvious predicate (Access.admits_desk?/3, whose type/doc_id overwrite IS the bug), and carries a positive control proving a legitimate grantee still writes. What falls short. (1) A whole slice died between its last stamp and its first commit and NOTHING in the wave's own reporting said so - it took a branch-vs-ledger diff to find a finished instrument one cycle away from deletion. That is the sixth consecutive wave to strand built work, and it is the single reason this is not an A. (2) Two instruments shipped contradictory prose about the same finding in the same wave - a coherence failure the wave had every opportunity to catch, since one slice explicitly refuted the other's figure in its own commit message. (3) The security slice's shipped non-vacuity test is a local constant-false STUB, not the reverted arm; the real revert was run and recorded in the stamp, but the artifact that MERGES cannot reproduce it - the reviewer had to re-run the mutation by hand to confirm. (4) Coverage is honestly partial and says so: paper_ops/2 and document_op/2 carry the new arm but are proven by READING, and the census's ExUnit rider was never run locally. No bloat: 489 lines for the security slice including a 361-line test, 333 for the census fold, 86 for the palette repair. Nothing was redesigned; the reviewer's edits are two latent-hazard closures and one prose reconciliation. Tree-tidiness was not pursued and has no value here. What the next wave should take MERGE ROUND 1 FIRST, IN THIS ORDER: #9377 (the security fix - it is the only thing in this wave that closes a live escalation), then #9379 (it turns the red Sheet-grid hook unit harness green, which is currently the only non-advisory red on the still-open #9335), then #9378 and #9380. Two of the four are owed a genuinely independent second reviewer before merge, and this workflow spawns exactly one reviewer, so that dispatch is a MANUAL LEAD STEP: #9377 (security / tenancy) and #9380 (whether leg A admits a fraudulent THROUGH - and it never got its builder's own review dispatch, so it has had ONE pair of eyes on 37 KB of shell). THEN THE DEFERRED ROUND-2 SLICES, EACH AS ITS DEPENDENCY MERGES: pds-w44-judgment-coverage-ladder after #9378 (both rewrite the census and every line number shifts - re-derive anchors at the new base, and PROVEN-BACKED must be one Enum.count over one MapSet.union, never an addition); pds-w44-hetzner-offline-door after #9380 (it edits the same declared set, so dispatching beside it produces a conflict, not a build - and BOTH legs or neither: the instrument AND its ELIXIR_TEST_ONLY_PATHS entry); pds-w44-charter-sweep-adjudication after the charter PR #9353 merges (the candidate vocabulary is MINED FROM THE CHARTER, so adjudicating before it lands produces a fresh red the moment it does - and this wave's own wave-log entry moved that vocabulary again). AND ONE NEW STANDING CHORE, from D653: every review must diff each wave task's stated branch against origin/main before it grades anything. An empty diff on a stamped task is a stranded slice, and the built-slice handoff structurally cannot report one. Wave 44 sealed 2026-08-03. 4 PRs open: #9377, #9378, #9379, #9380. Nothing merged - the lead merges, and closes the merge-gated criterion on each task as it does.

320.title: PDS wave 44 - recover wave 43's unlanded work, re-derive its one security claim, and make the price column RUN

390.bodyText: PDS wave 44 - recover wave 43's unlanded work, re-derive its one security claim, and make the price column RUN STRATEGIZE COMPLETE - the survey fleet is flying. PREMISE SMOKE RUN IN-PROCESS against `git show origin/main:<path>` at origin/main head c2affd445, never the primary checkout (300+ commits behind, 220 foreign modified files). VERIFIED: the charter on origin/main tops out at PDS-D632 - D633-D642 are NOT on main, they live only on PR #9312, so NO builder may carry a D633+ citation until that PR lands. VERIFIED: PDS-D578 exists at charter:11830 and says verbatim 'PROVEN-BACKED is 23/252 = 9.1%' - D640's citation of it COVERS what it is cited for. VERIFIED: api/lib/barkpark_web/studio/caps.ex on origin/main has write_capable?/2 at :283 with `Map.get(caps, :write) == true -> true` as the FIRST cond arm and `restricted?(assigns) -> false` as the SECOND, and restricted?/1 at :295 already contains `share_access == :read` - the ORDER defect #9332 claims is REAL AT SOURCE. Reachability is not yet proven and is survey question 1. VERIFIED: scripts/elixir-path-escape-check.sh is the SINGLE source of truth for ELIXIR_TEST_ONLY_PATHS - the name appears in NO workflow yml; elixir.yml consumes it through --print-set / --match. #9333 edits the right file. VERIFIED on origin/main: scripts/pds-ledger-census_test.sh, scripts/pds-live-hetzner-placement-group.sh, scripts/pds-scratch-target_test.sh, scripts/pds-charter-ledger-sweep.sh and api/test/barkpark/pds_residue_lens_test.exs all exist. VERIFIED: LiveScope.authorize_read/4 is a PRIVATE function at api/lib/barkpark_web/live_scope.ex:114, called from :88 - the non-admin reachability story runs through LiveScope.assign_scope, so the CALLER is what a verifier must pin. The wish, and the four things it asks for Wave 43 died mid-flight on a weekly account limit, not on a defect. It completed 36 of 41 agents, produced ten charter decisions (PDS-D633-D642), and pushed NOTHING. The lead recovered four branches out of their worktrees by hand and opened #9332, #9333, #9334, #9335 at 12:15 today. Wave 43's reviewer never ran; its debrief was never written. Those four PRs are UNREVIEWED BY ANYONE, and their commit messages are an author's own account of their own work. The wish asks for four things: (1) re-derive #9332's live write bypass from source before trusting a word of it; (2) verify the other three the same way; (3) confirm PDS-D633's measurement law - the in-BEAM meter is blind to port children and errs in the one direction a price column must not - and ship its blind-spot sentence in the meter's own moduledoc AND printed output; (4) finish the price column: N of 19 instruments under a required gate, every remaining refusal carrying a measured price, a named environment, or NOT-YET-BUILT. REFUTATION - the first one, and it is in the wish's own item 4 The wish states the price column's reason vocabulary is 'exactly three reasons: PRICE, ENVIRONMENT, NOT-YET-BUILT' and that 'the fence' is not an available answer. Wave 43's own PDS-D637 - which the wish is paraphrasing - found by RUN that three is not enough. It names FIVE classes: PRICE, ENVIRONMENT, NOT-YET-BUILT, plus CONTENT-RED (pds-charter-ledger-sweep.sh --selftest is rc=1 on main today at 2.36s user, refusing because an UNRESOLVED-CLAIM ARRIVAL is unadjudicated - neither a price nor an environment) and RED-BY-DESIGN / REPORTER (pds-record-parity.sh's live axis B exits 1 on 59 leaf rows, 48 of them belonging to twelve OTHER epics that never consented to the instrument; the arm is a reporter and must never carry a required check name). A related sixth, HUMAN-GATE, governs the sheet-grid harness, whose own workflow header says it only gates once a human registers it as a required check. The wish also says pds-record-parity.sh --selftest exits rc=3 with 'unknown argument' and calls that an ENVIRONMENT blocker. Wave 43 did not accept that framing - it walked a DIFFERENT door. #9333 gates scripts/pds-record-parity.test.sh, the instrument's own hermetic two-sided mutation harness (76 checks, zero of which read a live ledger row), at 1.30-1.47s user - the cheapest door in the inventory. So record-parity is not an ENVIRONMENT refusal; its HARNESS is a THROUGH and its LIVE arm is RED-BY-DESIGN. The wish's item 4 is the tenth consecutive dispatch this epic has refuted from the artifact, and it is refuted in the direction of GOOD NEWS. Direction - three movements, and the third is what makes this a wave and not a cleanup The finished experience: at the end of wave 44 a cold reader runs ONE command and gets the epic's honesty column back COMPUTED rather than quoted - every scripts/pds-* instrument, its gate status derived from the two things that actually make a door (a test file that shells it, and a matching ELIXIR_TEST_ONLY_PATHS line), its refusal class, and its price in the unit PDS-D633 says is legal. A new pds-* script arrives as an UNDISPOSED row and the thing goes red. A door that quietly stops running goes red. And the number that appears in the charter next wave is a number nobody typed. Movement 1 - LAND THE RECOVERED WORK, WITH INDEPENDENCE THAT IS REAL Charter #9312 merges FIRST and alone, because until it does every D633+ citation a builder would carry points at nothing on origin/main. Then the four slice PRs, each with an independent re-derivation that does NOT read the branch's own test as its oracle. #9332 gets the full treatment: the source-level order defect is already confirmed (cond arm 1 = caps.write, arm 2 = restricted?, and restricted? already contains share_access == :read), so the open question is REACHABILITY - can a real signed-in NON-MEMBER, through a real non-admin route, hold share_access: :read and caps.write == true simultaneously? That is the whole claim, and it must be re-derived through LiveScope.assign_scope -> authorize_read/4, not asserted from a fixture the branch authored. One suspected defect the wave carries in already, found while reading the diff and NOT yet proven: #9332's membership collapse routes through loadable_principal?/1, which accepts only %ApiToken{} and %User{}. Tenancy.Auth.authorize/3 on origin/main has a THIRD clause at :200 for %Barkpark.Content.CallerContext{}. If a socket's principals list can ever carry a CallerContext, the collapse silently drops a principal that authorize/3 would have decided - a behaviour change dressed as a round-trip saving, in the same slice as a security fix. Survey question 3 exists to settle it before a builder inherits it. Movement 2 - FINISH WHAT WAVE 43 PRICED Two of wave 43's six slices never got a builder at all. The LiveView residual 32-fold (PDS-D639: one missing lvs_walk/3 clause takes RESIDUAL 32 -> 0 and makes the headline deny fraction WORSE, 70.6% -> 60.9%, which is the strongest available evidence it is real) is unbuilt - no branch exists for it. The judgment-coverage ladder (PDS-D640: PROVEN-BACKED is 23 routed-write MEMBERS as an Enum.count over a MapSet.union/2, never an addition, with OVERLAP printed beside it) is its round-2 dependent and has had its numbers die three times. Both ship this wave, the fold first, with D639's three named obligations non-negotiable - especially (a), the plugin fixture, because without it the new clause is STRUCTURALLY unexercised and the class does not descend from its substitution. And the door walks D637 explicitly deferred to wave 44: pds-ledger-census_test.sh (PRICE ~20-23s, viable, python3 confirmed present on the Elixir runner by wave 43's own three-leg ledger note) and the best unexamined candidate, pds-live-hetzner-placement-group.sh --selftest-offline, NOT-YET-MEASURED. Each measured by the ONLY legal method: an OS meter around a SHELL, never from inside a BEAM parent. Movement 3 - THE DOOR CENSUS: the price column stops being prose This is the bold one. PDS-D637's column is, today, forty lines of charter prose sitting on an unmerged PR - and PDS-D633's own closing sentence is that a number from a meter must live in the instrument's moduledoc and printed output, NEVER in prose a copy-paste can drop. The column violates the law that produced it. Wave 44 turns it into an instrument: enumerate scripts/pds-*.{sh,exs} for the denominator; for each row DERIVE the gate status from two independent legs - leg A, a '../../../scripts/...' string literal in an api/test/** file that actually shells it; leg B, that same path present in elixir-path-escape-check.sh's declared set - and report THROUGH only when BOTH hold. One leg without the other is exactly the wave-42 #9290/#9292 defect (Test skipped while Elixir gate passed in 3s on the skip shim), and this makes that defect impossible to reintroduce quietly rather than merely remembered. Every non-THROUGH row carries a class from D637's FIVE (not three) and, for PRICE rows, a figure with the meter named. An instrument with no disposition is UNDISPOSED and the census exits non-zero - the same fail-closed shape the receipt census already uses. It prints D633's blind-spot sentence in its own output. And it rides its own door: it is an instrument, so it gets a test file and a path-set line like every other, which is the self-referential proof that the derivation works. The wave plan, provisionally # MOVEMENT WHY NOW STATE TODAY 0 merge charter #9312 alone, first D633-D642 are not on origin/main; every downstream citation is a phantom until it lands PR open, BLOCKED 1 independently re-derive + land #9332 (caps read-only share write bypass + derive collapse) a live authorization bypass reviewed by nobody; source-level order defect already confirmed PR open, unreviewed 2 independently re-derive + land #9333 (census + record-parity doors, 1 -> 3 of 19) carries the ELIXIR_TEST_ONLY_PATHS lesson wave 42 lost PR open, unreviewed 3 independently re-derive + land #9334 (ledger-lapse expiry arm, three shapes) ledger lapse is endemic; the lesson has been a paragraph in three debriefs PR open, unreviewed 4 independently re-derive + land #9335 (sheet-grid read mode) the one standing user-facing harm: a selection frozen at A1 that nothing can move PR open, unreviewed 5 BUILD the LiveView residual 32-fold (D639) with its three obligations never got a builder; blocks the ladder unbuilt, no branch 6 BUILD the judgment-coverage ladder (D640) after the fold merges numbers dead three times; union not addition deferred round 2 7 BUILD the DOOR CENSUS - the price column as a running instrument the honesty column violates the law that produced it new this wave 8 walk two more doors: pds-ledger-census_test.sh, pds-live-hetzner-placement-group.sh D637 named both for wave 44 by number and by name new this wave Direction debate - the rivals, and why this one won Rival A - RECOVERY ONLY Spend the whole wave making wave 43's four branches independently bulletproof and merged, plus the charter, and ship nothing new. The case for it is strong and honest: an unreviewed authorization change is the single riskiest object in the repo right now, and a wave that merges it carelessly while chasing new capability has failed at the only thing that mattered. It was rejected because it under-uses the wave, not because it is wrong: four PRs of independent re-derivation is roughly one round, and the fold plus the ladder are DESIGNED work with their obligations already derived by run - leaving them unbuilt for a second consecutive wave is how wave 43's best output rots. Rival A's real contribution survives: movement 1 goes first, alone, and no slice PR merges on its own author's oracle. Rival B - ADVANCE ONLY Treat the four branches as inherited fact, merge them on their green, and spend the wave taking the door from 3 of 19 to 6 or 7. Rejected outright: it is precisely the move the wish forbids, and the epic's own law forbids it too. A commit message is an exit code with better prose. Merging #9332 on its own test's word is 'a gate lies when its green costs nothing to produce', committed by the wave that coined the sentence. Rival C - THE DOOR CENSUS (winner, as movement 3 of three) The winning insight is that the epic has spent four waves arguing about a column it has never computed. Every wave restates the roster, re-prices some rows, and writes the total into the charter by hand - and PDS-D636 records that the census itself carries a FALSE SENTENCE about its own gating on main today. That is the exact failure mode this epic exists to end, committed by the epic, about the epic. Making the column an instrument is the epic's own law turned inward one more notch, and it is cheap: the derivation is two greps over files that already exist, and the prior art is already on main (api/test/barkpark/pds_residue_lens_test.exs). The sharpest attack on the winner, and how the wave absorbs it THE ATTACK: the door census is a THIRD census. This epic already has a receipt census, a residue lens, a ledger census, a record-parity arm and a charter-ledger sweep - nineteen instruments, three of which run anywhere. Building a twentieth instrument to count the nineteen is the purest possible instance of an epic measuring itself instead of shipping. And it will be WRONG on day one: leg A ('a test file shells it') has at least three encodings in the repo already (System.cmd with a module attribute, Code.require_file, a bare relative path), so a naive derivation will under-count and print a number LOWER than the truth - a different lie, in a friendlier direction. HOW THE WAVE ABSORBS IT. First, the door census is movement THREE of three - it ships only if movements 1 and 2 are honest, and the wave is graded on the security fix and the merges regardless. Second, the under-count objection becomes the instrument's design: the census is FAIL-CLOSED on ambiguity - a pds-* script it cannot dispose is UNDISPOSED and reds, and a test-side reference it cannot classify is an ERROR, never a silent 'not gated'.
