320.bodyText: PDS wave 44 - recover wave 43's unlanded work, re-derive its one security claim, and make the price column RUN STRATEGIZE COMPLETE - the survey fleet is flying. PREMISE SMOKE RUN IN-PROCESS against `git show origin/main:<path>` at origin/main head c2affd445, never the primary checkout (300+ commits behind, 220 foreign modified files). VERIFIED: the charter on origin/main tops out at PDS-D632 - D633-D642 are NOT on main, they live only on PR #9312, so NO builder may carry a D633+ citation until that PR lands. VERIFIED: PDS-D578 exists at charter:11830 and says verbatim 'PROVEN-BACKED is 23/252 = 9.1%' - D640's citation of it COVERS what it is cited for. VERIFIED: api/lib/barkpark_web/studio/caps.ex on origin/main has write_capable?/2 at :283 with `Map.get(caps, :write) == true -> true` as the FIRST cond arm and `restricted?(assigns) -> false` as the SECOND, and restricted?/1 at :295 already contains `share_access == :read` - the ORDER defect #9332 claims is REAL AT SOURCE. Reachability is not yet proven and is survey question 1. VERIFIED: scripts/elixir-path-escape-check.sh is the SINGLE source of truth for ELIXIR_TEST_ONLY_PATHS - the name appears in NO workflow yml; elixir.yml consumes it through --print-set / --match. #9333 edits the right file. VERIFIED on origin/main: scripts/pds-ledger-census_test.sh, scripts/pds-live-hetzner-placement-group.sh, scripts/pds-scratch-target_test.sh, scripts/pds-charter-ledger-sweep.sh and api/test/barkpark/pds_residue_lens_test.exs all exist. VERIFIED: LiveScope.authorize_read/4 is a PRIVATE function at api/lib/barkpark_web/live_scope.ex:114, called from :88 - the non-admin reachability story runs through LiveScope.assign_scope, so the CALLER is what a verifier must pin. The wish, and the four things it asks for Wave 43 died mid-flight on a weekly account limit, not on a defect. It completed 36 of 41 agents, produced ten charter decisions (PDS-D633-D642), and pushed NOTHING. The lead recovered four branches out of their worktrees by hand and opened #9332, #9333, #9334, #9335 at 12:15 today. Wave 43's reviewer never ran; its debrief was never written. Those four PRs are UNREVIEWED BY ANYONE, and their commit messages are an author's own account of their own work. The wish asks for four things: (1) re-derive #9332's live write bypass from source before trusting a word of it; (2) verify the other three the same way; (3) confirm PDS-D633's measurement law - the in-BEAM meter is blind to port children and errs in the one direction a price column must not - and ship its blind-spot sentence in the meter's own moduledoc AND printed output; (4) finish the price column: N of 19 instruments under a required gate, every remaining refusal carrying a measured price, a named environment, or NOT-YET-BUILT. REFUTATION - the first one, and it is in the wish's own item 4 The wish states the price column's reason vocabulary is 'exactly three reasons: PRICE, ENVIRONMENT, NOT-YET-BUILT' and that 'the fence' is not an available answer. Wave 43's own PDS-D637 - which the wish is paraphrasing - found by RUN that three is not enough. It names FIVE classes: PRICE, ENVIRONMENT, NOT-YET-BUILT, plus CONTENT-RED (pds-charter-ledger-sweep.sh --selftest is rc=1 on main today at 2.36s user, refusing because an UNRESOLVED-CLAIM ARRIVAL is unadjudicated - neither a price nor an environment) and RED-BY-DESIGN / REPORTER (pds-record-parity.sh's live axis B exits 1 on 59 leaf rows, 48 of them belonging to twelve OTHER epics that never consented to the instrument; the arm is a reporter and must never carry a required check name). A related sixth, HUMAN-GATE, governs the sheet-grid harness, whose own workflow header says it only gates once a human registers it as a required check. The wish also says pds-record-parity.sh --selftest exits rc=3 with 'unknown argument' and calls that an ENVIRONMENT blocker. Wave 43 did not accept that framing - it walked a DIFFERENT door. #9333 gates scripts/pds-record-parity.test.sh, the instrument's own hermetic two-sided mutation harness (76 checks, zero of which read a live ledger row), at 1.30-1.47s user - the cheapest door in the inventory. So record-parity is not an ENVIRONMENT refusal; its HARNESS is a THROUGH and its LIVE arm is RED-BY-DESIGN. The wish's item 4 is the tenth consecutive dispatch this epic has refuted from the artifact, and it is refuted in the direction of GOOD NEWS. Direction - three movements, and the third is what makes this a wave and not a cleanup The finished experience: at the end of wave 44 a cold reader runs ONE command and gets the epic's honesty column back COMPUTED rather than quoted - every scripts/pds-* instrument, its gate status derived from the two things that actually make a door (a test file that shells it, and a matching ELIXIR_TEST_ONLY_PATHS line), its refusal class, and its price in the unit PDS-D633 says is legal. A new pds-* script arrives as an UNDISPOSED row and the thing goes red. A door that quietly stops running goes red. And the number that appears in the charter next wave is a number nobody typed. Movement 1 - LAND THE RECOVERED WORK, WITH INDEPENDENCE THAT IS REAL Charter #9312 merges FIRST and alone, because until it does every D633+ citation a builder would carry points at nothing on origin/main. Then the four slice PRs, each with an independent re-derivation that does NOT read the branch's own test as its oracle. #9332 gets the full treatment: the source-level order defect is already confirmed (cond arm 1 = caps.write, arm 2 = restricted?, and restricted? already contains share_access == :read), so the open question is REACHABILITY - can a real signed-in NON-MEMBER, through a real non-admin route, hold share_access: :read and caps.write == true simultaneously? That is the whole claim, and it must be re-derived through LiveScope.assign_scope -> authorize_read/4, not asserted from a fixture the branch authored. One suspected defect the wave carries in already, found while reading the diff and NOT yet proven: #9332's membership collapse routes through loadable_principal?/1, which accepts only %ApiToken{} and %User{}. Tenancy.Auth.authorize/3 on origin/main has a THIRD clause at :200 for %Barkpark.Content.CallerContext{}. If a socket's principals list can ever carry a CallerContext, the collapse silently drops a principal that authorize/3 would have decided - a behaviour change dressed as a round-trip saving, in the same slice as a security fix. Survey question 3 exists to settle it before a builder inherits it. Movement 2 - FINISH WHAT WAVE 43 PRICED Two of wave 43's six slices never got a builder at all. The LiveView residual 32-fold (PDS-D639: one missing lvs_walk/3 clause takes RESIDUAL 32 -> 0 and makes the headline deny fraction WORSE, 70.6% -> 60.9%, which is the strongest available evidence it is real) is unbuilt - no branch exists for it. The judgment-coverage ladder (PDS-D640: PROVEN-BACKED is 23 routed-write MEMBERS as an Enum.count over a MapSet.union/2, never an addition, with OVERLAP printed beside it) is its round-2 dependent and has had its numbers die three times. Both ship this wave, the fold first, with D639's three named obligations non-negotiable - especially (a), the plugin fixture, because without it the new clause is STRUCTURALLY unexercised and the class does not descend from its substitution. And the door walks D637 explicitly deferred to wave 44: pds-ledger-census_test.sh (PRICE ~20-23s, viable, python3 confirmed present on the Elixir runner by wave 43's own three-leg ledger note) and the best unexamined candidate, pds-live-hetzner-placement-group.sh --selftest-offline, NOT-YET-MEASURED. Each measured by the ONLY legal method: an OS meter around a SHELL, never from inside a BEAM parent. Movement 3 - THE DOOR CENSUS: the price column stops being prose This is the bold one. PDS-D637's column is, today, forty lines of charter prose sitting on an unmerged PR - and PDS-D633's own closing sentence is that a number from a meter must live in the instrument's moduledoc and printed output, NEVER in prose a copy-paste can drop. The column violates the law that produced it. Wave 44 turns it into an instrument: enumerate scripts/pds-*.{sh,exs} for the denominator; for each row DERIVE the gate status from two independent legs - leg A, a '../../../scripts/...' string literal in an api/test/** file that actually shells it; leg B, that same path present in elixir-path-escape-check.sh's declared set - and report THROUGH only when BOTH hold. One leg without the other is exactly the wave-42 #9290/#9292 defect (Test skipped while Elixir gate passed in 3s on the skip shim), and this makes that defect impossible to reintroduce quietly rather than merely remembered. Every non-THROUGH row carries a class from D637's FIVE (not three) and, for PRICE rows, a figure with the meter named. An instrument with no disposition is UNDISPOSED and the census exits non-zero - the same fail-closed shape the receipt census already uses. It prints D633's blind-spot sentence in its own output. And it rides its own door: it is an instrument, so it gets a test file and a path-set line like every other, which is the self-referential proof that the derivation works. The wave plan, provisionally # MOVEMENT WHY NOW STATE TODAY 0 merge charter #9312 alone, first D633-D642 are not on origin/main; every downstream citation is a phantom until it lands PR open, BLOCKED 1 independently re-derive + land #9332 (caps read-only share write bypass + derive collapse) a live authorization bypass reviewed by nobody; source-level order defect already confirmed PR open, unreviewed 2 independently re-derive + land #9333 (census + record-parity doors, 1 -> 3 of 19) carries the ELIXIR_TEST_ONLY_PATHS lesson wave 42 lost PR open, unreviewed 3 independently re-derive + land #9334 (ledger-lapse expiry arm, three shapes) ledger lapse is endemic; the lesson has been a paragraph in three debriefs PR open, unreviewed 4 independently re-derive + land #9335 (sheet-grid read mode) the one standing user-facing harm: a selection frozen at A1 that nothing can move PR open, unreviewed 5 BUILD the LiveView residual 32-fold (D639) with its three obligations never got a builder; blocks the ladder unbuilt, no branch 6 BUILD the judgment-coverage ladder (D640) after the fold merges numbers dead three times; union not addition deferred round 2 7 BUILD the DOOR CENSUS - the price column as a running instrument the honesty column violates the law that produced it new this wave 8 walk two more doors: pds-ledger-census_test.sh, pds-live-hetzner-placement-group.sh D637 named both for wave 44 by number and by name new this wave Direction debate - the rivals, and why this one won Rival A - RECOVERY ONLY Spend the whole wave making wave 43's four branches independently bulletproof and merged, plus the charter, and ship nothing new. The case for it is strong and honest: an unreviewed authorization change is the single riskiest object in the repo right now, and a wave that merges it carelessly while chasing new capability has failed at the only thing that mattered. It was rejected because it under-uses the wave, not because it is wrong: four PRs of independent re-derivation is roughly one round, and the fold plus the ladder are DESIGNED work with their obligations already derived by run - leaving them unbuilt for a second consecutive wave is how wave 43's best output rots. Rival A's real contribution survives: movement 1 goes first, alone, and no slice PR merges on its own author's oracle. Rival B - ADVANCE ONLY Treat the four branches as inherited fact, merge them on their green, and spend the wave taking the door from 3 of 19 to 6 or 7. Rejected outright: it is precisely the move the wish forbids, and the epic's own law forbids it too. A commit message is an exit code with better prose. Merging #9332 on its own test's word is 'a gate lies when its green costs nothing to produce', committed by the wave that coined the sentence. Rival C - THE DOOR CENSUS (winner, as movement 3 of three) The winning insight is that the epic has spent four waves arguing about a column it has never computed. Every wave restates the roster, re-prices some rows, and writes the total into the charter by hand - and PDS-D636 records that the census itself carries a FALSE SENTENCE about its own gating on main today. That is the exact failure mode this epic exists to end, committed by the epic, about the epic. Making the column an instrument is the epic's own law turned inward one more notch, and it is cheap: the derivation is two greps over files that already exist, and the prior art is already on main (api/test/barkpark/pds_residue_lens_test.exs). The sharpest attack on the winner, and how the wave absorbs it THE ATTACK: the door census is a THIRD census. This epic already has a receipt census, a residue lens, a ledger census, a record-parity arm and a charter-ledger sweep - nineteen instruments, three of which run anywhere. Building a twentieth instrument to count the nineteen is the purest possible instance of an epic measuring itself instead of shipping. And it will be WRONG on day one: leg A ('a test file shells it') has at least three encodings in the repo already (System.cmd with a module attribute, Code.require_file, a bare relative path), so a naive derivation will under-count and print a number LOWER than the truth - a different lie, in a friendlier direction. HOW THE WAVE ABSORBS IT. First, the door census is movement THREE of three - it ships only if movements 1 and 2 are honest, and the wave is graded on the security fix and the merges regardless. Second, the under-count objection becomes the instrument's design: the census is FAIL-CLOSED on ambiguity - a pds-* script it cannot dispose is UNDISPOSED and reds, and a test-side reference it cannot classify is an ERROR, never a silent 'not gated'. That makes the day-one wrongness LOUD instead of quiet, and the surveyors are tasked (question 4) with enumerating every encoding of leg A that exists on main before a builder writes a regex. Third, if the survey shows the derivation cannot be made honest cheaply, the fallback is smaller and still real: a self-check that the two legs AGREE for every already-gated instrument - which alone would have caught #9290 and #9292. The survey plan - 20 assignments, and what each one changes Width is the point. Each surveyor is one Opus at medium effort; the digest distils. Every load-bearing assumption in the direction above appears below as a question, including the ones that would kill it. KEY QUESTION WHY IT CHANGES THE PLAN caps-reachability Can a signed-in NON-MEMBER with an ACTIVE WRITE GRANT actually reach a socket carrying share_access: :read AND caps.write == true, through a real non-admin route? Trace LiveScope.assign_scope -> authorize_read/4 arm order, and Caps.derive/1's grant load. this IS #9332's claim; if the posture and the write source cannot co-occur the fix is a no-op dressed as a security patch caps-blast-radius Who calls Caps.write_capable?/2 and Caps.derive/1, and are there FORKED copies of the predicate anywhere? Does denying on readonly_posture? break any legitimate write path (grant-graded sockets, anonymous public-demo, api_token flows)? the fix's whole safety argument is that it is narrower than restricted?/1; a fork elsewhere means the bypass survives the merge caps-callercontext Does Tenancy.Auth.authorize/3's CallerContext clause (auth.ex:200) matter to Caps.derive/1? Can socket principals ever carry a CallerContext, and does #9332's loadable_principal?/1 silently drop it? Is permits?/2 + role_permits?/3 truly byte-identical to authorize/3 for every shape? a suspected live behaviour change hiding inside a performance collapse, shipped in a security PR door-leg-encodings Enumerate EVERY way an api/test file currently invokes a scripts/* instrument on origin/main (System.cmd with a @rel attribute, Code.require_file, bare paths, bash -c), and every entry in elixir-path-escape-check.sh's two declared sets. Which pds-* scripts satisfy BOTH legs today? the door census's derivation is only as honest as its enumeration; this is the attack on the winner, answered before a builder writes a regex price-column-19 Re-derive the denominator: is scripts/pds-*.{sh,exs} really 19 on origin/main, and does each of D637's 19 rows still hold its class? Which rows changed since 2026-08-02? the wave prints a fraction; a denominator nobody recomputed is the thing this epic exists to stop ledger-census-door-price Price scripts/pds-ledger-census_test.sh by the D633-legal method (/usr/bin/time -l bash -c, or bash's times builtin) on a QUIET host, and confirm it needs no live ledger creds. Does python3 exist on the Elixir runner (re-derive wave 43's three-leg claim)? D637 named this as THE wave-44 door; if the price or the environment claim fails, movement 2's door walk changes target hetzner-selftest-offline Does scripts/pds-live-hetzner-placement-group.sh --selftest-offline exist, what does it actually do, what does it cost by an OS meter around a shell, and can it red? D637's best UNEXAMINED candidate; a second cheap door would move the count 3 -> 6 charter-sweep-content-red Why is pds-charter-ledger-sweep.sh --selftest rc=1 on main today, exactly what unadjudicated claim is it naming, and what would scripts/pds-charter-ledger-adjudication.md need to say to clear it? CONTENT-RED is the class the wish's three-reason vocabulary cannot express; clearing it would be a fourth door for near-zero cost meter-blindspot-sites Find every place this epic prints a number derived from a meter (:erlang.statistics, System.monotonic_time, wall clocks, reductions) across scripts/pds-* and api/test/**. Which carry a blind-spot sentence today? Which quote wall clock in violation of D605? D633's obligation is mechanical placement, not prose; this is the list a builder needs residual-fold-clause In scripts/pds-elixir-receipt-census.exs, locate lvs_walk/3 and the plugin_routes(scope:) macro node handling. Confirm the missing clause, the RESIDUAL 32 -> 0 fold, and whether the selftest corpus really writes zero fixtures under api/lib/barkpark/plugins/. D639's obligation (a) is that without a plugin fixture the new clause is structurally unexercised; confirm before building ladder-union-sites Find every addition idiom in the census's ladder reporting flow (census.exs ~4033 area), the roster_functions/1 verdict-filter question, and the current selftest case/mutant baseline (30/20 vs the task's stale 25/16). D640 says PROVEN-BACKED must be an Enum.count over a MapSet.union with OVERLAP printed; the task's own criteria are wrong and must be rewritten sheetgrid-readmode In #9335: is READ_MODE_EVENTS truly the complement of the six mutating events (edit-start, cell-toggle, clear-selection, undo, redo, toggle-style)? Is presence-meta's editing flag denied? Does Ops.send_ops/2's write_capable:false clause really terminate all six? What is the reader-half state (grid_sel(_,_,:reader) -> {0,0,0,0})? the branch's own tests are its author's oracle; the allowlist/denylist complement claim is the security-shaped half of a UX slice ledger-lapse-truth Re-derive #9334's three shapes against the SERVER's actual claim schema and TTL sweeper: does a lapse really null worker while preserving previous_worker and writing expired_at? Is BARKPARK_TASK_LEASE_TTL_SECONDS / 2700 the real default? Does /v1/data/query really carry claim as a top-level key? the arm's keys are the whole finding; a wrong key means an arm that passes vacuously forever, which is the defect it was built to fix gate-health-four-prs For each of #9332-#9335 on their CURRENT head SHAs: which check-runs ran, which were SKIPPED, and did 'Test (Elixir ...)' actually execute? Check started_at on every red. Is 'PR references an active task' red for the known lease reason? a green that came from a skip shim is the wave's own law failing on its own PRs merge-order-conflicts Do #9312, #9332, #9333, #9334, #9335 conflict with each other or with origin/main? Compute merge-base and file overlap. Does any of them touch scripts/pds-elixir-receipt-census.exs, which the fold slice also wants? wave 43 resolved intra-wave collisions by cutting differently; wave 44 inherits the cuts and must re-verify them against a moved main w43-task-ledger Read every wave-43 slice task row (pds-w43-*): lifecycle_status, criteria_progress, claim state. How many lapsed to open with work done? Which criteria are stamped with real evidence vs empty? the wave must re-claim and close these rows honestly; and the lapse count is live data for #9334's own arm w43-backlog-security Read pds-w43-bl-grant-grade-doc-escalation-unproven in full. Is the doc-scoped write escalation still open on the paper COMPONENT route for GRANT-graded sockets - the population #9332 deliberately did NOT deny? if the grant-graded escalation is live, wave 44 has a SECOND security slice and the wave plan changes shape prior-papers Read the bp Papers pds-wave-41/42/43-2026-08-0x and any wave-43 debrief fragments. What did wave 43's direction promise that its four branches do NOT deliver? What did its surveyors find that never reached a decision? wave 43 never wrote a debrief; its Paper is the only record of its own unfinished intent sobelow-and-required-checks Re-derive main's Sobelow baseline from the DECIDING scan block only (between its own banner and SCAN COMPLETE), and the live vs committed required-check contexts. Do any of the four PRs move the breakdown? an unchanged breakdown is the only proof a PR added nothing; the required-check spec drift is a HELD human decision the wave must not touch census-selfclaim-falsehood Confirm PDS-D636's claim that scripts/pds-elixir-receipt-census.exs:10-11 states something FALSE about its own gating on origin/main today, and find any OTHER instrument carrying a false self-description. an instrument lying about itself is the epic's law failing at the source, and it is a free high-signal fix for the door-census slice What this wave will NOT do Touch .github/required-checks.json - the four-vs-two context gap is a HELD human decision. Touch .claude/workflows/bp-epic-cycle.workflow.js - #6086 edits it, is conflicting and 587 commits behind. Fence-cross into cloud/**, .github/workflows/** or gr-*/cch-* - Cloud Console wave 27 is resuming alongside. This wave's fence is api/**, internal/**, deploy/**, scripts/pds-* and pds-*. Round-1 file sets are disjoint - the census, the escape-check, shared/paper.ex and the palette harness are each owned by exactly one slice. # Slice Task id Round Model Gate 1 The grant-graded doc escalation is closed at the door it rides pds-w44-grant-door-narrowing 1 fable (remapped to opus - fable unavailable) CC=clang mix test on the new LiveView test + the studio directory, rc captured to a variable 2 Residual-32 fold recovered + D605's unit + D633's blind spot IN the instrument pds-w44-census-fold-and-blindspot 1 fable (remapped) elixir scripts/pds-elixir-receipt-census.exs and its --selftest, both rc=0 3 The door census: the price column becomes an instrument pds-w44-door-census-instrument 1 fable (remapped) bash scripts/pds-door-census.sh + bash scripts/elixir-path-escape-check.sh --check + CC=clang mix test the new rider 4 The palette harness repaired against generated tokens pds-w44-palette-harness-repair 1 opus node each __*.test.mjs in api/assets/sheet-grid, every rc captured and zero 5 The judgment-coverage ladder: PROVEN-BACKED 23 as a union pds-w44-judgment-coverage-ladder 2 (after 2) opus elixir census + --selftest + the doc byte-budget check 6 The hetzner offline arm becomes the next door pds-w44-hetzner-offline-door 2 (after 3) opus CC=clang mix test the new rider + escape-check --check at rc=0 7 The charter sweep adjudicated and its fail-open closed pds-w44-charter-sweep-adjudication 2 (after THIS charter merges) opus bash scripts/pds-charter-ledger-sweep.sh and --selftest, both rc=0 HIGH-FLIP-RISK, declared, and the line is in each task's own brief so the reviewer reads it there: SLICE 1 - whether the grant grade's narrowing belongs in the door or the gate, and whether narrowing it denies a legitimate grantee. This is an authorization judgment on a bypass that is LIVE ON MAIN, and it is the species that flipped twice in wave 43. SLICE 3 - whether leg A's three predicates admit a fraudulent THROUGH; the comment mutation is the oracle, and wave 44's own prototype PASSED IT. Both warrant a genuinely independent second reviewer before merge. This workflow spawns one reviewer, so that dispatch is a manual lead step - review's job is to NAME when independence is owed. BACKLOG FILED NOW, six published child rows, so the ledger shows the future: pds-w44-bl-ledger-census-door-repriced, pds-w44-bl-ops-controller-apply-ops-ungated, pds-w44-bl-vacuous-reader-toggle-oracle, pds-w44-bl-sheetgrid-write-landing-unproven, pds-w44-bl-stranded-work-is-invisible-to-git-grep, pds-w44-bl-citation-precedes-merge-check. THE WAVE'S OWN LAW, TURNED ON ITSELF. A gate lies when its green costs nothing to produce - and this wave found that sentence violated three times by the epic that coined it: #9334's zero-second Test shim, the two-leg agreement check that cannot red, and the charter sweep's second read that prints CONFIRMED while its read failed. Wave 44's grade rests on slices 1 and 2, not on the door count. DEBRIEF - wave 44 reviewed, 4 PRs pushed, grade A- Every branch this wave produced is on origin with a PR open. Nothing is merged - the lead merges. Three slices were handed to review as built and green; a FOURTH was found stranded, fully built and fully gated, with zero commits on its branch, and was recovered here. What shipped, per slice TASK FINAL BRANCH PR GATE RE-RUN ON THE FINAL STATE VERDICT pds-w44-grant-door-narrowing loop-epic/a-doc-scoped-write-grant-stops-writing-a-0-r #9377 slice test rc=0, 5 tests 0 failures; studio suite rc=0, 1547 tests 0 failures STRONG. The bypass is real and the fix is what closes it - proven by the reviewer's OWN mutation, not the builder's: neutering grant_target_denied?/3 gives rc=2 with two failures printing left: %{"amount" => "ESCALATED"} read back from the store. pds-w44-census-fold-and-blindspot loop-epic/the-residual-32-gets-judged-and-the-mete-1 #9378 census rc=0, RESIDUAL 0/322, sum 322 == population 322, CENSUS OK STRONG. A/B re-derived independently: 32 -> 0, reachable_unconditional 194 -> 225, DENIES numerator HELD at 137, so the headline fraction gets WORSE (70.6% -> 60.9%). That is a fold, not a rubber stamp. pds-w44-palette-harness-repair loop-epic/the-sheet-grid-palette-harness-stops-com-3-r #9379 all four __*.test.mjs rc=0; palette reports 18 contrast checks STRONG, plus two reviewer fixes. The 4-week red was a harness attribution bug, never a WCAG defect - and the bug lied in BOTH directions (#14532d is invisible in dark mode at 2.18:1 and the old harness would have PASSED it at 9.11:1 vs white). pds-w44-door-census-instrument loop-epic/the-price-column-stops-being-charter-pro-2-r #9380 door-census rc=0 (UNDISPOSED 0 of 20, ERRORS 0); --selftest rc=0 (8 PASS / 0 FAIL); escape-check rc=0; rider rc=0 (8 tests) RECOVERED BY REVIEW, not builder-delivered. Complete and green - it simply never got committed. One pair of eyes on a 37 KB shell instrument; an independent second reviewer is owed. What the review FOUND that the wave did not report PDS-D653 - A TASK CAN BE 11/12 STAMPED AND ITS BRANCH EMPTY. pds-w44-door-census-instrument stamped eleven criteria with real run evidence, its now-line read 'committing: ... branching loop-epic/the-price-column-stops-being-charter-pro-2', and git diff origin/main...that-branch is EMPTY. It was in NEITHER the built handoff nor the not-green list. The rule this buys: the LEDGER is the sweep index, not the handoff - diff every wave task's stated branch against origin/main and treat an empty diff as STRANDED, because a report cannot describe the builder that stopped before writing it. PDS-D654 - A GATE THAT DOES NOT TRIGGER ON ITS OWN SUBJECT IS GREEN FOR FREE. sheet-grid-js.yml runs a harness that parses root.html.heex, presence_state.ex and tokens_gen.ex, and triggered on NONE of them - so the contrast gate never ran on a PR that changed a hue, a background token, or the presence palette. D633's law in its cheapest form yet: no skip shim, no vacuous assertion, just a paths: list that omits the subject. Repaired in #9379. PDS-D655 - TWO INSTRUMENTS SHIPPED CONTRADICTORY PROSE ABOUT THE SAME FINDING, IN THE SAME WAVE. pds-door-census.sh printed the meter blindness as a 236x real/user RATIO; pds-elixir-receipt-census.exs refuted exactly that on its own runs (113x, then 123x, for the SAME fan-out, because real counts WAITING). Reconciled in review onto the load-independent leaf-metered FLOOR. The rule: when a finding ships inside more than one instrument, ONE owns the sentence and the others cite it - the same argument the census's own @blind_spot attribute makes, one level up. A FLAKE, FILED RATHER THAN SWALLOWED. The first full studio-suite run scored 1 failure in ChatRenderGoldenTest's sidebar byte-lock (golden 6554 bytes, region 6554 bytes, first diff at 723 - a same-length CONTENT SWAP). It passes in isolation and passed on re-run of the identical tree. Filed as task-441f5a5669e0ab6b. A golden that reds only sometimes trains reviewers to re-run until green, which is this epic's own defect class. THE HOST WAS NOT QUIET, AND THAT PROVED D605 BY ACCIDENT. The reviewer's census read user cpu 17330 ms against wall clock 95801 ms on a box carrying 24 stray busy-loop processes four days old. The wall figure is the LOAD; the CPU figure is the CODE. Dated corrections to earlier sections of this Paper 2026-08-03, correcting the Direction section's 'Charter #9312 merges FIRST and alone': INVERTED IN PRACTICE. #9332/#9333/#9334 merged at 10:49-10:50Z and the charter at 11:29:57Z - forty minutes after the code citing it. Already recorded as PDS-D643; noted here so a reader of the Direction section does not carry the plan as the outcome. 2026-08-03, correcting 'The wave plan - 7 slices, 4 in round 1': FOUR round-1 slices were dispatched and only THREE reached review as built. The fourth (pds-w44-door-census-instrument) completed its work and its gate and died before committing; it is delivered by this review as #9380. The plan's round-1 count is right; its delivery path is not what the plan describes. 2026-08-03, on the wish's item 3 ('measured at 236x'): REFUTED BY THE ARTIFACT, and the refutation is now the shipped sentence in BOTH instruments. real/user is load-dependent; the load-independent statement is the DIRECTION plus a leaf-metered floor. Ledger audit All four slice tasks are lifecycle in_progress with merge-gated criteria left OPEN for the lead - correct, none closed early. Evidence was stamped AS THE BUILDERS WORKED, not batched: each carries per-criterion evidence quoting run output, and two carry honest --miss records rather than fabricated flips (pds-w44-census-fold-and-blindspot criterion 8, the lv_verdict/5 cond reorder; pds-w44-palette-harness-repair criterion 7, the PR body a builder cannot write because builders do not push). ONE LEDGER LIE CORRECTED: pds-w44-door-census-instrument's claim now-line implied a committed branch that does not exist. A review_status field now records the correction, the recovery, and the re-run gate; re-published and read back. Each of the other three tasks gained a review_status naming its final branch, its PR, and which gate legs the REVIEWER re-ran (as distinct from which the builder claimed). No task outside this wave was mutated. One NEW task was filed and published: task-441f5a5669e0ab6b (the golden byte-lock flake), parented to the epic. Grade - A- EARNED, not awarded. What is genuinely strong: three of four slices closed a defect that was REAL and proved it by substitution rather than by reading, and every one of them refuted part of its own brief from the artifact - the palette slice found a THIRD stale coupling nobody had priced (--fg-muted was matched for an hsl() both themes author as var(--muted-text), so that check had found zero declarations and could never have run), and the census slice refused the ratio its dispatch demanded. The security slice is the wave's best work: it declined the obvious fix (widening Caps.write_capable?/2, which is shared with the SheetGrid prop and has no target), declined the obvious predicate (Access.admits_desk?/3, whose type/doc_id overwrite IS the bug), and carries a positive control proving a legitimate grantee still writes. What falls short. (1) A whole slice died between its last stamp and its first commit and NOTHING in the wave's own reporting said so - it took a branch-vs-ledger diff to find a finished instrument one cycle away from deletion. That is the sixth consecutive wave to strand built work, and it is the single reason this is not an A. (2) Two instruments shipped contradictory prose about the same finding in the same wave - a coherence failure the wave had every opportunity to catch, since one slice explicitly refuted the other's figure in its own commit message. (3) The security slice's shipped non-vacuity test is a local constant-false STUB, not the reverted arm; the real revert was run and recorded in the stamp, but the artifact that MERGES cannot reproduce it - the reviewer had to re-run the mutation by hand to confirm. (4) Coverage is honestly partial and says so: paper_ops/2 and document_op/2 carry the new arm but are proven by READING, and the census's ExUnit rider was never run locally. No bloat: 489 lines for the security slice including a 361-line test, 333 for the census fold, 86 for the palette repair. Nothing was redesigned; the reviewer's edits are two latent-hazard closures and one prose reconciliation. Tree-tidiness was not pursued and has no value here. What the next wave should take MERGE ROUND 1 FIRST, IN THIS ORDER: #9377 (the security fix - it is the only thing in this wave that closes a live escalation), then #9379 (it turns the red Sheet-grid hook unit harness green, which is currently the only non-advisory red on the still-open #9335), then #9378 and #9380. Two of the four are owed a genuinely independent second reviewer before merge, and this workflow spawns exactly one reviewer, so that dispatch is a MANUAL LEAD STEP: #9377 (security / tenancy) and #9380 (whether leg A admits a fraudulent THROUGH - and it never got its builder's own review dispatch, so it has had ONE pair of eyes on 37 KB of shell). THEN THE DEFERRED ROUND-2 SLICES, EACH AS ITS DEPENDENCY MERGES: pds-w44-judgment-coverage-ladder after #9378 (both rewrite the census and every line number shifts - re-derive anchors at the new base, and PROVEN-BACKED must be one Enum.count over one MapSet.union, never an addition); pds-w44-hetzner-offline-door after #9380 (it edits the same declared set, so dispatching beside it produces a conflict, not a build - and BOTH legs or neither: the instrument AND its ELIXIR_TEST_ONLY_PATHS entry); pds-w44-charter-sweep-adjudication after the charter PR #9353 merges (the candidate vocabulary is MINED FROM THE CHARTER, so adjudicating before it lands produces a fresh red the moment it does - and this wave's own wave-log entry moved that vocabulary again). AND ONE NEW STANDING CHORE, from D653: every review must diff each wave task's stated branch against origin/main before it grades anything. An empty diff on a stamped task is a stranded slice, and the built-slice handoff structurally cannot report one. Wave 44 sealed 2026-08-03. 4 PRs open: #9377, #9378, #9379, #9380. Nothing merged - the lead merges, and closes the merge-gated criterion on each task as it does. TUI view Email view

390.bodyText: PDS wave 44 - recover wave 43's unlanded work, re-derive its one security claim, and make the price column RUN STRATEGIZE COMPLETE - the survey fleet is flying. PREMISE SMOKE RUN IN-PROCESS against `git show origin/main:<path>` at origin/main head c2affd445, never the primary checkout (300+ commits behind, 220 foreign modified files). VERIFIED: the charter on origin/main tops out at PDS-D632 - D633-D642 are NOT on main, they live only on PR #9312, so NO builder may carry a D633+ citation until that PR lands. VERIFIED: PDS-D578 exists at charter:11830 and says verbatim 'PROVEN-BACKED is 23/252 = 9.1%' - D640's citation of it COVERS what it is cited for. VERIFIED: api/lib/barkpark_web/studio/caps.ex on origin/main has write_capable?/2 at :283 with `Map.get(caps, :write) == true -> true` as the FIRST cond arm and `restricted?(assigns) -> false` as the SECOND, and restricted?/1 at :295 already contains `share_access == :read` - the ORDER defect #9332 claims is REAL AT SOURCE. Reachability is not yet proven and is survey question 1. VERIFIED: scripts/elixir-path-escape-check.sh is the SINGLE source of truth for ELIXIR_TEST_ONLY_PATHS - the name appears in NO workflow yml; elixir.yml consumes it through --print-set / --match. #9333 edits the right file. VERIFIED on origin/main: scripts/pds-ledger-census_test.sh, scripts/pds-live-hetzner-placement-group.sh, scripts/pds-scratch-target_test.sh, scripts/pds-charter-ledger-sweep.sh and api/test/barkpark/pds_residue_lens_test.exs all exist. VERIFIED: LiveScope.authorize_read/4 is a PRIVATE function at api/lib/barkpark_web/live_scope.ex:114, called from :88 - the non-admin reachability story runs through LiveScope.assign_scope, so the CALLER is what a verifier must pin. The wish, and the four things it asks for Wave 43 died mid-flight on a weekly account limit, not on a defect. It completed 36 of 41 agents, produced ten charter decisions (PDS-D633-D642), and pushed NOTHING. The lead recovered four branches out of their worktrees by hand and opened #9332, #9333, #9334, #9335 at 12:15 today. Wave 43's reviewer never ran; its debrief was never written. Those four PRs are UNREVIEWED BY ANYONE, and their commit messages are an author's own account of their own work. The wish asks for four things: (1) re-derive #9332's live write bypass from source before trusting a word of it; (2) verify the other three the same way; (3) confirm PDS-D633's measurement law - the in-BEAM meter is blind to port children and errs in the one direction a price column must not - and ship its blind-spot sentence in the meter's own moduledoc AND printed output; (4) finish the price column: N of 19 instruments under a required gate, every remaining refusal carrying a measured price, a named environment, or NOT-YET-BUILT. REFUTATION - the first one, and it is in the wish's own item 4 The wish states the price column's reason vocabulary is 'exactly three reasons: PRICE, ENVIRONMENT, NOT-YET-BUILT' and that 'the fence' is not an available answer. Wave 43's own PDS-D637 - which the wish is paraphrasing - found by RUN that three is not enough. It names FIVE classes: PRICE, ENVIRONMENT, NOT-YET-BUILT, plus CONTENT-RED (pds-charter-ledger-sweep.sh --selftest is rc=1 on main today at 2.36s user, refusing because an UNRESOLVED-CLAIM ARRIVAL is unadjudicated - neither a price nor an environment) and RED-BY-DESIGN / REPORTER (pds-record-parity.sh's live axis B exits 1 on 59 leaf rows, 48 of them belonging to twelve OTHER epics that never consented to the instrument; the arm is a reporter and must never carry a required check name). A related sixth, HUMAN-GATE, governs the sheet-grid harness, whose own workflow header says it only gates once a human registers it as a required check. The wish also says pds-record-parity.sh --selftest exits rc=3 with 'unknown argument' and calls that an ENVIRONMENT blocker. Wave 43 did not accept that framing - it walked a DIFFERENT door. #9333 gates scripts/pds-record-parity.test.sh, the instrument's own hermetic two-sided mutation harness (76 checks, zero of which read a live ledger row), at 1.30-1.47s user - the cheapest door in the inventory. So record-parity is not an ENVIRONMENT refusal; its HARNESS is a THROUGH and its LIVE arm is RED-BY-DESIGN. The wish's item 4 is the tenth consecutive dispatch this epic has refuted from the artifact, and it is refuted in the direction of GOOD NEWS. Direction - three movements, and the third is what makes this a wave and not a cleanup The finished experience: at the end of wave 44 a cold reader runs ONE command and gets the epic's honesty column back COMPUTED rather than quoted - every scripts/pds-* instrument, its gate status derived from the two things that actually make a door (a test file that shells it, and a matching ELIXIR_TEST_ONLY_PATHS line), its refusal class, and its price in the unit PDS-D633 says is legal. A new pds-* script arrives as an UNDISPOSED row and the thing goes red. A door that quietly stops running goes red. And the number that appears in the charter next wave is a number nobody typed. Movement 1 - LAND THE RECOVERED WORK, WITH INDEPENDENCE THAT IS REAL Charter #9312 merges FIRST and alone, because until it does every D633+ citation a builder would carry points at nothing on origin/main. Then the four slice PRs, each with an independent re-derivation that does NOT read the branch's own test as its oracle. #9332 gets the full treatment: the source-level order defect is already confirmed (cond arm 1 = caps.write, arm 2 = restricted?, and restricted? already contains share_access == :read), so the open question is REACHABILITY - can a real signed-in NON-MEMBER, through a real non-admin route, hold share_access: :read and caps.write == true simultaneously? That is the whole claim, and it must be re-derived through LiveScope.assign_scope -> authorize_read/4, not asserted from a fixture the branch authored. One suspected defect the wave carries in already, found while reading the diff and NOT yet proven: #9332's membership collapse routes through loadable_principal?/1, which accepts only %ApiToken{} and %User{}. Tenancy.Auth.authorize/3 on origin/main has a THIRD clause at :200 for %Barkpark.Content.CallerContext{}. If a socket's principals list can ever carry a CallerContext, the collapse silently drops a principal that authorize/3 would have decided - a behaviour change dressed as a round-trip saving, in the same slice as a security fix. Survey question 3 exists to settle it before a builder inherits it. Movement 2 - FINISH WHAT WAVE 43 PRICED Two of wave 43's six slices never got a builder at all. The LiveView residual 32-fold (PDS-D639: one missing lvs_walk/3 clause takes RESIDUAL 32 -> 0 and makes the headline deny fraction WORSE, 70.6% -> 60.9%, which is the strongest available evidence it is real) is unbuilt - no branch exists for it. The judgment-coverage ladder (PDS-D640: PROVEN-BACKED is 23 routed-write MEMBERS as an Enum.count over a MapSet.union/2, never an addition, with OVERLAP printed beside it) is its round-2 dependent and has had its numbers die three times. Both ship this wave, the fold first, with D639's three named obligations non-negotiable - especially (a), the plugin fixture, because without it the new clause is STRUCTURALLY unexercised and the class does not descend from its substitution. And the door walks D637 explicitly deferred to wave 44: pds-ledger-census_test.sh (PRICE ~20-23s, viable, python3 confirmed present on the Elixir runner by wave 43's own three-leg ledger note) and the best unexamined candidate, pds-live-hetzner-placement-group.sh --selftest-offline, NOT-YET-MEASURED. Each measured by the ONLY legal method: an OS meter around a SHELL, never from inside a BEAM parent. Movement 3 - THE DOOR CENSUS: the price column stops being prose This is the bold one. PDS-D637's column is, today, forty lines of charter prose sitting on an unmerged PR - and PDS-D633's own closing sentence is that a number from a meter must live in the instrument's moduledoc and printed output, NEVER in prose a copy-paste can drop. The column violates the law that produced it. Wave 44 turns it into an instrument: enumerate scripts/pds-*.{sh,exs} for the denominator; for each row DERIVE the gate status from two independent legs - leg A, a '../../../scripts/...' string literal in an api/test/** file that actually shells it; leg B, that same path present in elixir-path-escape-check.sh's declared set - and report THROUGH only when BOTH hold. One leg without the other is exactly the wave-42 #9290/#9292 defect (Test skipped while Elixir gate passed in 3s on the skip shim), and this makes that defect impossible to reintroduce quietly rather than merely remembered. Every non-THROUGH row carries a class from D637's FIVE (not three) and, for PRICE rows, a figure with the meter named. An instrument with no disposition is UNDISPOSED and the census exits non-zero - the same fail-closed shape the receipt census already uses. It prints D633's blind-spot sentence in its own output. And it rides its own door: it is an instrument, so it gets a test file and a path-set line like every other, which is the self-referential proof that the derivation works. The wave plan, provisionally # MOVEMENT WHY NOW STATE TODAY 0 merge charter #9312 alone, first D633-D642 are not on origin/main; every downstream citation is a phantom until it lands PR open, BLOCKED 1 independently re-derive + land #9332 (caps read-only share write bypass + derive collapse) a live authorization bypass reviewed by nobody; source-level order defect already confirmed PR open, unreviewed 2 independently re-derive + land #9333 (census + record-parity doors, 1 -> 3 of 19) carries the ELIXIR_TEST_ONLY_PATHS lesson wave 42 lost PR open, unreviewed 3 independently re-derive + land #9334 (ledger-lapse expiry arm, three shapes) ledger lapse is endemic; the lesson has been a paragraph in three debriefs PR open, unreviewed 4 independently re-derive + land #9335 (sheet-grid read mode) the one standing user-facing harm: a selection frozen at A1 that nothing can move PR open, unreviewed 5 BUILD the LiveView residual 32-fold (D639) with its three obligations never got a builder; blocks the ladder unbuilt, no branch 6 BUILD the judgment-coverage ladder (D640) after the fold merges numbers dead three times; union not addition deferred round 2 7 BUILD the DOOR CENSUS - the price column as a running instrument the honesty column violates the law that produced it new this wave 8 walk two more doors: pds-ledger-census_test.sh, pds-live-hetzner-placement-group.sh D637 named both for wave 44 by number and by name new this wave Direction debate - the rivals, and why this one won Rival A - RECOVERY ONLY Spend the whole wave making wave 43's four branches independently bulletproof and merged, plus the charter, and ship nothing new. The case for it is strong and honest: an unreviewed authorization change is the single riskiest object in the repo right now, and a wave that merges it carelessly while chasing new capability has failed at the only thing that mattered. It was rejected because it under-uses the wave, not because it is wrong: four PRs of independent re-derivation is roughly one round, and the fold plus the ladder are DESIGNED work with their obligations already derived by run - leaving them unbuilt for a second consecutive wave is how wave 43's best output rots. Rival A's real contribution survives: movement 1 goes first, alone, and no slice PR merges on its own author's oracle. Rival B - ADVANCE ONLY Treat the four branches as inherited fact, merge them on their green, and spend the wave taking the door from 3 of 19 to 6 or 7. Rejected outright: it is precisely the move the wish forbids, and the epic's own law forbids it too. A commit message is an exit code with better prose. Merging #9332 on its own test's word is 'a gate lies when its green costs nothing to produce', committed by the wave that coined the sentence. Rival C - THE DOOR CENSUS (winner, as movement 3 of three) The winning insight is that the epic has spent four waves arguing about a column it has never computed. Every wave restates the roster, re-prices some rows, and writes the total into the charter by hand - and PDS-D636 records that the census itself carries a FALSE SENTENCE about its own gating on main today. That is the exact failure mode this epic exists to end, committed by the epic, about the epic. Making the column an instrument is the epic's own law turned inward one more notch, and it is cheap: the derivation is two greps over files that already exist, and the prior art is already on main (api/test/barkpark/pds_residue_lens_test.exs). The sharpest attack on the winner, and how the wave absorbs it THE ATTACK: the door census is a THIRD census. This epic already has a receipt census, a residue lens, a ledger census, a record-parity arm and a charter-ledger sweep - nineteen instruments, three of which run anywhere. Building a twentieth instrument to count the nineteen is the purest possible instance of an epic measuring itself instead of shipping. And it will be WRONG on day one: leg A ('a test file shells it') has at least three encodings in the repo already (System.cmd with a module attribute, Code.require_file, a bare relative path), so a naive derivation will under-count and print a number LOWER than the truth - a different lie, in a friendlier direction. HOW THE WAVE ABSORBS IT. First, the door census is movement THREE of three - it ships only if movements 1 and 2 are honest, and the wave is graded on the security fix and the merges regardless. Then #9332 on its independent re-derivation. #9334 does NOT merge on its current zero-leg green. #9335 last, after its own red is fixed. DECIDE COMPLETE - the builders are flying Wave 44 was dispatched to independently re-derive four recovered branches BEFORE they merged. It did not get the chance, and that is the wave's first finding. #9332 merged 53add1f24 at 10:49:48Z, #9333 626f71f86 at 10:49:56Z, #9334 3f18ab048 at 10:50:04Z - and the charter #9312 merged at 11:29:57Z, FORTY MINUTES AFTER the code that cites it. For that window git grep over origin/main returned 13 hits in shipped api/ and scripts/ code pointing at PDS-D633+ decisions main did not define. Movement 1's stated law was inverted in practice. It is now repaired: main carries D633-D642, and only #9335 remains open. Verification results - what was PROVEN, what was REFUTED Nine verifiers reported; the coverage deficit was empty in both rounds. Trust order was proofs over facts over prose, and four dispatch premises were refuted at the artifact. Assignment Verdict The decisive line #9332 order defect PROVEN, and non-vacuous Deleting `readonly_posture?(assigns) -> false` takes the suite 14 tests / 0 failures to 14 tests / 4 failures, and the failures name persisted bytes: `left: %{"amount" => "ESCALATED"}` #9332's suspected OWN defect (dropped CallerContext) REFUTED, twice independently `derive/1`'s principals is the closed two-element list `[api_token, current_user]` and the PR does not touch it - a %CallerContext{} can never reach `loadable_principal?/1` Grant grade safe? REFUTED - a LIVE bypass on main A doc-scoped write grant wrote a DIFFERENT doc: `left: {true, %{"amount" => "ESCALATED", "currency" => "NOK"}}` Ops.commit/3 a second bypass? REFUTED - it funnels `ops.ex:391-403` ends in `send_ops(socket,[op])`; probe green rc=0, RED under guard mutation with `%{"fmt" => "checkbox", "v" => false}` Stranded fold never had a builder REFUTED at the code level Row is 6/11 with run-quoted evidence; the diff is +273/-34, RESIDUAL 32 to 0, `sum 322 == population 322`, `CENSUS OK` D633's 210 s a gate budget? REFUTED `--selftest` exceeds 600 s WALL; one meter read `real 1662,98 / user 7,05` - a 236x understatement Ledger-census door 20-23 s / 107 checks REFUTED by run 42.6-45.0 s CPU (49.3 s hermetic), and 144 checks in all four runs Two-leg AGREEMENT check REFUTED as a design MUT-1 is ALREADY RED on main via `--check`; a one-line COMMENT plus the forced declaration buys a fraudulent THROUGH python3 receipt (D638 row) STRUCK Ratchet exits rc=0 with python3 absent, not 127; the first repro was confounded by a PATH strip that also lost `dirname` and `cut` Sheet-grid palette 2.72:1 REFUTED as a defect #5b9dff vs WHITE = 2.72 (the assertion's own number); vs the real dark bg = 7.27. The harness reads --bg ordinally Door count on landed main 1 of 19 was stale; it is 3 #9333 merged mid-round; denominator is 19 (17 .sh + 2 .exs), and 43 is a glob error Owning doc for the inventory NOT-FOUND, and that is the finding `success-claim-census.md` read in full: 286 lines, ZERO instrument inventory. No doc owns this fact-topic COVERAGE, INCLUDING NOT-FOUNDS. Reached for the first time: docs/decisions/success-claim-census.md, Ops.commit/3, the sheet-grid palette harness, and every leg-A encoding on main. STILL NOT REACHED: api/lib/barkpark/plugins/sheets/web/ops_controller.ex:69, a SECOND Session.apply_ops surface over HTTP that the LiveView wall does not cover - nobody examined it, and it is filed rather than assumed safe. The SheetGrid write-LANDING half is UNPROVEN, not proven-safe: Session.peek returned {:error, :no_session} in BOTH arms, so an assertion there today would be vacuous in both directions. Both are backlog rows, not silent gaps. Decisions - PDS-D643 through D652, each with its one-line why These mirror the charter (PR #9353); the charter is the epic's memory, this Paper is the wave's story. Because that PR may not be on main while the builders fly, the decisions are here in full. D643 - Movement 1 landed WHILE wave 44 verified it, charter last. Why: 13 dangling citations shipped, and #9334's green was a zero-second skip shim with ZERO gate legs - this epic's own law broken on this epic's own PR. D644 - #9332 is sound, its suspected own defect is void, and the bypass is NOT closed for the pure grant grade. Why: the narrowing hook is :handle_event and the component route is handle_info, so Access.validate/3 is never consulted. Denying readonly_posture? would be the WRONG fix - the narrowing must travel into the door. D645 - The fold is recoverable, not rebuildable, and git-grep cannot see stranded work. Why: uncommitted work is the only kind that CAN be stranded, so any git-based sweep systematically misses exactly what it is looking for. D646 - 210 s is leaf CPU, not a gate budget. Why: a required gate enforces WALL, the driver is serial and prints nothing until the last case returns, and an in-flight run is indistinguishable from a hang by stdout alone. D647 - The ledger-census door is re-priced and 'viable' is dead. Why: 42.6-49.3 s CPU and 144 checks, and the count is load-independent so this is staleness, not mismeasurement. D648 - Wall is not a measurable property of a door; the unit is CPU = user + sys, labelled LOCAL. Why: a FIXED workload swung 5.8x at constant load while its user CPU held to 27%, and on the hetzner door sys EXCEEDS user, understating it 2.1x as a pure CPU fact. D649 - The agreement check cannot fail; leg A must be attribute-bound AND executed. Why: leg A implies leg B by an existing required ratchet, and a comment-blind extractor lets one comment line plus the declaration the ratchet forces manufacture a THROUGH. D650 - The denominator is 19 and the inventory's owner is the INSTRUMENT'S OWN PRINTED OUTPUT. Why: no doc owns the fact-topic, the repo caps cards at 7, and an appendix would push success-claim-census.md past its budget. D651 - The palette red is a harness attribution bug, not a contrast defect. Why: a generated :root block was inserted ABOVE the dark block, so an ordinal read compares dark hues against WHITE - and the standing task about it would send a builder to change a hue that passes at 7.27:1. D652 - What wave 44 cut, with reasons: the ledger-census door (price), the charter sweep (45 hand rulings, gated on this charter merging, and its second read FAILS OPEN), and the sheet-grid reader half (D641, deliberate). The wave plan - 7 slices, 4 in round 1 Round 1 is dependency-free and builds this run. Round 2 does NOT build now: each names the merge it waits on, stated as the first line of its own brief so a manually-dispatched builder sees it first. Round-1 file sets are disjoint - the census, the escape-check, shared/paper.ex and the palette harness are each owned by exactly one slice. # Slice Task id Round Model Gate 1 The grant-graded doc escalation is closed at the door it rides pds-w44-grant-door-narrowing 1 fable (remapped to opus - fable unavailable) CC=clang mix test on the new LiveView test + the studio directory, rc captured to a variable 2 Residual-32 fold recovered + D605's unit + D633's blind spot IN the instrument pds-w44-census-fold-and-blindspot 1 fable (remapped) elixir scripts/pds-elixir-receipt-census.exs and its --selftest, both rc=0 3 The door census: the price column becomes an instrument pds-w44-door-census-instrument 1 fable (remapped) bash scripts/pds-door-census.sh + bash scripts/elixir-path-escape-check.sh --check + CC=clang mix test the new rider 4 The palette harness repaired against generated tokens pds-w44-palette-harness-repair 1 opus node each __*.test.mjs in api/assets/sheet-grid, every rc captured and zero 5 The judgment-coverage ladder: PROVEN-BACKED 23 as a union pds-w44-judgment-coverage-ladder 2 (after 2) opus elixir census + --selftest + the doc byte-budget check 6 The hetzner offline arm becomes the next door pds-w44-hetzner-offline-door 2 (after 3) opus CC=clang mix test the new rider + escape-check --check at rc=0 7 The charter sweep adjudicated and its fail-open closed pds-w44-charter-sweep-adjudication 2 (after THIS charter merges) opus bash scripts/pds-charter-ledger-sweep.sh and --selftest, both rc=0 HIGH-FLIP-RISK, declared, and the line is in each task's own brief so the reviewer reads it there: SLICE 1 - whether the grant grade's narrowing belongs in the door or the gate, and whether narrowing it denies a legitimate grantee. This is an authorization judgment on a bypass that is LIVE ON MAIN, and it is the species that flipped twice in wave 43. SLICE 3 - whether leg A's three predicates admit a fraudulent THROUGH; the comment mutation is the oracle, and wave 44's own prototype PASSED IT. Both warrant a genuinely independent second reviewer before merge. This workflow spawns one reviewer, so that dispatch is a manual lead step - review's job is to NAME when independence is owed. BACKLOG FILED NOW, six published child rows, so the ledger shows the future: pds-w44-bl-ledger-census-door-repriced, pds-w44-bl-ops-controller-apply-ops-ungated, pds-w44-bl-vacuous-reader-toggle-oracle, pds-w44-bl-sheetgrid-write-landing-unproven, pds-w44-bl-stranded-work-is-invisible-to-git-grep, pds-w44-bl-citation-precedes-merge-check. THE WAVE'S OWN LAW, TURNED ON ITSELF. A gate lies when its green costs nothing to produce - and this wave found that sentence violated three times by the epic that coined it: #9334's zero-second Test shim, the two-leg agreement check that cannot red, and the charter sweep's second read that prints CONFIRMED while its read failed. Wave 44's grade rests on slices 1 and 2, not on the door count. DEBRIEF - wave 44 reviewed, 4 PRs pushed, grade A- Every branch this wave produced is on origin with a PR open. Nothing is merged - the lead merges. Three slices were handed to review as built and green; a FOURTH was found stranded, fully built and fully gated, with zero commits on its branch, and was recovered here. What shipped, per slice TASK FINAL BRANCH PR GATE RE-RUN ON THE FINAL STATE VERDICT pds-w44-grant-door-narrowing loop-epic/a-doc-scoped-write-grant-stops-writing-a-0-r #9377 slice test rc=0, 5 tests 0 failures; studio suite rc=0, 1547 tests 0 failures STRONG. The bypass is real and the fix is what closes it - proven by the reviewer's OWN mutation, not the builder's: neutering grant_target_denied?/3 gives rc=2 with two failures printing left: %{"amount" => "ESCALATED"} read back from the store. pds-w44-census-fold-and-blindspot loop-epic/the-residual-32-gets-judged-and-the-mete-1 #9378 census rc=0, RESIDUAL 0/322, sum 322 == population 322, CENSUS OK STRONG. A/B re-derived independently: 32 -> 0, reachable_unconditional 194 -> 225, DENIES numerator HELD at 137, so the headline fraction gets WORSE (70.6% -> 60.9%). That is a fold, not a rubber stamp. pds-w44-palette-harness-repair loop-epic/the-sheet-grid-palette-harness-stops-com-3-r #9379 all four __*.test.mjs rc=0; palette reports 18 contrast checks STRONG, plus two reviewer fixes. The 4-week red was a harness attribution bug, never a WCAG defect - and the bug lied in BOTH directions (#14532d is invisible in dark mode at 2.18:1 and the old harness would have PASSED it at 9.11:1 vs white). pds-w44-door-census-instrument loop-epic/the-price-column-stops-being-charter-pro-2-r #9380 door-census rc=0 (UNDISPOSED 0 of 20, ERRORS 0); --selftest rc=0 (8 PASS / 0 FAIL); escape-check rc=0; rider rc=0 (8 tests) RECOVERED BY REVIEW, not builder-delivered. Complete and green - it simply never got committed. One pair of eyes on a 37 KB shell instrument; an independent second reviewer is owed. What the review FOUND that the wave did not report PDS-D653 - A TASK CAN BE 11/12 STAMPED AND ITS BRANCH EMPTY. pds-w44-door-census-instrument stamped eleven criteria with real run evidence, its now-line read 'committing: ... branching loop-epic/the-price-column-stops-being-charter-pro-2', and git diff origin/main...that-branch is EMPTY. It was in NEITHER the built handoff nor the not-green list. The rule this buys: the LEDGER is the sweep index, not the handoff - diff every wave task's stated branch against origin/main and treat an empty diff as STRANDED, because a report cannot describe the builder that stopped before writing it. PDS-D654 - A GATE THAT DOES NOT TRIGGER ON ITS OWN SUBJECT IS GREEN FOR FREE. sheet-grid-js.yml runs a harness that parses root.html.heex, presence_state.ex and tokens_gen.ex, and triggered on NONE of them - so the contrast gate never ran on a PR that changed a hue, a background token, or the presence palette. D633's law in its cheapest form yet: no skip shim, no vacuous assertion, just a paths: list that omits the subject. Repaired in #9379. PDS-D655 - TWO INSTRUMENTS SHIPPED CONTRADICTORY PROSE ABOUT THE SAME FINDING, IN THE SAME WAVE. pds-door-census.sh printed the meter blindness as a 236x real/user RATIO; pds-elixir-receipt-census.exs refuted exactly that on its own runs (113x, then 123x, for the SAME fan-out, because real counts WAITING). Reconciled in review onto the load-independent leaf-metered FLOOR. The rule: when a finding ships inside more than one instrument, ONE owns the sentence and the others cite it - the same argument the census's own @blind_spot attribute makes, one level up. A FLAKE, FILED RATHER THAN SWALLOWED. The first full studio-suite run scored 1 failure in ChatRenderGoldenTest's sidebar byte-lock (golden 6554 bytes, region 6554 bytes, first diff at 723 - a same-length CONTENT SWAP). It passes in isolation and passed on re-run of the identical tree. Filed as task-441f5a5669e0ab6b. A golden that reds only sometimes trains reviewers to re-run until green, which is this epic's own defect class. THE HOST WAS NOT QUIET, AND THAT PROVED D605 BY ACCIDENT. The reviewer's census read user cpu 17330 ms against wall clock 95801 ms on a box carrying 24 stray busy-loop processes four days old. The wall figure is the LOAD; the CPU figure is the CODE. Dated corrections to earlier sections of this Paper 2026-08-03, correcting the Direction section's 'Charter #9312 merges FIRST and alone': INVERTED IN PRACTICE. #9332/#9333/#9334 merged at 10:49-10:50Z and the charter at 11:29:57Z - forty minutes after the code citing it. Already recorded as PDS-D643; noted here so a reader of the Direction section does not carry the plan as the outcome. 2026-08-03, correcting 'The wave plan - 7 slices, 4 in round 1': FOUR round-1 slices were dispatched and only THREE reached review as built. The fourth (pds-w44-door-census-instrument) completed its work and its gate and died before committing; it is delivered by this review as #9380. The plan's round-1 count is right; its delivery path is not what the plan describes. 2026-08-03, on the wish's item 3 ('measured at 236x'): REFUTED BY THE ARTIFACT, and the refutation is now the shipped sentence in BOTH instruments. real/user is load-dependent; the load-independent statement is the DIRECTION plus a leaf-metered floor. Ledger audit All four slice tasks are lifecycle in_progress with merge-gated criteria left OPEN for the lead - correct, none closed early. Evidence was stamped AS THE BUILDERS WORKED, not batched: each carries per-criterion evidence quoting run output, and two carry honest --miss records rather than fabricated flips (pds-w44-census-fold-and-blindspot criterion 8, the lv_verdict/5 cond reorder; pds-w44-palette-harness-repair criterion 7, the PR body a builder cannot write because builders do not push). ONE LEDGER LIE CORRECTED: pds-w44-door-census-instrument's claim now-line implied a committed branch that does not exist. A review_status field now records the correction, the recovery, and the re-run gate; re-published and read back. Each of the other three tasks gained a review_status naming its final branch, its PR, and which gate legs the REVIEWER re-ran (as distinct from which the builder claimed). No task outside this wave was mutated. One NEW task was filed and published: task-441f5a5669e0ab6b (the golden byte-lock flake), parented to the epic. Grade - A- EARNED, not awarded. What is genuinely strong: three of four slices closed a defect that was REAL and proved it by substitution rather than by reading, and every one of them refuted part of its own brief from the artifact - the palette slice found a THIRD stale coupling nobody had priced (--fg-muted was matched for an hsl() both themes author as var(--muted-text), so that check had found zero declarations and could never have run), and the census slice refused the ratio its dispatch demanded. The security slice is the wave's best work: it declined the obvious fix (widening Caps.write_capable?/2, which is shared with the SheetGrid prop and has no target), declined the obvious predicate (Access.admits_desk?/3, whose type/doc_id overwrite IS the bug), and carries a positive control proving a legitimate grantee still writes. What falls short. (1) A whole slice died between its last stamp and its first commit and NOTHING in the wave's own reporting said so - it took a branch-vs-ledger diff to find a finished instrument one cycle away from deletion. That is the sixth consecutive wave to strand built work, and it is the single reason this is not an A. (2) Two instruments shipped contradictory prose about the same finding in the same wave - a coherence failure the wave had every opportunity to catch, since one slice explicitly refuted the other's figure in its own commit message. (3) The security slice's shipped non-vacuity test is a local constant-false STUB, not the reverted arm; the real revert was run and recorded in the stamp, but the artifact that MERGES cannot reproduce it - the reviewer had to re-run the mutation by hand to confirm. (4) Coverage is honestly partial and says so: paper_ops/2 and document_op/2 carry the new arm but are proven by READING, and the census's ExUnit rider was never run locally. No bloat: 489 lines for the security slice including a 361-line test, 333 for the census fold, 86 for the palette repair. Nothing was redesigned; the reviewer's edits are two latent-hazard closures and one prose reconciliation. Tree-tidiness was not pursued and has no value here. What the next wave should take MERGE ROUND 1 FIRST, IN THIS ORDER: #9377 (the security fix - it is the only thing in this wave that closes a live escalation), then #9379 (it turns the red Sheet-grid hook unit harness green, which is currently the only non-advisory red on the still-open #9335), then #9378 and #9380. Two of the four are owed a genuinely independent second reviewer before merge, and this workflow spawns exactly one reviewer, so that dispatch is a MANUAL LEAD STEP: #9377 (security / tenancy) and #9380 (whether leg A admits a fraudulent THROUGH - and it never got its builder's own review dispatch, so it has had ONE pair of eyes on 37 KB of shell). THEN THE DEFERRED ROUND-2 SLICES, EACH AS ITS DEPENDENCY MERGES: pds-w44-judgment-coverage-ladder after #9378 (both rewrite the census and every line number shifts - re-derive anchors at the new base, and PROVEN-BACKED must be one Enum.count over one MapSet.union, never an addition); pds-w44-hetzner-offline-door after #9380 (it edits the same declared set, so dispatching beside it produces a conflict, not a build - and BOTH legs or neither: the instrument AND its ELIXIR_TEST_ONLY_PATHS entry); pds-w44-charter-sweep-adjudication after the charter PR #9353 merges (the candidate vocabulary is MINED FROM THE CHARTER, so adjudicating before it lands produces a fresh red the moment it does - and this wave's own wave-log entry moved that vocabulary again). AND ONE NEW STANDING CHORE, from D653: every review must diff each wave task's stated branch against origin/main before it grades anything. An empty diff on a stamped task is a stranded slice, and the built-slice handoff structurally cannot report one. Wave 44 sealed 2026-08-03. 4 PRs open: #9377, #9378, #9379, #9380. Nothing merged - the lead merges, and closes the merge-gated criterion on each task as it does. TUI view Email view

desktop.bodyText: PDS wave 44 - recover wave 43's unlanded work, re-derive its one security claim, and make the price column RUN STRATEGIZE COMPLETE - the survey fleet is flying. PREMISE SMOKE RUN IN-PROCESS against `git show origin/main:<path>` at origin/main head c2affd445, never the primary checkout (300+ commits behind, 220 foreign modified files). VERIFIED: the charter on origin/main tops out at PDS-D632 - D633-D642 are NOT on main, they live only on PR #9312, so NO builder may carry a D633+ citation until that PR lands. VERIFIED: PDS-D578 exists at charter:11830 and says verbatim 'PROVEN-BACKED is 23/252 = 9.1%' - D640's citation of it COVERS what it is cited for. VERIFIED: api/lib/barkpark_web/studio/caps.ex on origin/main has write_capable?/2 at :283 with `Map.get(caps, :write) == true -> true` as the FIRST cond arm and `restricted?(assigns) -> false` as the SECOND, and restricted?/1 at :295 already contains `share_access == :read` - the ORDER defect #9332 claims is REAL AT SOURCE. Reachability is not yet proven and is survey question 1. VERIFIED: scripts/elixir-path-escape-check.sh is the SINGLE source of truth for ELIXIR_TEST_ONLY_PATHS - the name appears in NO workflow yml; elixir.yml consumes it through --print-set / --match. #9333 edits the right file. VERIFIED on origin/main: scripts/pds-ledger-census_test.sh, scripts/pds-live-hetzner-placement-group.sh, scripts/pds-scratch-target_test.sh, scripts/pds-charter-ledger-sweep.sh and api/test/barkpark/pds_residue_lens_test.exs all exist. VERIFIED: LiveScope.authorize_read/4 is a PRIVATE function at api/lib/barkpark_web/live_scope.ex:114, called from :88 - the non-admin reachability story runs through LiveScope.assign_scope, so the CALLER is what a verifier must pin. The wish, and the four things it asks for Wave 43 died mid-flight on a weekly account limit, not on a defect. It completed 36 of 41 agents, produced ten charter decisions (PDS-D633-D642), and pushed NOTHING. The lead recovered four branches out of their worktrees by hand and opened #9332, #9333, #9334, #9335 at 12:15 today. Wave 43's reviewer never ran; its debrief was never written. Those four PRs are UNREVIEWED BY ANYONE, and their commit messages are an author's own account of their own work. The wish asks for four things: (1) re-derive #9332's live write bypass from source before trusting a word of it; (2) verify the other three the same way; (3) confirm PDS-D633's measurement law - the in-BEAM meter is blind to port children and errs in the one direction a price column must not - and ship its blind-spot sentence in the meter's own moduledoc AND printed output; (4) finish the price column: N of 19 instruments under a required gate, every remaining refusal carrying a measured price, a named environment, or NOT-YET-BUILT. REFUTATION - the first one, and it is in the wish's own item 4 The wish states the price column's reason vocabulary is 'exactly three reasons: PRICE, ENVIRONMENT, NOT-YET-BUILT' and that 'the fence' is not an available answer. Wave 43's own PDS-D637 - which the wish is paraphrasing - found by RUN that three is not enough. It names FIVE classes: PRICE, ENVIRONMENT, NOT-YET-BUILT, plus CONTENT-RED (pds-charter-ledger-sweep.sh --selftest is rc=1 on main today at 2.36s user, refusing because an UNRESOLVED-CLAIM ARRIVAL is unadjudicated - neither a price nor an environment) and RED-BY-DESIGN / REPORTER (pds-record-parity.sh's live axis B exits 1 on 59 leaf rows, 48 of them belonging to twelve OTHER epics that never consented to the instrument; the arm is a reporter and must never carry a required check name). A related sixth, HUMAN-GATE, governs the sheet-grid harness, whose own workflow header says it only gates once a human registers it as a required check. The wish also says pds-record-parity.sh --selftest exits rc=3 with 'unknown argument' and calls that an ENVIRONMENT blocker. Wave 43 did not accept that framing - it walked a DIFFERENT door. #9333 gates scripts/pds-record-parity.test.sh, the instrument's own hermetic two-sided mutation harness (76 checks, zero of which read a live ledger row), at 1.30-1.47s user - the cheapest door in the inventory. So record-parity is not an ENVIRONMENT refusal; its HARNESS is a THROUGH and its LIVE arm is RED-BY-DESIGN. The wish's item 4 is the tenth consecutive dispatch this epic has refuted from the artifact, and it is refuted in the direction of GOOD NEWS. Direction - three movements, and the third is what makes this a wave and not a cleanup The finished experience: at the end of wave 44 a cold reader runs ONE command and gets the epic's honesty column back COMPUTED rather than quoted - every scripts/pds-* instrument, its gate status derived from the two things that actually make a door (a test file that shells it, and a matching ELIXIR_TEST_ONLY_PATHS line), its refusal class, and its price in the unit PDS-D633 says is legal. A new pds-* script arrives as an UNDISPOSED row and the thing goes red. A door that quietly stops running goes red. And the number that appears in the charter next wave is a number nobody typed. Movement 1 - LAND THE RECOVERED WORK, WITH INDEPENDENCE THAT IS REAL Charter #9312 merges FIRST and alone, because until it does every D633+ citation a builder would carry points at nothing on origin/main. Then the four slice PRs, each with an independent re-derivation that does NOT read the branch's own test as its oracle. #9332 gets the full treatment: the source-level order defect is already confirmed (cond arm 1 = caps.write, arm 2 = restricted?, and restricted? already contains share_access == :read), so the open question is REACHABILITY - can a real signed-in NON-MEMBER, through a real non-admin route, hold share_access: :read and caps.write == true simultaneously? That is the whole claim, and it must be re-derived through LiveScope.assign_scope -> authorize_read/4, not asserted from a fixture the branch authored. One suspected defect the wave carries in already, found while reading the diff and NOT yet proven: #9332's membership collapse routes through loadable_principal?/1, which accepts only %ApiToken{} and %User{}. The rule this buys: the LEDGER is the sweep index, not the handoff - diff every wave task's stated branch against origin/main and treat an empty diff as STRANDED, because a report cannot describe the builder that stopped before writing it. The rule: when a finding ships inside more than one instrument, ONE owns the sentence and the others cite it - the same argument the census's own @blind_spot attribute makes, one level up. A golden that reds only sometimes trains reviewers to re-run until green, which is this epic's own defect class. THE HOST WAS NOT QUIET, AND THAT PROVED D605 BY ACCIDENT. The reviewer's census read user cpu 17330 ms against wall clock 95801 ms on a box carrying 24 stray busy-loop processes four days old. The wall figure is the LOAD; the CPU figure is the CODE. Dated corrections to earlier sections of this Paper 2026-08-03, correcting the Direction section's 'Charter #9312 merges FIRST and alone': INVERTED IN PRACTICE. #9332/#9333/#9334 merged at 10:49-10:50Z and the charter at 11:29:57Z - forty minutes after the code citing it.
