The fourth (pds-w44-door-census-instrument) completed its work and its gate and died before committing; it is delivered by this review as #9380. The plan's round-1 count is right; its delivery path is not what the plan describes. 2026-08-03, on the wish's item 3 ('measured at 236x'): REFUTED BY THE ARTIFACT, and the refutation is now the shipped sentence in BOTH instruments. real/user is load-dependent; the load-independent statement is the DIRECTION plus a leaf-metered floor. Ledger audit All four slice tasks are lifecycle in_progress with merge-gated criteria left OPEN for the lead - correct, none closed early. Evidence was stamped AS THE BUILDERS WORKED, not batched: each carries per-criterion evidence quoting run output, and two carry honest --miss records rather than fabricated flips (pds-w44-census-fold-and-blindspot criterion 8, the lv_verdict/5 cond reorder; pds-w44-palette-harness-repair criterion 7, the PR body a builder cannot write because builders do not push). ONE LEDGER LIE CORRECTED: pds-w44-door-census-instrument's claim now-line implied a committed branch that does not exist. A review_status field now records the correction, the recovery, and the re-run gate; re-published and read back. Each of the other three tasks gained a review_status naming its final branch, its PR, and which gate legs the REVIEWER re-ran (as distinct from which the builder claimed). No task outside this wave was mutated. One NEW task was filed and published: task-441f5a5669e0ab6b (the golden byte-lock flake), parented to the epic. Grade - A- EARNED, not awarded. What is genuinely strong: three of four slices closed a defect that was REAL and proved it by substitution rather than by reading, and every one of them refuted part of its own brief from the artifact - the palette slice found a THIRD stale coupling nobody had priced (--fg-muted was matched for an hsl() both themes author as var(--muted-text), so that check had found zero declarations and could never have run), and the census slice refused the ratio its dispatch demanded. The security slice is the wave's best work: it declined the obvious fix (widening Caps.write_capable?/2, which is shared with the SheetGrid prop and has no target), declined the obvious predicate (Access.admits_desk?/3, whose type/doc_id overwrite IS the bug), and carries a positive control proving a legitimate grantee still writes. What falls short. (1) A whole slice died between its last stamp and its first commit and NOTHING in the wave's own reporting said so - it took a branch-vs-ledger diff to find a finished instrument one cycle away from deletion. That is the sixth consecutive wave to strand built work, and it is the single reason this is not an A. (2) Two instruments shipped contradictory prose about the same finding in the same wave - a coherence failure the wave had every opportunity to catch, since one slice explicitly refuted the other's figure in its own commit message. (3) The security slice's shipped non-vacuity test is a local constant-false STUB, not the reverted arm; the real revert was run and recorded in the stamp, but the artifact that MERGES cannot reproduce it - the reviewer had to re-run the mutation by hand to confirm. (4) Coverage is honestly partial and says so: paper_ops/2 and document_op/2 carry the new arm but are proven by READING, and the census's ExUnit rider was never run locally. No bloat: 489 lines for the security slice including a 361-line test, 333 for the census fold, 86 for the palette repair. Nothing was redesigned; the reviewer's edits are two latent-hazard closures and one prose reconciliation. Tree-tidiness was not pursued and has no value here. What the next wave should take MERGE ROUND 1 FIRST, IN THIS ORDER: #9377 (the security fix - it is the only thing in this wave that closes a live escalation), then #9379 (it turns the red Sheet-grid hook unit harness green, which is currently the only non-advisory red on the still-open #9335), then #9378 and #9380. AND ONE NEW STANDING CHORE, from D653: every review must diff each wave task's stated branch against origin/main before it grades anything. An empty diff on a stamped task is a stranded slice, and the built-slice handoff structurally cannot report one. Wave 44 sealed 2026-08-03. 4 PRs open: #9377, #9378, #9379, #9380. The lead recovered four branches out of their worktrees by hand and opened #9332, #9333, #9334, #9335 at 12:15 today. Wave 43's reviewer never ran; its debrief was never written. The wish also says pds-record-parity.sh --selftest exits rc=3 with 'unknown argument' and calls that an ENVIRONMENT blocker. Wave 43 did not accept that framing - it walked a DIFFERENT door. #9333 gates scripts/pds-record-parity.test.sh, the instrument's own hermetic two-sided mutation harness (76 checks, zero of which read a live ledger row), at 1.30-1.47s user - the cheapest door in the inventory. So record-parity is not an ENVIRONMENT refusal; its HARNESS is a THROUGH and its LIVE arm is RED-BY-DESIGN. The wish's item 4 is the tenth consecutive dispatch this epic has refuted from the artifact, and it is refuted in the direction of GOOD NEWS. Direction - three movements, and the third is what makes this a wave and not a cleanup The finished experience: at the end of wave 44 a cold reader runs ONE command and gets the epic's honesty column back COMPUTED rather than quoted - every scripts/pds-* instrument, its gate status derived from the two things that actually make a door (a test file that shells it, and a matching ELIXIR_TEST_ONLY_PATHS line), its refusal class, and its price in the unit PDS-D633 says is legal. Movement 1 - LAND THE RECOVERED WORK, WITH INDEPENDENCE THAT IS REAL Charter #9312 merges FIRST and alone, because until it does every D633+ citation a builder would carry points at nothing on origin/main. Then the four slice PRs, each with an independent re-derivation that does NOT read the branch's own test as its oracle. #9332 gets the full treatment: the source-level order defect is already confirmed (cond arm 1 = caps.write, arm 2 = restricted?, and restricted? already contains share_access == :read), so the open question is REACHABILITY - can a real signed-in NON-MEMBER, through a real non-admin route, hold share_access: :read and caps.write == true simultaneously? It was rejected because it under-uses the wave, not because it is wrong: four PRs of independent re-derivation is roughly one round, and the fold plus the ladder are DESIGNED work with their obligations already derived by run - leaving them unbuilt for a second consecutive wave is how wave 43's best output rots. Rival A's real contribution survives: movement 1 goes first, alone, and no slice PR merges on its own author's oracle. Rival B - ADVANCE ONLY Treat the four branches as inherited fact, merge them on their green, and spend the wave taking the door from 3 of 19 to 6 or 7. Rejected outright: it is precisely the move the wish forbids, and the epic's own law forbids it too. A commit message is an exit code with better prose. Merging #9332 on its own test's word is 'a gate lies when its green costs nothing to produce', committed by the wave that coined the sentence. Rival C - THE DOOR CENSUS (winner, as movement 3 of three) The winning insight is that the epic has spent four waves arguing about a column it has never computed. Every wave restates the roster, re-prices some rows, and writes the total into the charter by hand - and PDS-D636 records that the census itself carries a FALSE SENTENCE about its own gating on main today. That is the exact failure mode this epic exists to end, committed by the epic, about the epic. Making the column an instrument is the epic's own law turned inward one more notch, and it is cheap: the derivation is two greps over files that already exist, and the prior art is already on main (api/test/barkpark/pds_residue_lens_test.exs). Building a twentieth instrument to count the nineteen is the purest possible instance of an epic measuring itself instead of shipping. Already recorded as PDS-D643; noted here so a reader of the Direction section does not carry the plan as the outcome. 2026-08-03, correcting 'The wave plan - 7 slices, 4 in round 1': FOUR round-1 slices were dispatched and only THREE reached review as built. The fourth (pds-w44-door-census-instrument) completed its work and its gate and died before committing; it is delivered by this review as #9380. The plan's round-1 count is right; its delivery path is not what the plan describes. 2026-08-03, on the wish's item 3 ('measured at 236x'): REFUTED BY THE ARTIFACT, and the refutation is now the shipped sentence in BOTH instruments. real/user is load-dependent; the load-independent statement is the DIRECTION plus a leaf-metered floor. Ledger audit All four slice tasks are lifecycle in_progress with merge-gated criteria left OPEN for the lead - correct, none closed early. Evidence was stamped AS THE BUILDERS WORKED, not batched: each carries per-criterion evidence quoting run output, and two carry honest --miss records rather than fabricated flips (pds-w44-census-fold-and-blindspot criterion 8, the lv_verdict/5 cond reorder; pds-w44-palette-harness-repair criterion 7, the PR body a builder cannot write because builders do not push). ONE LEDGER LIE CORRECTED: pds-w44-door-census-instrument's claim now-line implied a committed branch that does not exist. A review_status field now records the correction, the recovery, and the re-run gate; re-published and read back. Each of the other three tasks gained a review_status naming its final branch, its PR, and which gate legs the REVIEWER re-ran (as distinct from which the builder claimed). No task outside this wave was mutated. One NEW task was filed and published: task-441f5a5669e0ab6b (the golden byte-lock flake), parented to the epic. Grade - A- EARNED, not awarded. What is genuinely strong: three of four slices closed a defect that was REAL and proved it by substitution rather than by reading, and every one of them refuted part of its own brief from the artifact - the palette slice found a THIRD stale coupling nobody had priced (--fg-muted was matched for an hsl() both themes author as var(--muted-text), so that check had found zero declarations and could never have run), and the census slice refused the ratio its dispatch demanded. The security slice is the wave's best work: it declined the obvious fix (widening Caps.write_capable?/2, which is shared with the SheetGrid prop and has no target), declined the obvious predicate (Access.admits_desk?/3, whose type/doc_id overwrite IS the bug), and carries a positive control proving a legitimate grantee still writes. What falls short. (1) A whole slice died between its last stamp and its first commit and NOTHING in the wave's own reporting said so - it took a branch-vs-ledger diff to find a finished instrument one cycle away from deletion. That is the sixth consecutive wave to strand built work, and it is the single reason this is not an A. (2) Two instruments shipped contradictory prose about the same finding in the same wave - a coherence failure the wave had every opportunity to catch, since one slice explicitly refuted the other's figure in its own commit message. (3) The security slice's shipped non-vacuity test is a local constant-false STUB, not the reverted arm; the real revert was run and recorded in the stamp, but the artifact that MERGES cannot reproduce it - the reviewer had to re-run the mutation by hand to confirm. (4) Coverage is honestly partial and says so: paper_ops/2 and document_op/2 carry the new arm but are proven by READING, and the census's ExUnit rider was never run locally. No bloat: 489 lines for the security slice including a 361-line test, 333 for the census fold, 86 for the palette repair. Nothing was redesigned; the reviewer's edits are two latent-hazard closures and one prose reconciliation. Tree-tidiness was not pursued and has no value here. What the next wave should take MERGE ROUND 1 FIRST, IN THIS ORDER: #9377 (the security fix - it is the only thing in this wave that closes a live escalation), then #9379 (it turns the red Sheet-grid hook unit harness green, which is currently the only non-advisory red on the still-open #9335), then #9378 and #9380. Two of the four are owed a genuinely independent second reviewer before merge, and this workflow spawns exactly one reviewer, so that dispatch is a MANUAL LEAD STEP: #9377 (security / tenancy) and #9380 (whether leg A admits a fraudulent THROUGH - and it never got its builder's own review dispatch, so it has had ONE pair of eyes on 37 KB of shell). THEN THE DEFERRED ROUND-2 SLICES, EACH AS ITS DEPENDENCY MERGES: pds-w44-judgment-coverage-ladder after #9378 (both rewrite the census and every line number shifts - re-derive anchors at the new base, and PROVEN-BACKED must be one Enum.count over one MapSet.union, never an addition); pds-w44-hetzner-offline-door after #9380 (it edits the same declared set, so dispatching beside it produces a conflict, not a build - and BOTH legs or neither: the instrument AND its ELIXIR_TEST_ONLY_PATHS entry); pds-w44-charter-sweep-adjudication after the charter PR #9353 merges (the candidate vocabulary is MINED FROM THE CHARTER, so adjudicating before it lands produces a fresh red the moment it does - and this wave's own wave-log entry moved that vocabulary again). AND ONE NEW STANDING CHORE, from D653: every review must diff each wave task's stated branch against origin/main before it grades anything. An empty diff on a stamped task is a stranded slice, and the built-slice handoff structurally cannot report one. Wave 44 sealed 2026-08-03. 4 PRs open: #9377, #9378, #9379, #9380.
